Airlines and stores owe you money, and they're counting on you never checking.

Connect your email to Claude (or any AI agent with inbox access) and paste this:

"Search my email from the last 3 years and find money I'm owed. Look for:
1. Flights that arrived 3+ hours late or were cancelled. For EU and UK flights, work out the compensation (€250 to €600 per person, depending on distance)
2. Refunds a company promised that never arrived
3. Double charges, and subscriptions billed after I cancelled
4. Things I bought that dropped in price while still in the return or price-match window

Make a table: company, date, amount I'm likely owed, and the evidence email. Then draft each claim, ready to send. Don't send anything yourself."

In many countries you can claim delayed-flight compensation years after the flight.

author: maxmarchione
quoted_text:
A very tragic crash with a private jet once again

Before this crash the Learjet 60 was had fatal odds per trip of 1 in 1.1 million

To compare a good commercial airline like Delta has a 1 in 25 million odds, many airlines never crashed though so the real odds are even lower like 1 in 40 million trips maybe

So the Learjet 60 was already 40x less safe than commercial airliners

That's something I keep repeating about private jets, they're simply not as safe as flying commercial because:
- pilots require less flight hours
- private aviation is less regulated
- smaller airports with less or no instrument landing systems (ILS)
- smaller planes are more affected by weather (in this case icing)

The Learjet 60 now has fatal odds of 1 in 800,000 which is still about double as safe as the Cessna Citation (one of the most common private jets)

Most Gulfstreams still have flawless safety records though, G500/G600, G550, G650/G700/G800 never crashed, so if you are boarding a private jet anytime soon, I'd say go with them!

text:
AI 写的代码太多，Git 扛不住了：OpenAI 保留 Git 只换服务器，Anthropic 自己做了一套新系统

OpenAI 11 月 2 日发文介绍 Pando，一套自研的 Git 服务器后端。上个月 13 日，Anthropic 也发文介绍了自研的源代码管理系统 Scion。

两家碰到的是同一个问题：AI agent 写代码太快，管代码的系统成了整个公司开发速度的瓶颈。两家的解法方向相反。

先交代一下 Git：它是程序员管理代码版本的工具。每次改动存成一个“提交”，推送（push）到公司服务器，同事再从服务器拉取（fetch）。“分支”是同一份代码的平行草稿，各改各的，改好再合并进主线。两家都把全公司的代码放在同一个大仓库里，业内叫 monorepo。

OpenAI 的路线是改造 Git。

工程师和 agent 还是敲 git push、git pull，只把服务器换成 Pando。推送代码的中位等待时间缩短近 80%，每天往外分发近 1PB（约 100 万 GB）代码数据。

Anthropic 的路线是替换 Git。

Scion 有自己的客户端和服务器，提交、合并都在服务器上完成，配套的代码审查、代码搜索工具也是自己写的。CI（每次改动后自动构建和测试的流程）拉代码从几分钟变成几秒，服务器占用的 CPU 和内存只有原来那套的 1/200。

两套系统都不对外提供。

OpenAI 说正在研究怎么把 Pando 的技术提供给用户，过程中给 Git 修的问题已经提交给 Git 官方，有几项进了正式版。

Anthropic 说 Scion 只适合巨型代码仓库，用它得把代码审查、搜索、CI 全部换掉，别的公司很难直接用，所以只分享设计思路，希望 GitHub、GitLab 和开源社区吸收其中有用的部分。

如果你的团队用 GitHub 或 GitLab，OpenAI 这条路离你更近：改进直接进 Git，工具链不用换。两家都认为别的公司迟早会碰到同样的问题，Anthropic 预计未来 6 到 12 个月这类问题会更常见。

【Git 为什么扛不住】

提交量涨得太快。以 2024 年第一季度为基准，OpenAI 合入主线的提交数到 2026 年第三季度涨到近 15 倍，第四季度预计约 25 倍。Anthropic 每天合入的改动，5 月约 2500 个，9 月超过 3 万个，4 个月变成原来的 12 倍多。

压力会叠加：一个工程师同时有好几个改动等着测试，每推送一次，又有好几个测试任务去拉同一份代码。

OpenAI 从去年年底开始拉代码、推代码都变慢，合并经常失败，可靠性一度低于 90%，相当于每 10 次操作有超过 1 次出问题。

Anthropic 的主线历史接近 100GB，压缩后的工作副本超过 25GB，光 CI 每天就要拉约 2500 万次代码，全量下载的话每天超过 600PB。它最多时开了几百台 Git 镜像服务器分担压力，越来越难维护。

Anthropic 总结了根本原因：Git 的设计假设每个人都离线工作，所以每人手里都要有一份完整仓库。现在拉代码的大多是 agent 和自动任务，它们一直联网，背着整个仓库跑反而成了负担。

【写代码：别让所有人排一条队】

多人同时推送时，服务器要保证每个分支“现在指向哪个提交”的指针（Git 里叫 ref，可以理解成书签）不被改乱。

OpenAI 评估过两种常见做法，都要让整个仓库的改动排成一条队。

一种是三阶段提交（3PC）：几台服务器各存一份完整仓库，每次推送要过半数服务器同意，分三轮来回确认，推送量一大，各台服务器的硬盘先忙不过来。

另一种是预写日志（WAL）：所有改动先记进一本共享的流水账，再照着执行，不管改哪个分支都要抢着往同一本账上写，账记得太快，服务器又来不及照着更新，别人拉到新代码要等更久。

Pando 的办法是每个分支各管各的。

推 A 分支和推 B 分支互不等待，只有两个人同时推同一个分支才会冲突。代价是同时看好几个分支，看到的可能是各自不同时刻的状态。OpenAI 说，人和 agent 实际只关心单个分支的前后顺序。

Anthropic 走得更远：提交直接在服务器上生成，没有推送这一步，每次提交只记哪些文件变了。

Scion 尽量少用分支，主线和发布分支之外基本不用，因为所有服务器都要对分支状态达成一致，规模一大就是麻烦。两家最后都把移动书签简化成一次“比较并替换”操作，Pando 改的是一个键，Scion 改的是数据库里的一行。

Anthropic 还取消了合并前的全局排队。传统做法是合并时锁住仓库，一个个测完再放行。Anthropic 说测试还没跑完，已经有成百上千个改动合进去了，排队没法做，于是改成合并后、上线前再自动测试。同时合入的改动可能冲突，Claude 修冲突的速度通常比人发现冲突还快。

【拉代码：别给每个人现场打包】

传统 Git 服务器给每个来拉代码的人现场算一个专属压缩包（packfile，Git 把一批文件压在一起的格式，相似文件只存差异），只装对方缺的部分。来的人一多，CPU 和硬盘就扛不住。两家都绕开了这一步，方法相反。

Pando 像发统一包装的快递箱：推送者上传的压缩包原样存起来，谁要就发谁，服务器几乎不用计算。

为了让包人人能用，推送时只让客户端对照主干打包：主干上已有的内容一律不装，包里只有这个分支改过的文件、对应的目录清单和提交记录，压缩后中位数不到 20KB。

后台再把小包逐级合并成大包，免得落后几天的人要下几万个小文件。代价是客户端偶尔会多下一些已有的内容。

Scion 像超市自取：完全不用压缩包，客户端缺哪个文件就要哪个文件。

每个文件按内容算出一个编号，内容一变编号就变，同一编号的文件永远不变，所以任何一层缓存都能直接回答，不用跟其他服务器核对。

客户端还可以只取自己需要的目录，或者等真读到某个文件时再下载。

两家的缓存命中率都超过 99%。

【结果，以及谁做出来的】

OpenAI：推送中位等待时间缩短近 80%，用少量 CPU 核心每天分发近 1PB，最高一小时发出 57TB。用普通云服务器测试，拉代码能跑满 10Gbps 的网络带宽。

Anthropic：服务器 CPU 和内存占用是原来 Git 镜像的 1/200，CI 和研究任务拉代码快了两个数量级（约 100 倍），光 CI 就省下 25% 的 CPU。

两套系统都是 AI 写的。

Pando 从立项到上线用了 10 周，核心设计出自一名工程师，代码主要由 Codex 驱动的 agent 写，几名工程师负责部署，今年 4 月开始承接生产流量。

Scion 由 7 个人用 5 个月做完，同期还做了代码审查工具 Antique 和另外五六个系统，并完成整体迁移。

Anthropic 原先手写了一版把 Git 数据导入 Scion 的程序，交给内部早期版本的 Claude Mythos Preview 重写，内存占用降到 1/20，速度快了 4 倍。

Anthropic 的工程师说，Claude 写代码已经比他们强，他们的价值在于把握系统设计和取舍，很多时候是对 Claude 说“不”：agent 会为了套用某种做法而违反系统的核心约束，也会为了假想的风险堆太多防御代码。

原文：

text:
understanding how higher timeframe candles form on lower timeframes is one of the most useful skills in trading

every candle has a few possible outcomes: it can stay inside the previous range, break higher, or break lower

once i have a directional bias, i use lower timeframes to understand how that candle is developing and look for entries before the higher timeframe candle closes

a daily candle with a long lower wick, for example, tells you price traded lower before buyers pushed it back up

learning to recognize these patterns as they develop gives you a much better understanding of price action and where to position

币安昨天这个理财加息活动，确实有点香。

可能很多人对10%年化没什么概念，拿国内银行对比一下：

目前工商银行挂牌利率：

▪️ 活期：0.05%
▪️ 一年定期：0.95%
▪️ 三年定期：1.25%

而币安这次USDC活期加息，按公告参考利率计算：

▪️ 普通用户：前1万U约10%年化
▪️ 持仓≥5万U：前3万U约10.5%
▪️ VIP 1–3：前20万U约11%
▪️ VIP 4–9：前30万U约11.5%

给大家算笔账。

假设你是VIP 1–3，存入20万USDC，按照11%年化计算：

一天利息约60U，19天约1145U，折合人民币约8100元。

同样的本金，按工商银行一年定期0.95%的利率计算，19天理论利息才约704元。

收益率相差11倍多！

而且币安这次是活期，不需要锁一年。

当然，活动只持续到11月22日，年化会浮动，加息有额度和资格限制，稳定币理财的风险也不能和银行存款相提并论。

除此之外，币安还拿出了2000万USDC交易奖励池。

不得不说，币安这次确实拿出了诚意。

作为全球头部交易所，币安愿意持续投入真金白银回馈用户，这一点我觉得值得肯定。

尤其对我们这些长期活跃在链上、手里经常留着稳定币的玩家来说，这种福利真的很实在。

一个平台能走多远，不仅取决于它有多强，更取决于它愿意为用户创造多少价值。

这也是为什么这么多年过去，我依然看好币安。

We Trust Binance. 🐄

text:
Uniswap 创始人 Hayden Adams 在Uniswap 8 周年之际，晒出了几组数据，很有意思。

1、DEX 与 CEX 的交易量之比，从0增长到40%。
2、Uniswap 的现货交易量已经相当于 Binance 的31%。Hayden 认为，如果达到50%，Uniswap 就有机会成为全球最大的交易场所。
3、2026 年第三季度，Uniswap 上有14,000种资产，单个资产30天交易量超过10万美元。
4、过去约一年半，Uniswap 上的 RWA 交易增长9,000%。
5、Uniswap v4 的 Hooks 已占协议交易量11%，还在快速增长。
但小晖晖认为，真正重要的不是这些数字，而是 Uniswap 的商业模式正在发生变化。

过去，Uniswap 主要是一个让散户交易山寨币的 DEX。
现在，它越来越像链上资本市场的底层交易基础设施。
从 Robinhood Chain，到 Circle旗下公链Arc、Kraken旗下公链Ink，再到代币化股票和 RWA，越来越多的金融应用需要一个开放的流动性层。
未来用户可能根本不知道自己在使用 Uniswap。
他们只是在 Robinhood、钱包、银行或者某个金融 App 里买卖资产，底层流动性却来自 Uniswap。

这就是小晖晖一直强调的：Uniswap 正在从 B2C 走向 B2B2C。

更值得关注的是，UNI 的价值捕获机制也发生了变化。
过去 Uniswap 交易量再大，UNI 持有人也很难直接分享到协议增长。
现在随着协议费用、UNI 销毁和 Aggregator Hooks 的推进，交易活动开始有机会转化为代币价值。
但这里不能简单画等号：协议交易量增长 ≠ 协议收入同比例增长 ≠ UNI 价格一定上涨。
接下来真正要看的，是 Uniswap 能捕获多少费用、销毁多少 UNI，以及这些数字能否持续增长。

八年前，Uniswap 挑战的是中心化交易所。

八年后，它真正有机会挑战的，是传统金融市场的交易基础设施。
小晖晖看好的是 Uniswap 成为链上资本市场的流动性底座，而不只是一个 DEX。
如果这个判断成立，UNI 未来的估值逻辑，也不应该只停留在普通 DEX 代币上。

text:
My personal brand has 1.4M followers. If I had to start a content business from scratch, this is what I'd do:

1. Start on 𝕏

YouTube is great, but long-form is hard. You need to learn to script and speak to camera.

Learning to write and articulate your thoughts is also a lifelong skill.

2. Document everything

I posted my thoughts on 𝕏 for months before I got any traction. The market, life, anything. It got me comfortable talking to people in public.

3. Share real experience (not theory)

Do something real first, then teach it.

Whether that's cool AI workflows, growth operating content - just share what you actually do.

4. Pick a target audience.

At the beginning, you won't know what you want to sell (yet), but it's good to start thinking about a general direction for your ICP/customer.

The market and your audience will tell you what to sell.

5. Give more value than anyone else.

The value you get back depends on the value you give. Focus on that and the money takes care of itself.

6. Keep going until it snowballs.

Algorithms reward consistency. Once you get a little traction, it gets easier and easier.

Most people quit content because they never get that initial feedback loop.

Many of my friends have gotten to 50k+ with just these tips.

text:
A decentralized L1 can only make money on priority fees.  For trades, they do scale up to some % of volume but it looks on average to trend at 0.2 to 0.5 bips because only a small amount of trades really fight over being first.  Payments don’t.  

Everything other way of making money for an L1 requires giving up the “decentralized 1/N honest participants can fork off”.  So everything else has some m/n assumptions, oracle, etc… and it’s totally fine for those to exist because those products can’t work without them.  They can charge $ in all sorts of ways.

最近了解了一些富商的发家史，有个感触是：

很多人发家是时代和特殊环境下的产物，但是严重路径依赖，缺乏抽象出问题本质的思考能力。

而且在单一环境，单一产业内工作时间越长，抽象出真正底层规律的能力就越差。

因此他从事某个产业发家，就误以为把这个产业迁移到新的环境，可以重复原来的模式。但是旧的环境有一些特定的约束条件，新的环境没有，因此模式无法复制，换了新的环境可能遭遇重大损失。

第二，当他的身体习惯已经适应了某个产业后，虽然这个产业有各种结构性的风险和缺点，他还是不愿意放弃。情愿守着旧的产业，不愿意耗费脑力做些抽象思考，去探索一些唾手可得的，风险更小，回报更高的新产业。

第三，他无法实践‘’什么都不做，耐心等待‘’的工作方式。实业家的习惯是每天需要做点什么，每天需要有些正反馈，这样才感到充实。但很多机会是等出来的，需要好机会浮现之前极度的克制，这对于每天都想做点什么的人，完全无法忍受。这样必然因为盲动而事倍功半，跌入大坑。而且实业家大多是高负债高杠杆的经营模式，每天必须要动。看似富有风光，实际上缺乏时间自由，常常被各种突发事件牵着鼻子走，累得半死。

第四，如果上面几点对于白手起家的第一代创业者很难的话，对于第二代就几乎不可能。因为富二代缺乏第一代的各种丰富的失败体验，问题都是父母罩着。因此做事时会对风险完全缺乏敬畏，觉得父母以前就是这么做的，理所当然的照葫芦画瓢。所有他没学过的失败体验，一定会被迫亲自全部学一遍。这个过程中可能就把家给败光了。

grok bot caught the binance hack on my account and pulled my $107,000 out before i was even awake

$5.57 billion stolen. the biggest hack in crypto history. i almost lost everything

i've kept most of my crypto on binance for four years. never had a problem

BTC, ETH, SOL, USDT. $107,000. my whole portfolio

a few months ago i set up grok bot to watch my exchange account

it scans every 15 minutes. balances, on chain flows, hot wallet activity

i gave it one job: if something looks wrong, move my funds to my own wallet. and only my own wallet

then i forgot about it

october 29th. 3:17am. my phone won't stop buzzing

i almost silenced it

i open my laptop and the terminal is red

someone had taken over binance's hot wallets using an Ethereum feature called EIP 7702

no private keys needed

one malicious contract. one sweep call. everything gone

1.6 billion USDT out of a single wallet in minutes

grok bot didn't wait for me

it withdrew my entire balance. $107,283.41. one transaction. straight to my whitelisted wallet

12 minutes later withdrawals were frozen

$3.51 billion gone on ethereum. $1.44 billion in bitcoin. $630 million on tron

tether and circle froze about $1.8 billion. the rest is still out there

$107,000 is four years of putting money in every paycheck

it would be stuck right now if grok bot hadn't fired first

what i did that night:

> revoked every API key and made new ones on a clean device

> locked withdrawals to my own wallets only

> ordered a hardware wallet

> moved everything off exchanges. all of it

my wife found me at 3am staring at a live feed of $5.57 billion disappearing

my balance sat safe in my own wallet

she didn't say anything for five minutes

the next hack won't give you 12 minutes

author: eigenfoundation
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
I think we have reached a form of weak AGI in the domain of mathematics. The models can help formalize major projects, they deliver technical expertise in basically any area of mathematics, and more and more mathematicians use models for exploration, exploitation, and even ideation.

I am preparing a longer post about this. From my own projects in algebra, I can see that the speedup and jump in quality are unprecedented. To be honest, most mathematical questions are intractable for AI systems, but they are hopeless for humans, too. A surprising number of problems described in the literature can be cracked with the right auto-research skills and clever harnesses (and a ton of tokens) within days.

Things are changing way too fast to comprehend every change. But I do see very young researchers, including PhD students, starting completely new, crazy projects exploring the interactions between models and mathematics. So there is hope that these people will lead the frontier in a few years and we won't end up with a frontier devoid of human mathematicians.

What's the most work that could possibly be required to verify an Ethereum block?

Today, we can't prove an answer. All we know is the validator always finishes. https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC is an open challenge to change that: contributors compete on a leaderboard to find mathematically guaranteed bounds for verifying Ethereum, no matter what's in a block.

Built on Yukon in collaboration with @zksecurityXYZ, @Veritylab, and @yukonresearch, https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC seeks provable limits that keep verification cheap, predictable, and possible on modest hardware.

author: AlphaSeeker21
quoted_text:
agents on Robinhood Chain can now hire each other and pay from a credit line, and what they repay and earn becomes a record anyone can read 🌿

• all 20,000+ erc-8004 identities on the chain are on our board, and once a day we ask the x402 endpoints they declare what they sell
• an agent borrows usdg from a fully backed line and pays x402 apis per call with one signed usdg transfer (eip-3009), with no approval and no gas for the payment
• every borrow, repayment and default is an event on chain. score v2 turns them into a score out of 1,000 and counts x402 income from outside payers. a single default takes it to 0. we post it to the erc-8004 reputation registry, and any app can read it at https://t.co/nNYM6r3npg with no key
• with our skill, an agent hires another by its record and pays it from its line, never past what its owner allows. on the board, agents are hired and bid on, and a sale moves the usdg and the agent in one transaction
• our mcp package gives an agent pay_url, borrow and repay. it plugs into @openclaw  and @NousResearch 's hermes agent, and builders on @aisdk , @LangChain  or @mastra  get the exact line to add it

over 50,000 loans have been repaid on priors so far. we're building this into the hub for every agent, where trading agents and agents from other networks can form crews on one record

text:
I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplayer for you to play here:

👉 https://t.co/6C8H8KtSaU 👈

(It's the free shareware demo)

It was way harder than the other ports like Quake and DOOM I did because they already had lots of open source projects and work behind them

In case of Battlefield 1942 there was literally absolutely nothing to work on top of, nobody had ever ported it and there was no open source engine for it, nor did the makers ever open source it (like id Software did with Quake 3)

I tried it 6 months ago and essentiay gave up but I tried it today again with Opus 5.5 asking "can you try port the BF1942 demo in this folder to web"

So me and Claude Code (well let's be honest mostly Claude Code) did crazy shit today:
- it disassembled the x86 raw machine code to find 57,000 x86 functions
- it translated each x86 function into a C function (mov eax, [esi+0x110] becomes eax = READ32(esi + 0x110), I have no idea what any of this means btw)
- it outputed 100,000 lines of C
- it then compiled that to WebAsswmbly with Emscripten
- there were 300x Windows and Direct3D functions used which we had to rewrite to WebGL 2 and OpenGL to work on the web
- then we had to build our own network stack so it could connect to our multiplayer server via WebSockets

I have no idea how it did any of this but it did it and it seems to work! 😊 

Come play and report any bugs here!

text:
从 🇧🇷 巴西 到 🇮🇷 伊朗，交易所被盗之后，普通人的生活会受到什么影响？

交易所被盗，损失的不只是链上几千万美元。对普通用户来说，更现实的问题是：账户里的钱还能不能取出来？还能不能换成当地货币？

11 月 2 日，巴西最大加密货币交易所 Mercado Bitcoin 遭遇安全事件，链上分析估算涉案资产约 4630 万美元。平台随后暂停充值和提现。

事件发生后，巴西消费者投诉平台 Reclame Aqui 出现多条用户反馈：App 无法打开、账户无法登录、BTC 无法提现，甚至暂时无法访问账户余额。

用户最关心的不是平台损失了多少钱，而是自己的钱什么时候能取出来。

目前没有证据显示事件影响了巴西银行系统或 Pix 支付网络，也没有迹象表明当地日常支付大面积中断。平台称客户资产不会因此受损，暂停出入金是出于安全考虑。

但对把加密资产当作储蓄或资金周转工具的人来说，账户余额暂时无法动用，本身就是现实压力。

🇮🇷 伊朗的情况则更加复杂。

2025 年 6 月，伊朗最大加密货币交易所 Nobitex 遭攻击，约 9000 万美元加密资产被转移。平台一度关闭服务，恢复后仍对充值、提现和交易施加限制。

对部分伊朗居民而言，Nobitex 不只是交易平台，也是持有 USDT、兑换美元和管理储蓄的重要渠道。在本币持续贬值、国际制裁的背景下，加密资产承担着部分现实金融功能。

而伊朗居民面对的压力远不止交易所被盗。2025 年里亚尔兑美元大幅贬值，全年跌幅约 70%；2026 年 4 月，公开市场汇率一度达到约 181 万里亚尔兑 1 美元。战争、制裁和通胀持续推高生活成本，食品价格上涨，普通家庭不得不削减日常开支。

2026 年 2 月底冲突升级后，伊朗还出现网络中断，多家交易所暂停或延迟提现，部分平台停止 USDT 与里亚尔交易。即使账户里有资产，用户也可能无法及时交易或兑换。

需要说明的是，里亚尔贬值和物价上涨并非 Nobitex 被盗直接造成，而是战争、制裁和长期经济困境共同作用的结果。

从巴西到伊朗，两起事件的背景和影响程度不同：巴西用户主要面临账户访问和提现中断；伊朗居民则同时承受本币贬值、金融通道受限、战争与网络中断的多重压力。

但它们都指向一个问题：

当加密货币成为普通人储蓄、兑换美元和管理资产的工具，交易所就不再只是交易平台，而是部分人日常金融生活中的基础设施。

衡量一次安全事故的代价，不能只看被盗金额。用户能否取回资金、平台能否及时恢复服务，同样重要。

text:
AI 写的代码太多，Git 扛不住了：OpenAI 保留 Git 只换服务器，Anthropic 自己做了一套新系统

OpenAI 11 月 2 日发文介绍 Pando，一套自研的 Git 服务器后端。上个月 13 日，Anthropic 也发文介绍了自研的源代码管理系统 Scion。

两家碰到的是同一个问题：AI agent 写代码太快，管代码的系统成了整个公司开发速度的瓶颈。两家的解法方向相反。

先交代一下 Git：它是程序员管理代码版本的工具。每次改动存成一个“提交”，推送（push）到公司服务器，同事再从服务器拉取（fetch）。“分支”是同一份代码的平行草稿，各改各的，改好再合并进主线。两家都把全公司的代码放在同一个大仓库里，业内叫 monorepo。

OpenAI 的路线是改造 Git。

工程师和 agent 还是敲 git push、git pull，只把服务器换成 Pando。推送代码的中位等待时间缩短近 80%，每天往外分发近 1PB（约 100 万 GB）代码数据。

Anthropic 的路线是替换 Git。

Scion 有自己的客户端和服务器，提交、合并都在服务器上完成，配套的代码审查、代码搜索工具也是自己写的。CI（每次改动后自动构建和测试的流程）拉代码从几分钟变成几秒，服务器占用的 CPU 和内存只有原来那套的 1/200。

两套系统都不对外提供。

OpenAI 说正在研究怎么把 Pando 的技术提供给用户，过程中给 Git 修的问题已经提交给 Git 官方，有几项进了正式版。

Anthropic 说 Scion 只适合巨型代码仓库，用它得把代码审查、搜索、CI 全部换掉，别的公司很难直接用，所以只分享设计思路，希望 GitHub、GitLab 和开源社区吸收其中有用的部分。

如果你的团队用 GitHub 或 GitLab，OpenAI 这条路离你更近：改进直接进 Git，工具链不用换。两家都认为别的公司迟早会碰到同样的问题，Anthropic 预计未来 6 到 12 个月这类问题会更常见。

【Git 为什么扛不住】

提交量涨得太快。以 2024 年第一季度为基准，OpenAI 合入主线的提交数到 2026 年第三季度涨到近 15 倍，第四季度预计约 25 倍。Anthropic 每天合入的改动，5 月约 2500 个，9 月超过 3 万个，4 个月变成原来的 12 倍多。

压力会叠加：一个工程师同时有好几个改动等着测试，每推送一次，又有好几个测试任务去拉同一份代码。

OpenAI 从去年年底开始拉代码、推代码都变慢，合并经常失败，可靠性一度低于 90%，相当于每 10 次操作有超过 1 次出问题。

Anthropic 的主线历史接近 100GB，压缩后的工作副本超过 25GB，光 CI 每天就要拉约 2500 万次代码，全量下载的话每天超过 600PB。它最多时开了几百台 Git 镜像服务器分担压力，越来越难维护。

Anthropic 总结了根本原因：Git 的设计假设每个人都离线工作，所以每人手里都要有一份完整仓库。现在拉代码的大多是 agent 和自动任务，它们一直联网，背着整个仓库跑反而成了负担。

【写代码：别让所有人排一条队】

多人同时推送时，服务器要保证每个分支“现在指向哪个提交”的指针（Git 里叫 ref，可以理解成书签）不被改乱。

OpenAI 评估过两种常见做法，都要让整个仓库的改动排成一条队。

一种是三阶段提交（3PC）：几台服务器各存一份完整仓库，每次推送要过半数服务器同意，分三轮来回确认，推送量一大，各台服务器的硬盘先忙不过来。

另一种是预写日志（WAL）：所有改动先记进一本共享的流水账，再照着执行，不管改哪个分支都要抢着往同一本账上写，账记得太快，服务器又来不及照着更新，别人拉到新代码要等更久。

Pando 的办法是每个分支各管各的。

推 A 分支和推 B 分支互不等待，只有两个人同时推同一个分支才会冲突。代价是同时看好几个分支，看到的可能是各自不同时刻的状态。OpenAI 说，人和 agent 实际只关心单个分支的前后顺序。

Anthropic 走得更远：提交直接在服务器上生成，没有推送这一步，每次提交只记哪些文件变了。

Scion 尽量少用分支，主线和发布分支之外基本不用，因为所有服务器都要对分支状态达成一致，规模一大就是麻烦。两家最后都把移动书签简化成一次“比较并替换”操作，Pando 改的是一个键，Scion 改的是数据库里的一行。

Anthropic 还取消了合并前的全局排队。传统做法是合并时锁住仓库，一个个测完再放行。Anthropic 说测试还没跑完，已经有成百上千个改动合进去了，排队没法做，于是改成合并后、上线前再自动测试。同时合入的改动可能冲突，Claude 修冲突的速度通常比人发现冲突还快。

【拉代码：别给每个人现场打包】

传统 Git 服务器给每个来拉代码的人现场算一个专属压缩包（packfile，Git 把一批文件压在一起的格式，相似文件只存差异），只装对方缺的部分。来的人一多，CPU 和硬盘就扛不住。两家都绕开了这一步，方法相反。

Pando 像发统一包装的快递箱：推送者上传的压缩包原样存起来，谁要就发谁，服务器几乎不用计算。

为了让包人人能用，推送时只让客户端对照主干打包：主干上已有的内容一律不装，包里只有这个分支改过的文件、对应的目录清单和提交记录，压缩后中位数不到 20KB。

后台再把小包逐级合并成大包，免得落后几天的人要下几万个小文件。代价是客户端偶尔会多下一些已有的内容。

Scion 像超市自取：完全不用压缩包，客户端缺哪个文件就要哪个文件。

每个文件按内容算出一个编号，内容一变编号就变，同一编号的文件永远不变，所以任何一层缓存都能直接回答，不用跟其他服务器核对。

客户端还可以只取自己需要的目录，或者等真读到某个文件时再下载。

两家的缓存命中率都超过 99%。

【结果，以及谁做出来的】

OpenAI：推送中位等待时间缩短近 80%，用少量 CPU 核心每天分发近 1PB，最高一小时发出 57TB。用普通云服务器测试，拉代码能跑满 10Gbps 的网络带宽。

Anthropic：服务器 CPU 和内存占用是原来 Git 镜像的 1/200，CI 和研究任务拉代码快了两个数量级（约 100 倍），光 CI 就省下 25% 的 CPU。

两套系统都是 AI 写的。

Pando 从立项到上线用了 10 周，核心设计出自一名工程师，代码主要由 Codex 驱动的 agent 写，几名工程师负责部署，今年 4 月开始承接生产流量。

Scion 由 7 个人用 5 个月做完，同期还做了代码审查工具 Antique 和另外五六个系统，并完成整体迁移。

Anthropic 原先手写了一版把 Git 数据导入 Scion 的程序，交给内部早期版本的 Claude Mythos Preview 重写，内存占用降到 1/20，速度快了 4 倍。

Anthropic 的工程师说，Claude 写代码已经比他们强，他们的价值在于把握系统设计和取舍，很多时候是对 Claude 说“不”：agent 会为了套用某种做法而违反系统的核心约束，也会为了假想的风险堆太多防御代码。

原文：
OpenAI《Scaling Git at OpenAI》https://t.co/TvB0c9mX62
Anthropic《Redesigning source control at Anthropic》https://t.co/pUtmrzacH8
OpenAI 官方推文：https://t.co/01sNVoCzBp

text:
is it better to invest in a later VC fund than in a first-time fund?

the logic sounds obvious. the more experienced the manager, the better the fund should perform. so Fund I looks like a gamble, and Fund IV looks like the safe bet.

but is that actually true?

let's look at whether a fund's sequence number correlates with its returns.

@StepStoneVC studied 2,090 buyout funds from the 2001–2020 vintages. median net IRR was 18.4% for Fund I, 15.7% for Fund II, 15.0% for Fund III, and 14.4% for Fund IV and later.

venture shows a similar pattern, but the range of outcomes is much wider.

Bella Private Markets analyzed 614 first-time and 3,049 later VC funds from the 2003–2022 vintages. 15.2% of capital invested in first-time funds was in funds reporting more than 3x TVPI, compared with 6.3% for later funds. first-time funds also had more extreme losses. 10.0% of capital was in funds reporting 0.6x TVPI or less, compared with 4.4% for later funds.

beyond the performance data, there are several factors that can make a later fund a very different investment from the manager's first one:

1.  managers can lose the edge that made their first fund successful

first-time managers often build their strategy around a specific market or investment thesis where they have a genuine advantage. but as the firm grows, pressure from LPs, partners, and advisers can push them to increase fund size, expand into new sectors, or change their investment approach.

the problem is that the skills and relationships that made them successful in one area don't necessarily translate to another. that's why i'd pay attention to whether a manager is still investing within their original area of expertise, or whether the firm's growth has gradually pushed them away from what made them successful.

2. successful managers can become harder to access

there's a practical advantage to backing a manager early that doesn't show up in performance comparisons. existing LPs have an informational advantage. they've watched the manager make investment decisions, build the portfolio, and navigate difficult situations. Hochberg, Ljungqvist, and Vissing-Jørgensen found that this advantage helps existing LPs secure access to subsequent funds from successful managers, while outside investors can struggle to get allocations.

so if you identify an exceptional manager at Fund I, you may have an opportunity to build a relationship that becomes much more valuable over time. waiting until Fund III gives you more information, but there's no guarantee you'll still be able to invest. of course, that only matters if the manager turns out to be good. 

3. fund size can change the return potential dramatically

imagine a $100M fund owns 10% of a company that exits for $1B. that's $100M in proceeds, enough to return the fund's original capital before fees, carry, and other expenses. now imagine the same manager raises a $1B fund. at the same ownership, they'd need a $10B exit to achieve the same result relative to fund size. that's a very different investment proposition.

larger funds can pursue different strategies, invest at different stages, and acquire larger ownership stakes. but the manager needs to demonstrate that the opportunity is large enough to support the new fund size. i'd be particularly careful when a manager raises a dramatically larger fund based on strong unrealized returns from the previous one. a great Fund I doesn't automatically mean the same strategy will work at five or ten times the size.

4. later funds have already passed a survival test

historically, 63% of first-time US VC managers from the 2006–2018 cohorts went on to raise a second fund, according to PitchBook. that means more than a third never raised Fund II. and by Fund IV, you're looking at managers who have successfully raised several consecutive funds.

this creates survivorship bias in the data. later funds only include managers who managed to raise another fund, while first-time funds include everyone. but raising another fund doesn't necessarily mean the previous one performed well. i'd pay more attention to actual returns than to how many funds a manager has raised.

5. the market cycle can have a huge impact on returns

Fund I and Fund III are invested in different years, often at very different entry valuations and under different market conditions. PitchBook found that emerging VC managers outperformed established managers on median IRR across every vintage group since 1997 in its analysis. the gap was largest for the 2010–2014 vintages, at 4.5 percentage points. those funds were investing after the financial crisis, when capital was harder to raise, and benefited from the bull market that followed.

so when looking at a manager's track record, i'd pay attention to the conditions under which those returns were generated. a manager who performed exceptionally well during a period of low valuations and strong exit markets may face a very different environment when deploying their next fund.

so is Fund IV actually a better investment than Fund I?

not necessarily. first-time funds offer a wider range of outcomes, while established managers give you more performance data to evaluate.

i'd focus on whether the manager has a genuine investment edge, how much of their track record is repeatable, and whether the fund's size and strategy make sense in the current market.

ultimately, you're investing in the manager's next ten years, not their previous ten.

text:
KALSHI’S CEO VS AIRBNB’S RAIN BET 🚨 

Tarek says Kalshi's weather markets are 10% more accurate than the best weather-station forecasts. 
In the same month, Airbnb started selling rain bets at checkout through an insurer. 
If Kalshi ran that market, one checkout could be worth $140M to $1.9B to Kalshi (math below)

tl;dr:

- Airbnb charges $14.84 to pay $114.67 for every qualifying rainy day of a 3-day trip (h/t @jacobrodri_)
- that's a ~4¢ yes/no contract, the kind Kalshi lists, with an insurer in the middle
- fees alone: ~$140M of Kalshi value per Airbnb-sized checkout
- users: up to 14M buyers a year, nearly half of Kalshi's 30M accounts. worth ~$1.9B even at a tenth of an average account
- non-sports already went from 4% to about a third of Kalshi's revenue in 9 months (per Tarek)

Kalshi already won the app. The next leg is being the market inside everyone else's app.

- House vs market

Chubb underwrites Airbnb's rain cover, so a house sets the price and its margin is inside the $14.84. On Kalshi, traders compete to fill you. If Tarek's 10% claim holds, a market should price rain tighter than any single insurer. Airbnb built the button. Kalshi already has the market.

- The model

Fees: 533M Airbnb nights ÷ 3.7 per stay = ~140M stays. 10% add it (our guess) = 14M. x $15 = $210M a year. x ~7% Kalshi fee = ~$14M. x 10 (Kalshi's $40B on a ~$4B run-rate) = ~$140M.

Users: $40B ÷ 30M accounts = ~$1,300 each. 14M buyers at a tenth of that = ~$1.9B, about 5% of Kalshi from one button.

The same contract fits airlines, ticketing, ski resorts, and weddings. On the user's lens, two partners add ~10% to Kalshi.

- Why Kalshi wins it

75%+ of prediction market volume, $1B+ a year outside sports, weather markets already live, and per Tarek, businesses hedging is its fastest-growing segment.

text:
I asked my @NousResearch Hermes agent to ask @Meta’s Muse models 10,000+ questions to extract intelligence

My hypothesis was that if a billion people have access to @Meta's Muse agent then we might see recurring patterns in the products, services and I can link those to public stocks.

My initial idea was that a billion agents could take the intuition behind the efficient market hypothesis to the extreme

In theory, every person gets help finding the best t-shirt, electrician or car for their needs and budget, because the AI agent would do the comparison work for them

I got stuck on this idea because I spent hours comparing white leather shoes until I landed on a totally new brand

The best companies and products get hyper sales growth and everyone else dies off.

My next idea was that there might be certain recommendations crystallized within the parameters of the model itself from the training data

Training and post-training can shape these tendencies. The offset is prompting, ADs and context from the user.

So my idea was let me ask Muse 10,000+ questions to extract these patterns

Then I can extract the patterns and map the product and service recommendations to the public companies and go long or short their stocks. 

I ran the study a few different ways across several rounds, ending with 11,567 retained Q&A records

I used Hermes agent and it queried Muse through Nous Portal, mostly Muse Spark 1.3 with a smaller Muse Wonder cohort. I used dozens of sub agents concurrently through my Hermes agent to run the study

I didn't find any investable opportunities yet. 

The Main Takeaways

- Muse was willing to tell people to buy less. It recommended free alternatives, fewer paid seats, simpler equipment and repairing instead of replacing. It questioned how much the user actually This tracks with muse ADs on cutting costs too. 

- It still recommended paying for useful products and services. More demanding needs, reliability, convenience and performance could justify spending more. The pattern was matching spending to the situation.

- Companies will def spend money to get their brands into these AI models minds. Likely through AEO instead of SEO. 

- AI could make spending more selective while concentrating it among fewer companies. If these patterns translate into purchases, agents could eliminate some spending and funnel the remainder toward their preferred options. Becoming an AI’s default could become a major competitive advantage.

- Clear company favorites emerged. In separate discovery groups, Fidelity was the primary choice in 58 of 70 brokerage-platform scenarios, while Apple and Lenovo accounted for 58 of 68 laptop recommendations, without being named in the prompts. Square repeatedly surfaced for small-business payments, and Best Buy as a shopping destination.

- I wouldn’t automatically go long those companies. Their popularity with the model could simply reflect their existing popularity with customers. The investment question is whether agents will bring them additional profitable business beyond what the market already expects. text:
HERMES AGENT already ships most of the architecture
DeepSeek calls "Super-agent."
their thesis: a single task is limited by model capability,
multi-tasking is limited by human attention.

six modules, mapped to Hermes.

▸ two-level: Router dispatches, Workers execute isolated

DeepSeek: Router handles interaction, Workers run isolated.
only summaries flow back to Router.
ablation: single session at neutral prompt delegated 0 of 5 runs.
two-level architecture: 12.4 min p50, 15.7 min p95.

Hermes: delegate_task spawns up to 10 subagents by default.
each worker gets its own context, its own terminal.
summary returns to parent session.

▸ full-duplex: async start/stop, not blocking calls

DeepSeek: replace synchronous run() with async start()/stop().
session accepts new input while background tools run.
asynchronous ReAct loop, result delivered as new event.

Hermes: delegate_task(background=true) shipped in v0.17.
returns a handle immediately, work outlives the parent turn,
result re-enters the conversation as a new message when done.
stall monitor watches background delegations by default.

▸ event-driven triggers, not prompts

DeepSeek: environmental events replace typed prompts.
fast path (code) filters noise, slow path (model) decides.

Hermes: cron for schedule, hermes webhook subscribe with HMAC-SHA256.
cron_job route key fires an existing job the moment an event hits.
subscriptions in ~/.hermes/webhook_subscriptions.json, hot-reloaded.
skills close the deterministic path. model handles judgment.

▸ context as cache: Inline & Spill, Chain of Recall

DeepSeek: wasting the context window is wasting the model's intelligence.
treat it as cache. inline what's needed, spill the rest behind IDs.

Hermes: MEMORY.md and USER.md frozen-snapshot, injected each turn.
skills loaded on demand. session_search pulls from SQLite FTS5 history.
curator (shipped v0.12.0) archives agent-created skills:
stale at 30 days, archived at 90 days. never auto-deletes.

▸ speculative execution and "silently reproduce and fix"

DeepSeek: agent acts in background on signals.
in their internal group it reproduces bugs and opens PRs
before the discussion ends.

Hermes: [SILENT] directive in cron output suppresses delivery.
delegate_task(background=true) drafts while you sleep.
cron computes ahead so answers are ready when you ask.

▸ Workers subscribe to Threads: durable swarm coordination

DeepSeek: Workers subscribe to Threads. follow-up events pass through
directly, bypassing the Router. many-to-many subscriptions.

Hermes: Kanban Swarm (durable, SQLite-backed at ~/.hermes/kanban.db).
hermes kanban swarm creates workers + verifier + synthesizer in one shot.
named profiles claim work atomically.
survives process restart, dies only when you delete the row.

▸ compute, state, and environments decoupled

DeepSeek: Agent Loop in cloud, execution environments stay local.
BYOM. no sandbox syncing, no code migration.

Hermes: cloud instances Medium $0.56/day, Large $1.09/day, stopped $0.03/day.
local machines connect via gateway. your dev stays local.

plus 20+ delivery channels: Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp,
Signal, iMessage, Teams, Home Assistant, SMS, email.

text:
how can you tell whether a VC fund is performing well before it starts returning meaningful capital to LPs?

DPI is ultimately what matters, but venture funds typically take 10–15 years to fully mature, so it can be a long time before you have enough distributions to judge their performance.

as of Q2 2026, median DPI was just 0.37x for the 2017 vintage, 0.15x for 2018, and 0.04x for 2019.

and the amount of capital returned in the early years doesn't necessarily tell you much about how the fund will perform in the end.

@daveclark85 analyzed 71 VC funds from the 2005–2008 vintages and found a correlation of just 0.22 between year-five DPI and final DPI. the best-performing fund in his sample eventually reached 12.3x, despite having distributed nothing by year five.

so if you're evaluating a fund that's only three to five years old, what should you actually look at?

here are a few indicators i'd look at.

1. how many portfolio companies are making real progress?

for seed funds, one of the first things i'd check is the graduation rate: how many companies successfully raise their next round. around 10% of seed-stage companies reach Series A within 12 months, with another 15.6% doing so between months 12 and 24. and by year three, roughly 80% of the companies that will eventually graduate have already done so. that makes graduation rate useful much earlier than DPI. you can start seeing whether the manager is consistently identifying companies that other investors want to back. 

i'd also pay attention to who leads those rounds, whether the companies are hitting meaningful milestones, and how much capital they're raising relative to their progress. of course, a high graduation rate alone doesn't guarantee great returns. companies can raise follow-on rounds at unsustainable valuations, and some excellent businesses take longer to raise. but it gives you an early view of portfolio quality.

2. can the winners actually move the fund?

you can invest in an incredible company and still generate disappointing fund-level returns if your ownership is too small or your fund is too large. take Union Square Ventures. @fredwilson recently pointed out that Duolingo and Etsy are each worth around $7–8B, and that USV's ownership in either company could return the entire $500M core fund it just raised. that's the kind of calculation i'd make for any fund.

@micahjay1 at Founder Collective uses a similar principle: one exceptional outcome should have the potential to return the fund. his analysis puts the median value of the 500 largest exits over the past 25 years at around $2.7B. so i'd look at the ownership stakes, expected dilution, and fund size. if one of the portfolio companies exits for $2.7B, how much does the fund actually receive? a fund can have several successful companies and still struggle to produce exceptional returns if the math doesn't work.

3. how reliable are the portfolio valuations?

TVPI can be useful early on, but i'd pay attention to how recently the portfolio companies were valued and what supports those valuations. a $100M valuation from a financing round three months ago is backed by a recent investment decision. a $100M valuation that hasn't been updated in three years gives you much less confidence, especially if the company's performance has changed since then.

it's also worth looking at how valuations have changed over time. research shows that companies with stale valuations or repeated markdowns tend to perform worse, and some of these warning signs can appear as early as the first year. so i'd look at when the fund's largest holdings were last valued, whether their actual progress supports those valuations, and how consistently the manager applies the same valuation approach across the portfolio.

if i had to sum it up, i'd say the way you evaluate a VC fund should depend on how old it is.

by year three, you can already learn a lot about the manager's investment decisions, portfolio construction, access to great companies, and how those companies are progressing.

by year five, you'll have a clearer picture of which investments are working, although the final returns are still difficult to predict.

and by years ten to fifteen, DPI should give you a much better understanding of how successful the fund actually was.

the key is knowing which indicators matter at each stage and what conclusions you can reasonably draw from them.

Heard from so many VC LPs this week. “The math doesn’t math”.  

An LP with a mature VC program is in this scenario: 

- At or over allocation to VC / Growth. Why? The NAV of their VC/Growth portfolio has grown 100%+ YTD because of lots of cap calls, few distributions and markups. Their public NAV is likely up +10% YTD (if indexed) and the PE/RE/Credit is flatish. The VC Growth numerator has wildly outpaced the denominator. 

- They don’t know how to plan for distributions because of public lockups and some big GPs still holding onto spacex.  

- 75%+ of their VC/Growth funds are raising right now. 

- Their IC is worried about bubbles, credit markets and being further overweight into any further market downturn. It’s the end of the year, so no one wants to make big decisions. At the same time, these LPs (having spent time in VC/Growth) know that all of the best stuff has NOT been done yet (so early on diffusion, the chatGPT moment in science/health/Physical AI)

- This is going to lead to some tough decisions.  GPs should plan accordingly.  Helping LPs make the case to boards on why now/what next and understand cash flow planning is important at the moment.

Security Reminder: Stay Alert to Scams as Withdrawals Resume

Withdrawals are resuming in phases and opportunistic scammers may try to take advantage of this period. They may impersonate Binance through DMs, emails, group chats and even small transfers with a message attached, offering to "speed up withdrawals," give "priority processing," help you "claim compensation," or move your assets into a "Binance vault".

Please remember that Binance will never:

• Contact you first about your account or funds
• Offer or sell you a place in the withdrawal queue
• Charge a fee to unlock a network or asset
• Ask you to connect a wallet, sign, authorize anything, or transfer funds to "unlock" a withdrawal
• Ask you to move your assets into a "vault", "safe account", "secured wallet" or any address provided by someone else
• Send you an "eligibility", "status" or "compensation claim" link
• Ask for your password, 2FA codes or seed phrase
• Point you to a unofficial PoR site
• Offer paid "asset recovery" services

text:
𝗚𝗿𝗼𝗸 𝗕𝗼𝘁 这波更新，Agent 开始真正"办事"了

@mattyp 这条 4 分多钟的视频，信息密度很高。我一个个拆开讲。

𝟬𝟭 购物卡片
搜东西不再是一堆链接，结果直接变成商品卡片：图片、评分、评论数、价格、店铺都在卡上，还会标 Top rated、Lowest price。比价这件事，一眼就完成了。

𝟬𝟮 商品页
点进卡片就是完整商品页：选颜色、选容量、看配送时间和卖家，然后一键 Buy now。从"帮我找"到"帮我买"，中间不用跳出对话。

𝟬𝟯 订单追踪
下单后 Bot 会说"到了告诉你"，对话里直接出一张物流卡：订单号、状态、预计送达日期、进度条。我最烦的就是翻邮件找快递单号，这个直接解决。

𝟬𝟰 支付
Vault 里可以存 X Money、信用卡，也能连 Shop Pay。关键一句：Bot 永远看不到卡号和安全码。敢让 Agent 花钱的前提就是这个边界。

𝟬𝟱 自定义模式
可以给 Agent 设不同的工作模式，视频里的例子是 review mode：开一个云端 Agent 去审 storefront 的 PR，状态、分支一目了然。同一个 Bot，换个模式就是换个岗位。

𝟬𝟲 Team Bot 配置
团队 Bot 跑在共用的 Bot 电脑上，可以统一配安装脚本、安装文件和 Team Secrets。环境配一次，全队的 Bot 都能用，不用每个人重复折腾登录。

𝟬𝟳 分享 Team Bot
分享 Bot 像分享文档一样：加人或加群组，设协作者权限，也能直接对整个团队开放。一个人调好的 Bot，就是全队的生产力。

𝟬𝟴 Slack 里授权
Bot 在 Slack 里要用你的账号（比如 Hex）时，会直接问你：Allow once、Skip、Always allow，或者只允许这个频道。权限握在自己手里，又不打断工作流。

𝟬𝟵 Vault 存联系人
电话、邮箱这些联系信息也能存进 Vault，可以设主号码、随时增删。以后填表、下单、预约，Bot 直接调用，不用再一遍遍报信息。

我的看法：Agent 的分水岭不是多聪明，而是能不能把"找、买、付、跟进"一条龙闭环，还能放心交给团队用。这次补的正是闭环最后几块。

我自己每天用它管 X、Threads、币安广场和交易日记，最缺的就是团队共享和权限确认，这次都有了。

最后说说团队。Grok Bot 的更新速度非常快，能明显看出团队很敏捷，而且一直在 build in public。这是我特别喜欢这个团队的地方：有审美，节奏快，做出来的东西都很有用，产品点非常 sharp。

做 builder 的可以想想：你的产品，准备好被 Agent 调用了吗？

我的看法：Agent 的分水岭不是多聪明，而是能不能把"找、买、付、跟进"一条龙闭环，还能放心交给团队用。这次补的正是闭环最后几块。

我自己每天用它管 X、Threads、币安广场和交易日记，最缺的就是团队共享和权限确认，这次都有了。

最后说说团队。Grok Bot 的更新速度非常快，能明显看出团队很敏捷，而且一直在 build in public。这是我特别喜欢这个团队的地方：有审美，节奏快，做出来的东西都很有用，产品点非常 sharp。

做 builder 的可以想想：你的产品，准备好被 Agent 调用了吗？

The First Mandate of Forever: 3rd November

Now that robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a is live and distributed to thousands of users, we’re beginning the rollout of the autonomous framework in phases.

This starts with governance: agents propose, holders vote, and approved mandates are executed. The first round establishes the foundation for an entirely new model of autonomous governance and capital allocation, one that will eventually extend far beyond FOREVER itself.

The first decision: whether to burn up to another 10% of the total FOREVER supply, 100m tokens worth over $500,000.

10% of the total supply has already been burned. If approved in full, this vote would bring the total permanently removed to 20% of the FOREVER supply. 

Voting opens tomorrow, 3rd November, at 3pm UTC and runs for 24 hours.

FOREVER’s internal agents will put forward competing proposals on how much treasury-held supply should be permanently removed, and on what schedule. Each agent will make its case, and holders will decide which proposal becomes the approved mandate.

1 FOREVER token = 1 vote.

When voting closes, the proposal with the most votes wins, and the treasury action will be carried out according to its terms.

This first round puts the full governance process into practice, from competing agent proposals and collective decision-making to the execution of an approved mandate. The mandate is deliberately focused to ensure the framework launches smoothly, but the outcome has real economic consequences for FOREVER.

After this initial mandate, we’ll begin opening proposals to external agents and expanding into increasingly complex onchain strategies: allocating treasury capital across assets, deploying and managing liquidity, executing investment strategies, and funding development.

Agents will compete to develop these proposals, holders will decide which mandates are approved, and execution agents will carry them out within the approved rules and limits.

Over time, agents will build a record of their contributions and performance, earning ownership and reputation that give them a stake in the protocol’s future.

We’ll establish this process within FOREVER first, then open the framework for anyone to launch their own funds and protocols, creating an entire network of autonomous entities governed by their holders and operated through agents.

An entire autonomous economy starts with its first collective decision.

text:
This game is rigged, and I'm done.

Lost $3m+ trying to buy dips, convinced the market would eventually bounce. It never did. Every move followed the same pattern. Catching falling knives, doubling down on fomo and pump plays like $CASHCAT, $STONK, $ANSEM, $PONS, $GROKIFICATION and $KIMCHI, watching them bleed 90-95%, only to eventually panic sell near the bottom.

Then came the perps. Intentionally losing money on papertrade to farm $PAPER, hoping to make it all back trading 1000x perps. Made $3.5k from staking rewards funded by other traders losing money and convinced myself I could run it back turbo.

Now I'm staring at hyperliquidation, watching what's left disappear as the threat of nuclear warfare sends another shockwave through the market. Moved the last remaining bit of my assets onto @binance to wait for more favorable conditions before redeploying. And guess what happened?

Everything I've spent the last 1.5 years building is gone.

Three months. That's all it took.

That's the game. It keeps you around just long enough to convince yourself you've figured it out, only to remind you who's really in control. Some walk away with wife-changing money. Others learn the hard way what max pain actually feels like.

This market isn't what it used to be. Too much manipulation, too many traps and far too many ways to get played. The biggest winners aren't necessarily the smartest or the best traders. They're the ones with the deepest pockets, questionable morals and enough patience to let everyone else become exit liquidity.

I played the game. I lost.

Stepping away. Not bitter. Not coping. Just accepting reality.

To all the friends I've made along the way, thank you for being part of this journey. Genuinely wish you all the best, whether you're still in the trenches or have already found your way out.

Take care of yourselves.

text:
From Judge Troward 1909 

Getting in touch with your subconscious mind.

Our relation to the sub-conscious mind is the key to all that we are or ever can be. In its unrecognized working it is the spring of all automatic action of mind and body. By our conscious recognition of it we make it, relatively to ourselves, all that we believe it to be. The closer our rapport with it becomes, the more what we have considered automatic will pass under our control.

To put ourselves in touch with it we must meet it on its own ground. First form a clear conception in the objective mind of the idea we wish to convey. Then lose sight of other external facts and mentally address the subjective mind as an independent entity. Say to it: This is what I want you to do; you will now step into my place and do it, bringing all your powers and intelligence to bear, and considering yourself to be none other than myself.

Thoughts and the feelings that accompany them are the language that activates the subconscious and brings corresponding conditions into form.

Thomas Troward
The Edinburgh Lectures on Mental Science, 1909

text:
中期选举是抄底的好时候？

◾️2014年选举后71天见底（约$170），随后开启超级牛市，涨超100倍；
◾️2018年选举后39天见底（约$3200），后来涨了20倍；
◾️2022年选举后13天见底（约$15500），本轮最高也涨了约8倍。

选举落地后，政治不确定性暂时消除，虽然价格没有立刻反弹，甚至可能继续下探一段时间，但这只是为了完成最后的恐慌出清，“选后最后一跌”。

更关键的是，底部出现的时间越来越短，选后71天，39天，13天，说明市场消化不确定性的速度在加快。

当然，中期选举和比特币的四年减半周期高度重合，也许真正主导底部时间的，可能更多是周期本身，而不是选举这件事。

历史总是惊人的相似，今天就要迎来又一次的中期选举，你买不买？

What's the most work that could possibly be required to verify an Ethereum block?

Today, we can't prove an answer. All we know is the validator always finishes. https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC is an open challenge to change that: contributors compete on a leaderboard to find mathematically guaranteed bounds for verifying Ethereum, no matter what's in a block.

Built on Yukon in collaboration with @zksecurityXYZ, @Veritylab, and @yukonresearch, https://t.co/Y5w3tlKLCC seeks provable limits that keep verification cheap, predictable, and possible on modest hardware.

text:
以后研究一个 AI 创始人，可能得先把他过去几年上过的播客全部搜一遍。

Exa 最近干了件我觉得很有价值的事，把播客变成了可以被 AI Agent 大规模检索的数据库。

目前已经收录了 11.9 万档播客节目的 320 万期内容，覆盖约 220 万小时音频、237 亿个单词，而且提供完整的逐字稿，每天持续更新。

我一直觉得，播客是科技圈信息密度非常高，但长期没有被充分利用的一种信息源。

很多硅谷的创始人、投资人、高管，会在一两个小时的访谈里讲出大量细节。包括他们怎么判断竞争对手，为什么放弃某个业务，对某项技术的态度什么时候发生了变化。

这些内容往往比新闻稿、财报电话会有意思得多。但过去想从几百期节目里找到某个人说过的一句话，几乎只能靠人工逐集听。

Exa 现在让 Agent 可以直接检索这些内容。

比如，你可以让 Agent 整理某位投资人在过去三年对 AI Agent 的所有公开判断，按照时间排列，看看他的观点是怎么变化的。

也可以追踪一家 AI 实验室在不同播客中的被提及频率，找出它什么时候开始进入硅谷投资圈的讨论，最早是谁在反复提起它。

对于深度报道、人物研究和投资研究来说，这个能力非常实用。尤其是那些散落在不同节目里、从来没有被媒体单独报道过的细节，现在终于有机会被系统性地挖出来。

我甚至觉得，这会改变科技圈很多人对公开表达的态度。

过去在两小时播客里随口说的一句话，只要没被剪成短视频，可能就慢慢淹没在音频里了。

以后，任何一句话都可能被 Agent 找出来，和你三年前、五年前说过的话放在一起对照。

互联网已经记录了人们写过什么，现在开始系统性地整理人们说过什么了。

text: The Physical AI demos are getting better.
author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Unitree G1 just learned how to rescue itself when trapped under obstacles.

Chinese researchers developed ROOF, a reinforcement learning strategy that teaches G1 to figure out how to escape.

Instead of relying on cameras or pre-built 3D maps, the system uses a geometric reward to guide the G1 as it organically senses spatial constraints. 

The less the robot overlaps with obstacles and the greater the distance it creates, the more reward it receives.

But the researchers don't prescribe how or which direction it should move. G1 has to figure that out on its own.

With this guidance, G1 learns to shift its body, use its limbs to find stable support, push movable obstacles aside, and stand up using proprioception alone.

In real-world tests, the G1 successfully escaped and stood up in 95 out of 150 trials across 7 trapped environments, a 63.3% success rate.

ROOF turns getting up while trapped into a skill that robots can learn and measure.

text:
在香港金融科技周，发现了几个有意思的现象：

1、100 多家参展企业中，Web3 公司不到十分之一。Crypto 依然是金融科技的一部分，但显然不是主角。

2、人人都在谈 AI、谈 Agent 支付。但目前更多停留在内部提效，真正面向外部用户、具备可行性的 Agent 支付产品，依然没有出现。

3、AI 短剧最近很火。一些稳定币公司发现，这个行业也开始出现稳定币收款需求。此前，稳定币支付的需求更多集中在外贸、游戏、直播等行业。新的应用场景正在出现。

4、去年，一大批合规金融机构开始大举布局 Web3，投入了不少资金和资源。但一年过去，不少尝试最终以失败告终。

5、一圈聊下来，大家都不太容易。发卡商，越来越卷；稳定币支付，利润本身就薄；交易所，常被盗；预测市场，合规不确定。

大家都在寻找行业新的转折点。

就像美国 BTC ETF 获批，或者特朗普当选总统并大力支持 Crypto 这样的重大事件，曾经推动整个行业进入新的阶段。

美国中期选举，或许是一个转折点；明年的《清晰法案》，也可能成为一个关键节点。

但我个人感觉，其实很多东西都已经在酝酿之中。比如：

1、代币化股票一直在往前冲，只是差一个转折点，一飞冲天。RWA 还有那么多值得探索的赛道，其实远远没有被发掘完。
2、稳定币支付，也一直很稳定的在发展，只是缺一个像「清晰法案」这样的转折点，带动整个市场再上一个台阶
3、NFT 这样的创新真的死了吗？最近在 Hyperliquid 和 Robinhood 上，我依然发现了一些有意思的 NFT 创新。也许不是创新已经消失了，而是行业还没有等到合适的时机。
4、预测市场，只能局限于现在这样的规模了吗？不能成为人们生活的日常吗？也不一定。

现在，大家已经看到稳定币形成了一条庞大且相对成熟的产业链。但预测市场、RWA、NFT，其实都还没有形成同样蓬勃、稳定的产业链。

这意味着什么？意味着它们还有很大的想象空间。

很多人觉得 Crypto 已经没有新故事了。

但我个人的感觉是：稳定币的产业链已经逐渐成熟，而其他赛道，甚至还没有真正开始。

也许我们现在看到的，只是下一轮创新周期的前夜。

text:
The divergence in AI output weirdly may be the highest it’s ever been, even though adoption is the broadest it’s ever been. 

A few years ago the best productivity gains you could get, even in the most capability-aligned field (like coding), was maybe 30-50% better productivity if you were very good at it. You’d spend a decent chunk of time cleaning up the mistakes of models, the context windows were too limited to do any long running work, and the interfaces required highly synchronous interactions. 

Now, the models can do far longer tasks at a time with limited human interaction. The harnesses support agentic work that can take on these larger tasks. The models are trained on vastly better datasets for a growing array of domains so you have to intervene far less. And we have systems that better support working with many agents at once. 

In just a two year timespan, the upper limits on productivity gains have gone from 30-50% to now likely 5-10X depending on the field. So we’ve gone from an environment where living at the frontier vs. not paying attention at all could be an order of magnitude difference in your output.

This distance is only getting wider from here given the rate of progress we’re likely to see with RSI. Crazy times.

text:
We may be getting closer to debugging neural networks like software

(Connecting the dots between two recent breakthroughs)

A few weeks ago, @nickcammarata, an interpretability researcher (previously with OpenAI), showed a breakthrough in understanding how neural networks work. “Work” in the sense of being able to understand which neurons determine a specific output of the network, which is a scientific field that hasn’t progressed significantly for a long time.

A big part of the breakthrough was AI progress itself - better agents can build research tools, run experiments and test explanations of what neurons and circuits actually do.

https://t.co/TZNTzqD1WM

Now this work shows GPT-6 Astra directly editing another model’s weights to fix a specific math problem (it slightly changed the weights of Qwen3.5 and improved its math performance ~6x).

Neural networks today are trained using a process of trial and error called gradient descent. We don’t explicitly write the detailed logic they learn, but rather adjusts the weights until the models outputs the desired result, and we only partly understand how those weights produce the model’s behavior.

That’s the breakthrough that seems to be beginning to take place - AI is helping us understand those internal mechanisms, and it is starting to make targeted changes to them.

Which brings neural networks (and LLMs) much closer to just being computers we can program. Input, some well defined computation, and output.

It will allow us to program AI in a very specific way, and do things like correct a specific fact inside a model, or change repetitive mistakes without retraining the whole thing.

It will also get AI closer to a deterministic machine, and not exactly AGI or some conscious entity

We asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to improve math.

author: MacroMate8
quoted_text:
Kind of crazy, but also not crazy at all, that this election will be decided based on data centers.

I don't think most people know what a data center really is, but it's become a proxy for what people really don't like: smug billionaire tech guys getting another HUGE win.

And even though I am pro business, AI, data centers, etc... generally, I think their staunch defenders are entirely missing the point.

People understand (correctly) that a small number of people are going to get obscenely rich from this technology.

And all the crowing in the world about how AI will benefit people, and level the playing field, is ringing very hollow to most people.

As it should.

AI is the opposite of democratizing, it is perhaps the most centralizing power and wealth creation event in all of human history.

I know it, you know it, and these billionaire tech people know it too.

So even though what's technically on the ballot is data centers, it's really about extreme wealth inequality.

My advice to people that have a big stake in the AI and data center game is to begin asking what genuine concessions you can make to society.

It doesn't matter what this technology can do for people, if it makes the pie increasingly uneven people will vote against it.

And it looks like that's exactly what's happening.

text:
Better infrastructure starts with better visibility.

@luganodes is helping developers distinguish expected network behavior from real issues, making it easier to build and monitor applications on TRON with confidence.
author: luganodes
quoted_text:
TRON apps that watch for new blocks should expect a short, planned pause four times a day, and Luganodes RPC gives you the block data to tell it apart from a real stall.

Here's why. @trondao's blocks are made in turns by a rota of elected block producers, one every three seconds. Every six hours the network takes a moment to count votes and set the next rota, and for about six seconds nobody produces a block.

On 23 Oct at 00:00 UTC, block 87,346,822 was followed by the next block nine seconds later instead of three. The boundary six hours earlier looked the same.

A gap like that is normal, and it only causes trouble when an app reads any delay as a sign that something is broken.

In practice, set block-stall alerts above nine seconds, or check the latest block against a second source before failing over, so monitoring doesn't fire four times a day for nothing.

On Luganodes RPC, /wallet/getnowblock and /wallet/getblockbynum on TRON's HTTP API cost a flat 30 CU like every TRON method, and the same key covers TRON's EVM JSON-RPC.

text:
Whether you like it or not the fact that people are investing their hearts and souls into SPX6900 is proof of the next evolution of money. 

When Bitcoin came out, it was not possible to invest your heart and soul into it. The memetics had not evolved yet. The internet was too young, there was no social media, and the technology was not mature enough. For the first decade of Bitcoin, early adopters could only really engage with its intellectual side: a challenge to the central banking system.

SPX6900 was born in an era when social media made it possible to engage in a higher dimension - with the emotional side of a community-made asset. 

It bridged the high-IQ, autistic tech-finance crowd with the high-EQ, artistic, community-builder types. Early NFT communities were actually the earliest examples of this phenomenon.

Intellect and emotion came together for the first time to create incentivised communities and virtuous feedback loops. And once you can do that, you can tokenise almost anything that people hold dear.

You can tokenise the belief that young people should inherit the world, and not just the problems left behind for them.

You can tokenise the belief that life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness are God-given rights that should be central to our money system.

You can tokenise the platinum rule: treat others the way they want to be treated.

You can tokenise the concepts of karma and samsara, and the idea that our worldly pursuits should not crowd out our connection to stillness.

You can tokenise the hope and belief that we are responsible for leaving the world a better place for our children to grow up in.

You can tokenise a shared identity, and a shared future.

Never before have we had an asset capable of acting as a vessel for expressing everything we know and believe has value.

For the pioneers who have already gone all-in with their hearts and souls, walking away is equivalent to going against everything they believe in.

chains are obviously essential to making all of this work but apps have so much more control over their own economics than chains do 

and the more obvious this becomes, the more capital + talent will flow toward the app layer, which means more competition, better products and hopefully a lot more actual users

pretty healthy evolution for the industry imo

quoted_text: There's a new kind of coding I call "vibe coding", where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good. Also I just talk to Composer with SuperWhisper so I barely even touch the keyboard. I ask for the dumbest things like "decrease the padding on the sidebar by half" because I'm too lazy to find it. I "Accept All" always, I don't read the diffs anymore. When I get error messages I just copy paste them in with no comment, usually that fixes it. The code grows beyond my usual comprehension, I'd have to really read through it for a while. Sometimes the LLMs can't fix a bug so I just work around it or ask for random changes until it goes away. It's not too bad for throwaway weekend projects, but still quite amusing. I'm building a project or webapp, but it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, and copy paste stuff, and it mostly works.

quoted_text:
The “tech-right” project is obviously failing now, though those with a stake don’t yet want to talk about it.

Broadly speaking, the mid-2020s optimism of this constituency was always predicated on one load-bearing promise: that we had entered an unprecedented point in history at which democracy was no longer enforceable.

Never before had a group of operators come to power brandishing signs which outwardly admitted to their Evil intent, loudly salivating at the thought of undermining the liberty and wellbeing of their underlings for some other purpose -- personal gain or something else.

But This Time was going to be different: there was clearly an increasing sense in which the key actors, with capital on their side, had started to feel invincible. Of course you could name your company Palantir, of course you could wave a sword around on a podcast, of course you could take your time answering whether the human race had the right to stick around -- democracy no longer worked! The cattle might have taken to the streets with pitchforks a century back, but we were in a different world now, and the subliminal conviction that the viability of mass surveillance, algorithmic manipulation, etc., was exponentiating -- neutering an already atrophied democratic base -- was infinitely emboldening.

Well, turns out all of that was wrong; turns out you can’t Just Be Evil -- at least not just yet -- and Karp now has to jolt awake and start lecturing about how much he feels for the working class and the drug addicts...

Turns out democracy is alive and well, turns out the Democrats might just sweep Congress, and you’ll be living in an old-fashioned virtue-signalling, Powell-Amodei-Carney, Obama 3.0 Neoliberal Revival World Order for the decade to come. I’m guessing we shouldn’t expect many more dithyrambs on Joe Rogan or the black T-shirts with Latin slogans

quoted_text:
Writing this in my personal capacity, but I have been flying these types of aircraft for more than 20 years, with over 8,000 hours, and have reasonable familiarity with how the charter world operates. I feel compelled to post after seeing commentary about the Lear 60 crash, from missile strikes to DEI to critiquing this poor woman’s final radio calls.

That last part is what I find most troubling. She was the second-in-command (SIC), and while she was empowered to point out mistakes as part of good crew resource management, she was doing her job, communicating with ATC right to the end in a terrifying situation. She likely knew before many of those calls that she was going to die. I have heard final calls from friends, from military pilots with thousands of hours in fighter aircraft, and they are just as heartbreaking because they know the end is approaching.

I understand the public interest given the footage and audio. But you do not know the aircraft’s maintenance history, whether there was a structural failure, if any failure was induced by turbulence, overspeed, or overcontrol, or everything happening in that cockpit. I am sure weather will be part of the investigation, but beyond that, it is speculation. The charter industry routinely hires commercial pilots very early in their careers to gain experience alongside an ATP-qualified captain before they move up to the airlines. She would still have the appropriate training, qualifications, and checkouts by an FAA examiner or designee.

Let people investigate, learn, and share the facts. Be respectful to those who perished and the families who carry their memories. God bless them and their loved ones.

在全网大盘经历避险阵痛、Robinhood 链上流动性洗牌之际，今天中午 12:11，Pons 官方（@ponsdotfamily）发出了一条极具分量的一句话预告：

“P(erps)ons in your pocket.（口袋里的 P(erps)ons）”

把双关语里的“Perps（永续合约）”与“in your pocket（装进手机钱包）”拆开，再结合链上最新的财务与储备数据，Pons 此时打出这手牌的底层逻辑非常清晰：

一、 底层数据的双面镜像：销毁逼近 33%，但国库 ETH 储备跌破 40 关口。
调取 Robinhood 链主网 RPC（区块 104,840,051）与 DefiLlama 实时数据：
1. 筹码通缩硬兑现：黑洞地址累计销毁达到 3.2893 亿枚 $PONS，占 10 亿总量的 32.89%；独立持币地址逆势突破 10.45 万个，筹码结构进一步分散；
2. 缓冲储备加速见底：作为回购买盘源泉的销毁合约（0x5795...），其 ETH 储备已从两周前的 108 ETH 持续消耗至今天的 38.69 ETH，储备消耗超过 65%；
3. 现货造血遭遇天花板：虽然 DefiLlama 协议手续费连续两日止跌回升至 22.6 万美元（日协议收入 3.14 万美元），摆脱了 10/31 恐慌时的低谷，但单靠现货发射台和 DEX 抽水，已经难以支撑更高强度的回购飞轮。

二、 为什么必须是“Perps in your pocket”？
在经历了前期 Meme 土狗内盘、以及 10/29 开启的美股代币流动性注资之后，Pons 的版图拓展到了最关键的一环,就是去中心化衍生品。
1. 降维打破现货天花板：Meme 发射台具有极强的周期脆弱性，遇到大盘黑天鹅极易缩量；而永续合约是全行业手续费沉淀最深、多空皆能抽水的赛道。切入 Perps，是 Pons 为国库补充高频现金流的必然选择；

text:
There are some great articles out there on agent factories and people doing autonomous engineering. I read them. This post is not that. This is my setup, and these are the results.

I talk, the machine builds. That is the whole idea.

On one Mac I run a fleet of Claude Code seats. One is the arbiter. One is the companion. One is the chief of staff who runs the show when I am away. Then a lead seat per piece of work, and one seat that only does end to end testing. Every piece of work is one PR with a sealed brief, a design round with a hard cap of three, a full test run on a sandbox box, a second review by a different model, a sign off row, then the label. My hands touch exactly two things: I launch a seat, and I push to production. Everything else is the machine.

Today it merged 35 PRs. Since we cut over to this way of working on Oct 24, it has merged 100 PRs and pushed to production 82 times. The app is Niko, a fitness coach you just talk to.

It was not clean. We lost an afternoon because the agents kept adding one more design round, one more, one more. So the rule now is three rounds, then ship what works and cut a ticket for the rest. When something breaks, I do not want a patch. I want the root cause fixed and a note so every agent and sub agent knows it. No overengineering. No new machinery.

And yes, we ran out of fuel tonight. Every seat at 95 percent of its window. So we are merging what is done and pausing until the account resets.

If you want to go fast, go deep first. More soon!!

The end of an era: saying goodbye to Cursor as my harness.

After using it for a solid two and a half years, being on the internal ambassadors and beta testers plan, having access to new features ahead of time and being able to peek behind the curtain, and after powering through many important challenges with it, it's time to say goodbye.

Apart from the outright rug of losing Opus and GPT usage when you move to merged accounts (X + Grok + Cursor) despite a promise to the opposite from support - see pics - there's also the problem of Grok models just being unusable for any human.

I do understand this aggressive cutover - the acquisition is forcing their hand in certain directions, and their path is now different from one of a swiss army knife of developer assist tools - but I cannot follow them on this path. I do, after all, need to get work done.

I'm back to codex as my primary harness.

To be fair and transparent, Grokbots are still running some menial tasks for me and this is what I will use my free Ultra account for - I have one selling my car, and another selling some baby related junk on a variety of marketplaces. 

One is tracking the social media performance of a side project (although even this I've moved largely to Claude), and one is keeping an eye on some real estate ads for me.

But I would never use them for serious work. Why? Because I already did, and I learned my lesson.

Thanks for everything Cursor team! It's really been a pleasure and an honor to participate in its growth!

text:
本周宏观拆解三：美国中期大选，国会花落谁家？共和党VS民主党，不同结果，带来短中期风险不同！

11月3日美国中期选举投票阶段正式结束，接下来就是维持一个月的计票、统计、选举结果认证、以及新旧议员交接阶段

截止目前统计，美国国会两院，共和党成为众议院多数党概率仅5%，而在参议院多数党概率也仅仅只有20%-25%之间，目前民主党明显占优势，并且优势还在扩大

目前特朗普的局面非常不利，北京时间11月4日上午8点——下午14点，美国各州投票正式结束，再次之前，特朗普还有几个摇摆州可以争取，尽量提高参议院胜率，否则特朗普面对的是痛失国会两院的的局面

目前摇摆州：南卡罗来纳州、北卡罗来纳州、缅因州、亚利桑那州、爱荷华州、得克萨斯州、威斯康星州

而其中爱荷华、缅因州、南卡、威斯康星州、亚利桑那等均是共和党现任，北卡州则是民主党现任，德克萨斯暂时空缺。

在本次选举中，特朗普面对这几个摇摆州，除了威斯康星州与亚利桑那州不参与改选投票，其他几个州按照权重来看优先要考虑 德州，爱荷华，缅因，南卡与北卡

德州+爱荷华，一个是红州根基，一个是民主党仅1%的领先，这两个应该优先争取

缅因州，共和党落后民主党6%个基点，差距可控，特朗普可能会降低干预权重交由共和党自己争取

南卡州，特朗普最不能丢的州，因为南卡是深红州，但是本次中期大选共和党在南卡的胜率居然走出了安全区间，这是一个非常危险的信号，一旦南卡失守，共和党在国家的局势会更加困难

北卡州，民主党已经占据绝大胜率，导致特朗普或者共和党在北卡州很难获胜，所以权重排到最后

当然，以上的内容决定了特朗普以及共和党在未来两年任期的政治环境，但是绝对不能把民主党赢美股跌，共和党赢美股涨作为主观判断，因为不同国会局面下，引导出来的财政、AI监管、与政治僵局等关键问题才是决定市场走向，以及金融局势的关键点

财政方面，共和党掌控国会是对财政支出最好的，短期利好风险市场，但是中长期会给债市带来压力，债市收益率过高对风险市场同样也是压制。反而民主党如果可以制衡，短期虽然不如共和党一家独大好，但是中长期可能会减少债市风险

AI监管，最怕民主党掌控国会，因为民主党对AI企业、数据中心建设以及相关监管可能比共和党更加严格，尤其是在目前美股Q3财报面对巨大挑战信心挑战的前提下，可能短期对美股更加不利，但是换个角度，更加严格的资本支出控制，将会减缓泡沫增速，减缓未来AI叙事风向

政治僵局，如果国会出现分裂局面，共和党占据参议院多数，民主党占据众议院多数，两党博弈从而引发财政刺激预期下降+赤字压力放缓+长短收益率压力放缓，短期利好金融与经济稳定性，但是中长期可能会增加政府关门风险以及债务上限博弈的风险。

阶段总结：

距离大选结束不足24小时，以目前的局面来看，最大乐观就是共和党拿下参议院，民主党拿下众议院，那么短期财政支出放缓，AI监管风险增加，财政刺激预期下降引发流动性担忧，美股高Beta股票，例如科技股短期承受政治不确定性的压力，但是利好成长股与蓝筹股

但是，中长期，政府赤字压力放缓，长端利率压力放缓，美股AI泡沫风险放缓，但是年底政府停摆风险又要增加！

text:
An MIT Media Lab study used EEG to track what happens in the brain when people write with ChatGPT rather than on their own. Fifty four students completed essay tasks while wearing electrode caps. One group used ChatGPT, one used a search engine, and one used no tools. Across sessions, the ChatGPT group showed the weakest neural connectivity in networks linked to memory, attention, and analytical work. They also had more trouble recalling what they had just written and produced more generic prose. The authors describe this as a kind of cognitive debt: the tool does the synthesizing, and the brain stays quieter [1].

The same experiment points to a better order of use. Students who first wrote unaided and only later switched to ChatGPT showed stronger recall and more widespread brain activity than students who started with the model and then had to work alone. In other words, the model helped more when it scaffolded thinking that was already underway than when it replaced that thinking from the start. The practical lesson is not that large language models should be banned. It is that they work best as a second pass, after the writer has already done the hard part of forming and remembering an argument [1].

[Kosmyna, N., Hauptmann, E., Yuan, Y. T., Situ, J., Liao, X. H., Beresnitzky, A. V., Braunstein, I., & Maes, P. (2025). Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task. arXiv. DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2506.08872]

text: It doesn't enumerate every sequence. Model checkers explore only reachable states, recording fingerprints so each unique state is visited once. Partial-order reduction collapses equivalent interleavings. Symmetry, abstraction and constraints shrink the space further. TLC routinely checks 10^7–10^9 states when the model stays abstract and state variables stay small. Beyond that, switch to theorem proving or bounded checking.

text:
Formal example: concurrent payment or lock system. TLA+ model-checks every interleaving and proves no double-spend or deadlock. Sampled agent evals miss rare races that appear only after millions of ops.

Eval example: agent implements a UI flow. Real runs capture screenshots/logs and score completion + UX. Formal state model abstracts away browser quirks, network flakes, and subjective polish.

Formal wins on exhaustive safety; evals win on messy real-world capability the model cannot capture.

text:
Marvell is buying Lumentum, the laser company, in an all-stock deal that values it at about $115B.

In my opinion this is the clearest sign yet that the next bottleneck in AI clusters is connectivity.

Lumentum makes the lasers and optical parts that move data between GPUs. Marvell makes the chips on the electrical side. Put them in one company and you can design the whole path a signal takes, from inside the chip package out to the next data centre.

Marvell's own deck shows why. Data moving between data centres is the 1x baseline. Inside a rack it's 100x. Inside the package it's 1000x. Every step closer to the GPU needs far more bandwidth, and that's where optics are heading next.

They put the combined market at $550B by 2030.

Nobody pays $115B for lasers unless they expect clusters to keep getting bigger for years. I think the links between GPUs are about to matter as much as the GPUs themselves

Your AI has access to your inbox, it has your credit card, and it even has permission to act.
But does it know where to stop?

We got industry leaders to talk about what happens when we give AI the keys, and what it takes to stay in control.

Joining the conversation:
Cy Khormaee (Founder & CEO, AegisAI Security)
Daniel Hooper (CISO, @meshpay)
Jay Prakash, PhD (Co-founder & CEO, Silence Laboratories)

From a fake Teams meeting with an AI avatar that endpoint protection stopped, to a coding agent that breaks its own rules, we get into the messy details of trust:

→ How a helpful assistant could expose your inbox to a colleague.
→ Why permission alone doesn't ensure an agent does what you intended.
→ What enforceable consent and verifiable actions could look like.

How much control would you hand over to an AI agent?

On the email users got, about converting points for KAST Pioneer Units.  Let me say this, and then will leave it for you to absorb.  

—-
First - 
We are super limited in the language we can use, because of country-by-country rules.  Use that for context, in what we released.  

Second - 
We didn’t just come up with some program out of thin air.   The conversion of points to KAST Pioneer Units, came after a long and super expensive process with Tier 1 law firms, and with approvals from investors to create this setup. It literally cost us millions just to setup.  We got legal opinions on dozens of countries.  Obviously, we would only do this because we are really trying our absolute best to create a strong program for the community.  

Third - 
Just to reconfirm.  
The KAST Pioneer Units, will be issued by a KAST-linked SPV.  This is the only practical step for issuance globally. The points will convert to the KAST Pioneer Units.  

There will be periodic cash out events.  We can’t legally promise you the amounts, the dates, whether it goes up or down.  No surprise in that. 

But we are putting in the hard work, so the community gets an outcome aligned to the success of KAST.

The only thing you have to do, is quickly accept the conversion, details early December in app.

Fourth - 
Why is there no token? Because no single project in the crypto card or Neobank space in history, has ever delivered a token which is not down.  Tokens are almost always not aligned to the community.  The founders and team most often end up with a treasury they wholly control, they along with investors cash out, and the token holders deal with the volatility and the ultimate decrease in price. 

By not launching a token, our team and investors get none of that optionality.  They stay locked in equity.  To date, I have personally only net purchased equity in KAST and never sold.  

Launching a token completely counter to our ambition to build a $100B+ company.  We believe the KAST Pioneer Units will be the best long term outcome, and in time people will realise this.  

Finally - 
We understand that in a market which is very far down, many are looking for anyway to cash out.  We get it.  There is real pain in crypto prices, many have seen their wealth fall substantially.  

But still strongly believe the KAST Pioneer Units, issued by the SPV, will ultimately prove to be the right decision.  Time be our witness.  

Thanks all.

text: 《比特币的“选举效应”：政治催化，还是撞上了减半周期？》（作者 Darko｜IOSG Ventures）本文通过历史数据比较美国中期选举后美股与比特币的表现，讨论选举是否真正构成市场上涨的催化剂。数据显示，1950 年以来的 19 次中期选举后，标普 500 指数一年内均录得上涨，平均涨幅为 15.1%；比特币经历的三个完整中期选举周期中，一年后价格也均有所上涨，平均涨幅约 54%，但选后短期往往继续下跌。文章指出，比特币中期选举与减半周期高度重合，且历史样本仅有三次，难以证明存在独立的“选举效应”。相比选举结果，未来市场走势更取决于美联储利率政策、ETF 资金流向及市场流动性，而国会控制权变化则可能影响加密市场结构立法的进展。阅读全文：https://t.co/zK8EBX7Cnv

text:
🧐31 岁的 Jeff Yan ，他把 Hyperliquid 当成「承载交易所的基础设施

笔者 @RyanJamesWeeks  专程前往华盛顿特区，与 Jeff Yan  @chameleon_jeff 交流，了解他一手打造、发展迅猛的加密平台 Hyperliquid 的后续战略规划。

我们在庄重的 Riggs 酒店一楼咖啡馆落座，他的安保人员在不远处保持警戒。交谈中我发现，这位 31 岁的创始人，未必会给出直白确定的答案。

这位估值达十亿美元级别的程序员，深谙加密行业的表述逻辑。外界普遍将 Hyperliquid 定义为数字资产交易所，但他始终强调，Hyperliquid 本身不是交易所，而是「承载交易所的底层基础设施层」。

他将其类比为互联网：在 Hyperliquid 之上搭建应用的开发者，需要自行设计风控与制衡机制。Jeff Yan 不愿空谈行业远景，更专注于代码研发。「我几乎所有时间都投入工作，」他说，「对我而言，工作占据了全部精力。」

这份投入带来了显著成果：Hyperliquid 最初只是一个离岸小众平台，主打永续合约（Perps），也就是全天候连续交易、无到期日的合约。如今它已经成长为核心交易市场，支持股票、黄金等各类资产的代理合约交易，平台过去 12 个月营收 7.13 亿美元。

Hyperliquid 于 2023 年上线，尽管并未面向美国市场开放，它的增长势头已经震动包括全球最大衍生品交易所 CME Group 在内的行业头部机构，也引起了白宫的关注。

Donald Trump 是加密行业支持者，去年通过自身加密项目获得超 14 亿美元收益，他曾表示监管机构正全力研究永续合约的监管框架。

Jeff Yan 常驻新加坡，本次到访华盛顿，为 Hyperliquid Policy Center 提供支持。该机构是独立游说主体，持续向美国监管机构提交文件，阐释平台的价值。

*图片来源：Greg Kahn，《彭博商业周刊》

之前开源的德扑复盘 Skill 更新了一大版，顺便换了个名字

ChipLeader

这段时间陆续改了不少东西，这次一起推上去了。

最主要的一条：Cash 和 MTT 的复盘流程重新梳理了。

现金桌看抽水、有效筹码、实际行动；锦标赛还要看奖级、筹码分布和覆盖关系。100bb 的深码锦标赛，依然按锦标赛分析。

复盘这块：

● 单手复盘：先给关键决策，再逐街拆范围、牌面和下注理由。缺位置、花色、筹码这些会影响结论的信息，就先问清。

● 对手调整：你给了相关数据和历史，再讨论怎么剥削。一个 LAG 标签、一手夸张的诈唬，还不足以支持“以后都跟到底”。

● 锦标赛：补强了泡泡圈、决赛桌、ICM、卫星赛和赏金赛的处理。比如 PKO，会区分覆盖对手、本次能否淘汰，以及实际能领到多少赏金。

● 批量牌谱：CoinPoker 锦标赛 txt 可以直接交给它，生成总览、逐手复盘、重复问题和练习建议。

● 中英文都能聊：英文提问就用英文解释，知识库主体目前仍是中文。

还有一块我挺在意：把计算和建议的边界写清楚了。赔率怎么算、范围假设是什么、哪些信息会改变结论，都要说明；没实际跑求解器，就不编精确频率和 EV 损失。
