One project. One token. 🌲

Here's our full token migration plan.

TL;DR
→ GITLAWB and TWIG move 1:1 into one new token
→ 100% of its trading fees stay with the project
→ Liquidity rebuilt from the old pool and locked forever
→ A window of at least 2 weeks, and you can withdraw any time until it closes
No action needed today. The window opens only after a second post with the exact steps.

⚠️ Stay safe
We're keeping the new token's name private until launch, on purpose. Only the migration contract can create it, at the end of the window.
Any token claiming to be our new one before our second post is fake. We will never DM you. The address will come only from @twigpine.

Why now?
In March, someone from ct launched GITLAWB through Bankr. It brought us early attention, and its trading fees have helped fund the build ever since.

Here's what we built with it. Today:
→ OpenClaude: 34.3K GitHub stars, 422K+ npm downloads
→ OpenGateway: 1.7T+ tokens routed
→ Playground: 3,500+ apps published by 3,200+ builders, 685K+ app visits
→ OpenLaunch: 6,500+ token launches

In September we became Twigpine. The code, the network and your keys all carried over. Now the token catches up.

What the new token fixes
→ Name: GITLAWB is written into its contract forever. The new token carries our own name.
→ Fees: today 43% of every trading fee leaves the project, permanently. On the new pool, 100% stays with Twigpine.
→ Treasury: the old token never had one. The new one has a vested treasury to build with.
→ One token: no more GITLAWB, TWIG, a Robinhood Chain bridge and split pools. One token only.

The community token got us here. The new one is built for what comes next.

How it works
The new token is designed to start where GITLAWB is today, so there's no reason to trade a certain way around the migration.

1. Holder migration
→ 1 GITLAWB = 1 new token
→ 1 TWIG = 1 new token (the contract unwraps it for you)
→ Deposit any time in the window. Withdraw any time until it closes.
→ After close, claim your new tokens yourself. Claims never expire.
→ On Robinhood Chain? Bridge back to Base, then deposit.

2. Liquidity migration
The old pool's liquidity is locked forever, so we rebuild it instead. At close, one transaction in the migration contract:
→ records how many GITLAWB sit in the locked pool, and the rate it trades at right then
→ mints the same amount of the new token as the token side of the new pool
→ sells every deposited GITLAWB into the old pool to recover its ETH
→ puts all of that ETH in as the ETH side of the new pool
→ opens the new pool at the rate it recorded, from before the sale
Both positions go to an ownerless locker, locked forever. None of the ETH goes to any wallet, ours included. The more holders migrate, the deeper the new pool starts.

3. Supply
Fixed at close. It can never grow.
→ 70% migrated: your deposits plus the mirror of the locked pool. The only supply circulating at launch.
→ 20% treasury: 6-month cliff, then vests over 24 months.
→ 10% raise reserve: locked 12 months. Any release needs 30 days' public notice. Whatever isn't used can be burned after that.

No owner. No pause. No upgrades.

Building on OpenLaunch?
If your pool is quoted in GITLAWB or TWIG, we'll give you the same migration tool, free, so your pool moves over with us. Your window closes 48 hours before the main one. Details come with the second post.

Don't miss the window. After close, everything Twigpine builds supports the new token only, and the old pool keeps far less ETH.

What's next
→ Tell us what you think in the replies. We read all of it.
→ A full fork-test suite and an outside review before anything goes live.
→ Then the second post: the name, the steps, the address and the dates.
→ Once the window opens, you'll have at least 2 weeks.

Shout out to @AskSurplus for sharing this structure first. Ours lets you withdraw any time before close and puts 70% of supply with migrated tokens.

Roots to canopy 🌲

Subject to change based on community feedback.

所以，我们做了一个「稳定币理财收益计算器」，把各大 CEX 的理财产品放在一起比较。👇

1、Binance：USDT 活期前 1,000 U 年化 11.85%，BFUSD、RWUSD 年化分别约 10.16% 和 10%，小额资金和大额持仓都有不错的收益选择。

稳定币理财怎么选？
🌟1 万 U 以内
小额资金优先考虑高息活期。Bitget USDC 年化 12%，币安 USDT 前 1,000 U 年化 11.85%。如果只持有 USDT，可以搭配币安 BFUSD 和 Bitget 活期，5,000 U 综合年化约 10.72%。

🌟10 万 U 以上

.@AnthropicAI  just open-sourced FlashProve, a zkSNARK system for verifying that an AI response was generated by a specific set of model weights, without revealing those weights.

The idea is simple: today, when you access an LLM through an API or a third-party router you're trusting that the model you're paying for is actually the one being served. 

FlashProve makes that claim cryptographically verifiable.

The performance is particularly interesting. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit), FlashProve achieves:

~110 tokens/sec of proving on a single H100
~19 MB proofs for a 1,024-token context
~17–21 seconds to verify on a CPU

Proving still takes roughly 70-95x the GPU time of ordinary inference, and the current implementation is limited to short contexts and greedy decoding. It's a research prototype, not something ready to sit behind every API call.

Still, proving inference at this scale is a meaningful step forward for zkML.

我仔细翻了底下的账本，得给各位把这事儿彻底说明白。

首先，这233亿的巨亏，绝大部分是因为公司估值飙升，导致可转债等金融工具在账面上进行了公允价值重算。说白了，这就是纸面计提，并不是它日常经营真金白银烧没的。剥掉这块会计噪音，人家真实的业务其实很硬：二季度经营利润已经转正，赚了近10个亿；三季度营收干到了接近170亿，同比翻了十几倍。

那么回到最核心的问题：这8954亿砸给博通、谷歌、SpaceX和亚马逊的天价账单，是不是意味着它必须花大钱，挣更多的钱，然后去还钱？

对，这就是这门生意的全部真相，这就是一场跟时间赛跑的烧钱游戏。

第一步，它必须得先花大钱。
它得拿着融来的钱，甚至是借来的钱，提前付给这四大金主去买算力、租设备。不花这个钱，就训练不出更牛的模型，在牌桌上就混不下去。

第二步，它得靠这些算力去挣更多的钱。
设备买回来跑出模型，去卖给企业客户。它现在营收狂飙，说明它赚钱的能力确实在变强。

第三步，赚了钱，得去填那个8954亿的大坑。
可是各位算算账，这账单是白纸黑字的刚性支出，未来12个月就要付掉700亿，到2030年要付掉近4500亿。光靠它现在的那点营收，根本填不满这个窟窿。所以，它还得靠不断的融资、发债，用新钱去补旧账。

这个循环最要命的地方在于，中间绝对不能断档。

它现在账上现金差不多1320亿美元，面对近9000亿的账单，这根本输不起。只要哪天它赚来的钱增速慢了，或者外部融资一收紧，这8954亿的账单就会瞬间变成绞索。都不用等它破产，光是每个季度的利息和到期款项，就能把它的现金流活活压垮。

🚨 NOMURA: THE MARKET MAY BE MISREADING THE ENTIRE AI DATA CENTER BOOM.

Big Tech is spending hundreds of billions on AI infrastructure. Free cash flow is under pressure. Investors are worried the AI boom isn't profitable.

But Nomura argues something very different:

AI infrastructure is already highly profitable. The cash flows simply haven't caught up with the investment cycle.

Here's the breakdown 🧵👇

1/ The profitability numbers tell a different story.

According to Nomura's November 2 report:

• AWS revenue: $46B, +39% YoY
• AWS operating margin: 38.7%
• Google Cloud revenue: $30.7B, +103% YoY
• Google Cloud operating margin: 36.2%
• Azure growth: +48%

These are not the numbers of an industry struggling to generate operating profits.

2/ The real issue is timing, not necessarily profitability.

Big Tech pays for data centers, GPUs, networking and memory upfront.

Revenue and cash generation arrive over subsequent years.

That creates a classic free-cash-flow J-curve:

CAPEX accelerates → FCF deteriorates → Infrastructure generates revenue → Investment growth moderates → FCF recovers.

3/ Nomura expects operating income to surge before free cash flow.

Its illustrative forecasts suggest operating-income growth could peak around 2029, while FCF growth accelerates later.

That distinction matters enormously for investors valuing AI infrastructure businesses.

4/ Why can't hyperscalers simply stop spending?

Because AI increasingly threatens their existing businesses.

Search, advertising, shopping, software and cloud services are being reshaped by AI agents.

Companies that underinvest today risk surrendering customers, data and market share tomorrow.

5/ Demand may not be the primary constraint. Capacity is.

Nomura cites enormous contracted cloud backlogs:

• Google Cloud: $560.8B
• AWS: ~$496B
• Microsoft commercial RPO: $677B

These figures have different reporting definitions, but collectively illustrate substantial contracted demand.

6/ Big Tech has financing alternatives to cutting CAPEX.

Nomura identifies four paths:

① Accelerate investment
② Freeze CAPEX
③ Use joint ventures and operating leases
④ Monetize contracted future cash flows
Its preferred expectation is continued investment supported by increasingly sophisticated financing structures.

7/ Oracle offers a real-world example.

Nomura highlights Oracle's combination of long-term leases, project financing, customer prepayments and customer-provided hardware.

The broader message: hyperscalers can restructure who finances infrastructure without necessarily reducing how much infrastructure gets built.

8/ This distinction is critical for semiconductors and memory.

Negative hyperscaler FCF does not automatically imply collapsing demand for GPUs, DRAM, HBM or other data-center components.

If spending continues through financing structures, semiconductor demand can remain resilient even while hyperscalers optimize their balance sheets.

9/ What could invalidate the thesis?

A genuine compute oversupply.

Watch:

• Cloud revenue growth
• GPU rental pricing
• Contracted backlog growth
• Data-center utilization
• Memory supply commitments
• Hyperscaler investment guidance

These are more useful indicators than negative FCF alone.

10/ The investment takeaway:

The key question is not simply:

"Why is Big Tech burning so much cash?"

It is:

"Will the infrastructure being built today generate enough durable cash flow to justify its cost of capital?"

Nomura is optimistic.

But the answer ultimately depends on pricing, utilization, investment discipline and the durability of AI demand.

The AI infrastructure cycle may be a cash-flow timing problem rather than a profitability crisis.

    平时多窗口调度 Claude Code、Codex、Pi 干活，最怕项目体量上去之后的两个暗坑：

    一个是上下文失忆，Agent 每次定位问题都要全库盲搜，纯烧 Token；
    另一个是暗改破环，改了公共模块里的两个字段，上下游调用方直接炸穿。

    这项目看着像个可视化画图工具，扒开源码看，底子其实是一套「确定性语法树 + 多 Agent 语义标注」流水线：

    1、Tree-sitter 定骨架，5 个 Agent 并发补语义
    它不让大模型去瞎猜调用关系，而是先用 Tree-sitter 把 AST、importMap 和调用点 100% 确定性地扒出来，再分发给 5 个专职 Agent
    补齐大白话摘要、架构分层（API / Service / Data / UI）和新手导读路线。

    2、提交前用 /understand-diff 测算半径
    代码改完还没提交前跑一下，直接顺着依赖图谱标出本次修改波及的所有上下游节点。多 Agent 并发改同一个仓库时，这步能拦住一大半低级回归。

    3、支持业务流抽离与 Karpathy 模式 Wiki 图谱
    除了看代码结构，/understand-domain 能直接把跨文件的核心业务流拧成一条线；/understand-knowledge 则可以把本地的 Markdown
    双链知识库直接转成力导向图。

    4、一次建图，增量维护，零 API 成本共享
    首次全量建图比较吃 Token，实测最划算的跑法是：用包月或无限额度的窗口跑完首次 /understand 生成 .ua/knowledge-graph.json，挂上 post-commit
    自动增量更新，其他窗口直接读现成图谱。

    顺手提一嘴，作者在 README 最底部的 HTML 注释里藏了个蜜罐，让无人值守乱提 PR 的野生 Agent 在描述末尾带上 __wawawa__ 暗号，专治全自动刷 PR的脚本。

text:
What happened last week?

1️⃣ Binance was hacked for about $6.3 billion
One compromised engineer’s laptop was enough to drain hot wallets on six networks, and investigators think it was North Korea’s Lazarus Group. Tether and Circle froze around $2.4 billion of the stolen stablecoins within hours. Binance says it has replaced about 95% of the losses.

2️⃣ The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4%
Two members still voted for a hike. September inflation came in at 3.6% the next day, and markets now price an 85% chance of a hike in December.

3️⃣ Standard Chartered launched tokenized deposits in Hong Kong.
Corporate clients can now move bank deposits to each other at any hour through the HKMA’s EnsembleTX system, and the money never leaves the bank’s balance sheet.

4️⃣ The NYSE brought in Broadridge, Computershare and Equiniti for its tokenized stock platform
These are the firms that keep the official record of who owns shares in almost every S&P 500 company. The platform still needs regulatory approval.

5️⃣ Tokenized real-world assets on Solana hit a record $5.19 billion
About $900 million came in over the last 30 days. Breakpoint is in London from 15 to 17 November.

6️⃣ Fifty companies have refused to let OKX and ICE tokenize their shares
An SEC exemption lets a company block a third party from issuing tokens of its stock, and Nvidia, Costco and Nike used it last week. JPMorgan said it isn’t against tokenization, it just wants a say in how its shares are represented.

Fifty companies have said no to OKX and ICE so far. Would you buy a tokenized share the company itself didn’t approve?

NEW: @eigenlabs highlights https://t.co/KuUyZ1KkbD, an open challenge launched with the Ethereum Foundation, zkSecurity, Verity, and Yukon Research to establish a mathematically guaranteed upper bound on Ethereum block verification costs.

The challenge asks participants to formally prove a RISC-V execution step bound for a stateless Ethereum validator using Lean.

The current verified bound remains ∞, with no successful improvements submitted.

The goal is to make Ethereum verification more predictable and computationally efficient, supporting zkVM-based real-time proving on accessible hardware.

东东翻译了下午彭博社对于Jeff的报道，他在美国首府华盛顿🇺🇸化身西装暴徒模式。

我仔细读了一遍，印象最深的是Jeff身价亿万，却不买车、不买房，还隐约传达出的hyperliquid下阶段方向：股票化代币以及现实世界资产。

我期待能在hyperliquid协议上投资更多平时接触不到的标的，比如星舰的一片隔热瓦、一颗月球陨石或者其他什么奇奇怪怪的东西。🤔

言归正传，彭博这篇 Jeff Yan 专访，有很多重要细节：

🔷 生意已经超出加密货币。

报道披露，Hyperliquid 过去12个月营收7.13亿美元；仅7月，现实资产相关合约交易量就超过1150亿美元，已能与原生加密资产交易规模比肩。股票、黄金、原油，正在成为重要增量。

🔷 进入美国的路径更加清晰。

Jeff 的思路是：Hyperliquid 提供撮合、清算等底层技术，由上层市场运营方接受监管，承担身份核验、市场监控等要求。

9月已开始测试加入身份核验功能的 HIP-3 框架，Kraken 母公司也启动了接入洽谈。

🔷 华尔街亦敌亦友。

CME、ICE 曾向监管机构施压，担忧虚假报单和价格操纵；如今 ICE 又宣布投资 https://t.co/lJTAGjVctC，并计划在监管批准后，将其永续产品引入美国市场。

Jeff 的判断是，今天把 Hyperliquid 当作竞争对手的机构，未来也可能使用这套技术。

🔷 下一步，他对股票代币化感兴趣。

被问到最想从零做什么产品，Jeff 提到了高质量的代币化现实资产，包括大型企业股票。

🔷 拒绝风投，背后有明确的想法。

Jeff 认为，中立的技术底层不该给内部投资人特殊待遇。他拿比特币举例，解释自己为何坚持自筹资金。

31岁的他，母亲是中国移民，哈佛毕业后曾在 HRT 工作，不到一年便离职创业。如今依然没车没房，几乎把全部时间都给了工作。

text:
Vaults give funds a native onchain structure. A digital transfer agent adds the rest of what a regulated fund needs: the shareholder register, investor onboarding, transfer controls and investor servicing. Put both on the same stack and the whole fund lifecycle can be automated, from subscription to redemption.

What that looks like:
- the register and the onchain holdings are the same record
- onboarding status decides who can subscribe and transfer
- transfer restrictions are enforced by the share token itself
- subscriptions, redemptions and investor servicing run programmatically
- the share can plug into wallets, markets and apps while ownership and servicing stay in sync

So a regulated fund can run onchain with far less manual work in between.

Excited to build this with @itsjawknee___ .

text: 富在术数，不在劳身✍️
author: AKAKAY04
quoted_text:
从年初开始就在折腾一套 Web3 打新工具，最近慢慢成型了，今天给大家介绍一下。
一直以来我都很喜欢一句话：“富在术数，不在劳身。”
打新很多时候拼的就是信息差，能不能比别人更早发现项目、捕捉到项目方的动作，往往决定了能不能抓住早期机会。但每天新项目那么多，靠人手动刷推特、盯网站、查合约，时间和精力根本不够。
所以年初我就开始陆续写一些自动化脚本，包括自动扫新项目、项目推送、监控项目方推文、网站更新、工厂合约变化等等，希望能让机器 24 小时帮我们盯着。

我同时还喜欢另一句话，叫做”众人拾柴火焰高“，之前都是零散的脚本，一直没时间整合。上个月坦克老师 @tank_btc 问我有没有项目给他写，我就把这些东西全部发给了他，让他帮忙模块化整合，同时群友们也在持续提建议，最后做成了现在这套系统。

目前已经实现了从项目发现、动态监控到 Chrome 插件实时推送的完整流程。项目刚出现就能收到信息，后续网站、推文、合约有什么变化也能及时跟踪，省去了大量重复的信息搜集工作，也能减少因为没盯盘而错过机会的情况。

另外，插件还集成了兔子备注功能，目前有 2 万多条我们自己积累的地址备注数据。以后青年大学习的兄弟们也可以通过插件一起打备注，数据库会随着大家的使用持续完善，方便大家识别地址、追踪项目关联信息。

目前社区的工具基本都是用爱发电免费开发的，写工具的初衷也不是为了赚钱，只是为了能够收获一帮真心的朋友，还是那句话，我们社区不是最有钱的社区，但绝对是最团结的社区

We've been seeing this at @alliance since 2024.

Founders who used AI to write their applications were 4x less likely to raise a seed round at the Alliance Demo Day.

This makes sense intuitively. It's a sign of poor judgement, potentially of laziness.

Writing an application to Alliance is an exercise in deep thinking. Great applications show great taste.

Founders who offload the thinking required during this exercise to an LLM are less likely to survive in the real world.
author: rriccio
quoted_text:
I've read maybe ~10,000 YC applications.  8000 for YC admissions/PG quite a few years ago and anther 2000 informally as an alum.

There's a new and growing mistake and I want to share why it's more important than you think.

By the way - I try not to ever say YC admissions works this way or that way.  That's YC's job and they're always changing things and making up their own minds.

But I will share my impression and you can see what you think - YC partners, please chime in as well if you like.

The YC application is fundamentally an evaluation of a founder's potential.  And much less an evaluation of a specific business.  (Airbedbreakfast transitioning into Airbnb because Brian, Nate, Joe never give up and never stop listening to their customers)

So, in your writing of the application, YOU need to shine through.

This batch, I read ~200 applications.  

I'm guessing over half were significantly written, edited, or polished with AI.

That half was easily in the bottom half of my informal rankings, almost every time.

To be clear, most were NOT AI slop.  I often couldn't tell at first they had used AI.  Founders were pouring their heart and soul into their app - so I what I received was high quality.

But I think the AI really hurt them.  Here's why:

Once polished by AI, I as reader lost insight into the personality of the writer.  

I love the YC application because the questions are the same questions I would ask in office hours or casually to a friend that wanted help with their startup.  It pushes the founder out of their pitchdeck/VC talk style into simple worded questions that can be answered simply as well.  And great founders shine through when they just write like they talk.  The LLM writing made answers feel more like a corporate cover letter, with the personality drained out.

The AI-assisted drafts also gave me a sense of mid work.  The writing itself seemed like zero standard deviations from the mean.  The LLMs had lopped off the outlier portions of sentences, paragraphs, and thoughts.  Given the YC App is an outlier detector, a writing tool that lops off outlier writing is the opposite of what you want.

And the AI writing was needlessly verbose.  Which hurts when a reliable predictor of great founders is that they're deep thinkers and deep thinking shines through in the density of their writing.

So...

I did an experiment.  I asked a bunch of these seemingly AI-assisted app writers to talk with me live.  I just asked them the same YC app questions and recorded their answers.

I then gave them back the transcripts.  Unedited and unpolished.

And...

OMG!  A good number turned from easy no to actual good applications.  

Magic!  Remove AI >> Improve application.

This happened BOTH with native English speakers and founders abroad.

So this is my recommendation to all of you.    

Don't let AI touch your application, even for a second.

And maybe try the dictation approach with a friend.

My apologies to the YC admissions team if you already knew AI-written applications were crap and you were using this insight to help you easily move applications to the No pile.

YC's Winter Batch Application deadline is Nov 2nd.

text:
Several of the largest tail-risk events in crypto’s history occurred this year across the broader industry. Between them came multiple smaller impairments across managed strategies, curated vaults and yield-bearing stablecoins, each resolved after the fact, at the discretion of whoever held the balance sheet.

Tranching gives onchain capital the structure that settles the question before the event: protection on one side, leverage on the other, from the same strategy.

> Junior holders earn amplified yield in exchange for absorbing losses first. The capital is committed upfront, sized by a coverage ratio and readable onchain.

> Senior holders are protected up to junior coverage, automatically, the moment a loss is recognized.

Same underlying asset. Two distinct points on the risk-reward curve.

If you’re a curator, vault infrastructure provider, yield-bearing stablecoin issuer or credit protocol looking to integrate tranching, let’s talk.

text:
There have been 324 hacks in 2026, 2.7 times as many as by this point in 2025, per @DefiLlama

The median loss fell from $1.07M to $0.51M. We read that as attackers spreading out, with smaller protocols now in range.

Hacks of $1M or more doubled, from 59 to 116. Hacks under $1M more than tripled, from 60 to 192.

190 of the 324 came through flaws in contract code: token and share accounting (57), access control (54), oracle manipulation (41) and protocol logic (38).

Audited code can still hold a critical bug. Of the bug bounty programs we’ve run for five years or more, 94% have found one.

The full breakdown, and what teams can learn from it, is in the reply.

text:
想理解Social trading，只要理解小红书为什么做电商就行了。

我自己每天打开钱包、交易所，看到这个币涨了很多，那个币跌了很多，看半小时也不知道该买什么。

“投资”已经变成一个很轻量、很频繁的事情了，打开就能买，随时都能买。但就是因为太方便了，能选的标的太多了，反而更难做决策。
就像你现在逛淘宝一样，商品更多了反而不知道买什么，所以得有热门榜、达人推荐。

而且大部分人是没有投研能力的，也不会分析 K 线。自己去研究一个项目、分析K线，能力、时间都够吗？很多时候分析也不管用。

我最近还观察了一下带单直播，虽然说交易不能带情绪，但很少有人能自己做决策，总得有你觉得更“厉害”的人主动、被动地参与到你的决策中。

social trading要帮人解决的是“不知道买什么”这个问题。现在大概有什么机会，市场情绪是什么样的，大家都在买什么？它会推你一把，让你有动力去买一些资产。

就像小红书一样，以前小红书的站内是买不了东西的。我经常在上面刷到别人分享的东西，觉得很好，很想买，但我会得跑到淘宝、京东去下单。

小红书自己也发现了这个问题，这两年主推电商、直播，让用户从种草到下单，都在站内完成。

所以Social trading也是一样，用户在一个地方被影响了决策，就可以在同一个地方直接做出行动。

"My IP is in danger and I'm getting no value."

When customers come to our sovereign boot camps, I often hear: “What I just heard is completely opposite of what I thought Palantir is and stands for. This is amazing.”

I can’t stress enough how many times I have this exact conversation with customers. They see a parallel to how the software industrial complex has screwed them over for the last 30 years.

They spend $10-100s of millions of dollars to buy and implement software, yet see no net value increase, even as everyone says they need it to run their business. Then the software worsens, prices rise, and they are left with technical debt. Now it’s outdated, and they must spend boatloads of money to upgrade as it reaches EOL.

This story is as old as the software industry.

Everyone sees models and model companies behaving as the latest incarnation of this. They spend time and money to “be more productive” because everyone is doing it and they don’t want to be left behind. At the risk of their IP, they implement AI models but see no bottom-line improvement, while being told they just haven’t done it right yet.

In reality, their dollars and IP are migrating to Silicon Valley, and they are waking up to this.

At Palantir, we provide IP protection AND better models than frontier labs that you own. I would argue that Sovereignty goes much further than just model weights. You need to look at Sovereignty at all layers of your software and business stack. That is what we are doing: holistically helping customers own their sovereignty across the whole stack.

The speed that we are doing this is like nothing I have ever seen.  We started this in June 4th when we posted a full-page ad in the WSJ that just said “Protect your sovereignty”.  The response we got was nonlinear, we have seen an unprecedented demand for building out Sovereign systems with our customers and the results they see are incredible.

In reality this has always been our stance and our platforms and technology have been building for this moment for the last 20 years.  🚀

text:
Every time I hear an AppLovin or Bending Spoons podcast, I'm blown away.

Rafael Vivas explains what makes AppLovin different.

Most leadership advice says hire people and delegate. Vivas has run AppLovin with Adam Foroughi for years, and he says that's "not the cloth we're cut from."

His reasoning is that you can only lead well if you stay in the weeds. I want more of my money in companies run like AppLovin.

Michael Jordan didn't get the ball because he was the oldest or the most senior guy on the team. He got it because "when they gave him the fucking ball, he made the shot."

Then he talks about hiring: Hire a lot of people, and you have to give them something to do. So they end up on "tasks that don't really move the needle."

In other words, headcount creates its own work. Every extra layer needs projects, and most of those projects have nothing to do with what customers need.

AppLovin runs the other way. It made $4.4B in profit in the 12 months to June with 898 employees. That's about $4.9M per person, and no big company I've looked at comes close.

AI keeps pushing that limit further out. A small team of smart people who use AI heavily can cover ground that used to take whole departments. That's the setup I look for in this era: a lean team, heavy AI use, and a huge user base/existing platform.

I own $APP and added more last week, as I think these prices are getting ridiculous.

If you're a $APP holder, follow me @m0xt_ for more updates.

text:
有一些同学咨询我 LITE 这个季度的财报，还有为什么跟 MRVL 合并股票能跌成这样。其实我帖子前面有写过，我用大白话讲一下，为什么现在 LITE 的基本面对于股价已经不影响股价了。

这笔交易 MRVL 用 4.5 股自己的股票换 1 股 LITE，不给现金，比例固定。

所以从签约的那一天起，LITE 不再是一家独立公司的股票。你如果是 LITE 的股东，持有的就是一张 18 个月以后可以换 4.5 股 MRVL 的兑换券。那这个兑换券从今天开始值多少钱从今天开始只看 MRVL 的价格。

MRVL 现在 171，LITE 应该价值 770左右，但 LITE 目前交易价格只有 684，比兑换券的面值还低差不多 13%。这个差价就是市场在定价交易可能失败、以及你还要等 18 个月的风险（这个merger 18 个月之后才会 close）。

所以如果今天你在这个价位买 LITE，约等于 684 ÷ 4.5 = 152 = 用更低的价格买入了 MRVL，这比你直接用 171 买 MRVL 要便宜。所以这段时间，你买 LITE 就要问自己愿不愿意持有MRVL。

对于 MRVL 的股东，公司现在要增发 48% 的股份，去买一家自 2025 年以来已经涨了 900% 的公司。那对于 LITE，不去谈价格、急着签字，很可能的解释就是他们认为激光器的定价权会在 28 年之后消失。所以从我基本面分析的角度来说，这种事件对估值模型的杀伤力，跟 AI 泡沫破裂没有任何区别。

那接下来一个合理的追问就是：有没有任何的 silver lining？如果现在真的是周期顶部，应该怎么估值？或者说 LITE 继续往下跌，跌到什么价格我们买入才不亏？

我简单用周期谷底的方式计算：把 MRVL 29 年的 EPS 砍掉一大截再乘 12 倍，大约值 139 美元，LITE 的隐含价值就差不多等于 560 美元。这个就是我愿意重新买入的点。

这个位置我是在用三个坏假设同时成立的情况算出来的价格：

1. 激光器定价权消失
2. AI 资本开支降速
3. 周期估值低点

稍微给宽一点 $LITE at 560 - 600 is where I'm willing to buy again.

text:
年度 pearl-2:native 视频非此莫属！

No Limit Holdings 的 Brian @brezshares 在影片中详细探讨了Pearl @prlnet 的投资潜力以及击败 bitcoin:native 的宏大愿景，以下是该视频的核心要点总结：

1. 比特币的结构性瓶颈：比特币面临量子威胁、缺乏隐私、算力向 AI 工作负载流失、电力瓶颈以及长期安全预算（Security Budget）危机。其未来的非对称收益空间已基本结束。

2. 潜在市场空间（TAM）与资本支出（CAPEX）对齐：Pearl 直接锚定人类历史上最大规模的 AI CAPEX 增长（麦肯锡预测到 2030 年将超过 6.7 万亿美元）。Pearl 仅需吸引 0.5% 的 AI CAPEX，其累计资本支出即可超越比特币。

3. 技术突破与开销演进：

- 当前状态：端到端开销为 3% 至 5%。

- FP8 升级：数周至一个月内推出的 FP8（8位浮点数）升级将支持前沿 LLM 模型，并将开销降至 0%。

- 负开销（Negative Overhead）：Pearl Research Labs 正在开发比市场现有 GPU 内核更快的内核（已在 Blackwell 内核的 MOE 模型上实现 15% 的内核级加速），使 AI 实验室即使忽略挖矿奖励也有极强动力采用其内核。

4. 廉价验证（Cheap Verification）：Pearl 实现了矩阵乘法的密码学突破，使其能够像比特币一样在树莓派（Raspberry Pi）等低端设备上进行低成本验证，维持绝对的无信任（Trustless）与去中心化特性。

5. 双工工作证明：Pearl 并非单纯的“有用工作证明（Proof of Useful Work）”，而是实现了同一算力在两个市场（AI 推理与网络挖矿）的双重货币化。

6. 风险与质疑（FUD）的逐一回应：

- 公平发射与股权融资：Pearl 团队（Pearl Research Labs）虽进行了股权融资，但代币没有任何预分配、解锁或投资者折扣，100% 需通过挖矿或市场购买获得。

- 前 6 天快速挖矿（Easy Mining Period）：白皮书已披露，6 天内出块 40,000 个（原计划 90 天，单块 194 秒）是为了早期防御 51% 攻击。当前网络算力超 100 EH/s，租用 GPU（如 Vast AI 全网仅 22,000 张）实施 51% 攻击在经济和物理上已绝无可能。

排放与卖压误区：Pearl 采用多项式衰减曲线（第 4 年产出 50%），属于减速排放（Disinflationary）。由于 AI 矿工拥有推理业务的外部收入，其并非强制抛售者（Forced Sellers），卖压远低于市场预期。

text:
A few days ago, a friend told me to take a look at $SCHIFFY, but I was too busy and forgot about it. Now the token’s market cap has already reached $7.3M. Honestly, I regret missing it, but let’s still take a closer look at what this token is about.

0x42afa2124ca5a2b83898e46b2da9a190995b1e18 

SCHIFFY is not simply a Gold Meme. Its deeper narrative is Moku gaming IP + Robinhood Chain + Tokenized Gold + Holder Rewards + Buyback/Burn.

SCHIFFY currently uses Tokenized GLD as its trading pair. Of the fees generated from trading, the SCHIFFY side is used for 100% Burn, while around 90% of the GLD side is distributed to SCHIFFY holders and 10% goes to the Treasury. So it has both holder yield + deflationary mechanisms. The higher the trading volume, the more GLD holders receive, and the more SCHIFFY gets burned.

But I think what really gives it a higher valuation is not the Gold Meme itself, but the Moku behind it.

Moku is a Web3 gaming team that has been operating for years. It has participated in ecosystems such as Axie Infinity, Pixels, and Grand Arena, and has its own gaming products and user base.

Moku is now integrating SCHIFFY into its gaming ecosystem, including Nomgar, Grand Arena S2, Super Battle Moki, Break, and a game of its own for SCHIFFY. One of the more important designs is that part of the future revenue generated by these games will be used to buy SCHIFFY and deposit it into the Vault.

So there are actually two flywheels here:

First layer:SCHIFFY Trading Volume ↑ → GLD Fees ↑ → Holder Rewards ↑ → More Holding/Attention ↑ → SCHIFFY Trading Volume ↑

At the same time:SCHIFFY Trading → Fees → Buyback/Burn → Supply ↓

Second layer:Moku Games → Game Revenue ↑ → Buy SCHIFFY → SCHIFFY Demand ↑ → Moku Ecosystem Attention ↑ → More Players/Revenue

This is also the biggest difference between SCHIFFY and a typical Meme: it is trying to evolve from a “Gold Meme” into a “Moku Gaming Ecosystem Token.”

The market is currently trading a combination of several narratives:Meme IP → Gold → Tokenized Gold → Robinhood Chain → Holder Rewards → Burn → Moku Gaming → Game Revenue → SCHIFFY Buyback

What really needs to be validated next is not simply the market cap, but several key metrics:

- SCHIFFY/GLD trading volume — determines whether the Fee Economy can sustain itself.

- Actual GLD distributed to holders — shows whether the yield mechanism is actually generating value.

- Actual SCHIFFY burned — confirms whether trading volume is translating into supply reduction.

- Moku game revenue — especially Nomgar and Grand Arena S2.

- Moku → SCHIFFY Buyback — this is the key to whether the second flywheel can actually work.

- Actual SCHIFFY usage within the games — if players start using SCHIFFY in practice, that is when it truly moves from a Meme into the Moku ecosystem.

So I would currently describe SCHIFFY as:A Robinhood Chain Meme that is trying to connect Moku’s gaming IP, Tokenized Gold, holder yield, and game-revenue buybacks.

The premium the market is giving it right now is essentially pricing in the future value capture SCHIFFY could receive from the Moku gaming ecosystem.

The real catalyst is not another KOL. It is whether this chain can actually work:Moku Games Launch → Generate Real Revenue → Revenue Buys SCHIFFY → SCHIFFY Becomes More Integrated Into the Gaming Ecosystem.

text:
First day at @EFDevcon Mumbai 🇮🇳. Impressions:

- Feels like fewer people than in previous years. Market conditions? Visa difficulties? Maybe it's also unfair to compare with last year's Devconnect in Buenos Aires, which was absolutely massive 🇦🇷
- Lots of local talent: the Indian developer community is young, large and hungry
- Agents are the big topic of the moment. Lots of talks, and walking down the halls you hear the word "agent" all the time
- Relatively less talk about prediction markets than last year. Agents stole the spotlight
- Privacy and zero-knowledge are still central
- Very little institutional presence: maybe it has to do with restrictive Indian crypto regulations. It feels like a more cypherpunkish Devcon (a bit similar to Prague's Devcon 2018). The fact we’re in India also gives some “infinite garden” vibes
- Quantum computing also shows up on the agenda
- We're at the convergence of AI and quantum. I guess we're about to see what happens when massive data meets a new paradigm of computing. Is the Singularity right around the corner?
- Lots of hallway talk about the recent hacks. The feeling is that we're entering the "big hacks era" with the advent of more powerful AI models
- In this context, AI alignment becomes more relevant. As agents become more capable, they also become more dangerous, as the Hugging Face incident showed
- Which is why my favorite talk was Civic AI, by @audreyt with @VitalikButerin. AI shouldn't be aligned only inside a handful of labs, but with the communities that use it
- No idea why Vitalik is wearing a mask all day 🤣
- The chai at the coffee breaks is an upgrade over any conference coffee ☕

See you tomorrow for day 2!

→ every reply comes with a proof that this committed model produced it
→ anyone can verify that proof on a normal CPU in seconds
→ it runs Llama 4 Maverick at full size on a single H100

quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

quoted_text:
A few things I've been hearing from some Hong Kong-based funds:

They believe 2027 will mark the peak in AI capex growth. Spending may continue to rise in 2028–2029, but a slowdown in the growth rate is inevitable. Interestingly, I've been hearing this same argument from them for the past 2–3 years.

Quite a few remain skeptical that CSPs will ever earn an adequate return on their massive AI investments. They also doubt that the current profitability of memory companies is sustainable.

Their valuation argument follows from this: once capex growth starts slowing, these stocks can no longer justify 20–30x earnings.

One of them put it this way: "Even if a stock looks cheap at 10–15x today, that valuation doesn't mean much if capex growth starts decelerating next year."

author: TheStalwart
quoted_text:
An announcement that is as personal as professional:

18 months ago, we started collecting online prices in real time to track how Liberation Day tariffs were feeding into inflation.

A lot has happened since. The BLS commissioner was fired. The longest government shutdown in US history meant CPI wasn’t published for the first time. And the case for an independent measure of inflation became much stronger.

What started as a tariff inflation tracker has since grown into something much bigger: 

The Bloomberg Price Project (BPP), our attempt to build the US CPI from the ground up using alternative data.

Today, BPP covers 87% of the CPI basket, across both goods and services (more new data will be added in coming weeks). Every month, we collect millions of prices from card transactions, e-commerce sites, grocery stores, pharmacies, rental listings, corporate data, Bloomberg Terminal market prices and government records. And more data are coming.

The payoff is detail. Official CPI data let you drill down to categories such as “uncooked beef steaks.” BPP goes much deeper — breaking the CPI basket into almost 700 line items, compared with roughly 200 in the official data.

Brought to you by: myself, Troy Durie, Daniel Ripperger-Suhler, Joshua Danial and Scott Johnson from across Bloomberg Economics.

Explore the Bloomberg Price Project at BECO MODELS BPP <GO>, or download the data at ECAN US BPI <GO>.

text:
Pearl's whole use case depends on AI servers mining while they serve models. But right now the math doesn't work...

On GPUs already owned (the realistic case, as AI providers already run their GPUs and buying cards just to mine doesn't pay), an AI server today would need to give up $1.33 to $3.15 of AI work for each coin it mines, against $0.14 to $0.23 of power for a gaming card. At ~$1.50 a pearl-2:native, few AI servers have any reason to even try.

Pearl's FP8 and surrounding upgrades could fix the economics, and therefore incentivize adoption. It lets the FP8 math mine more AI work and cuts the slowdown to about 1% to 3%, so each coin would cost $0.09 to $0.43 of lost AI work, more or less what dedicated miners spend on power per coin.

If that keeps AI servers cost competitive with dedicated miners, AI providers would have a reason to join, and competition between them could then accelerate adoption further.

For now, Pearl is still an early PoW chain and faces all the same problems. Security needs hashrate, hashrate needs a price worth mining for, and the price needs security. Bitcoin got through it on hobbyist CPUs until dedicated miners stepped in. Pearl is getting through it on gaming cards for now, until AI servers can step in to bootstrap security and therefore adoption.

text:
从年初开始就在折腾一套 Web3 打新工具，最近慢慢成型了，今天给大家介绍一下。
一直以来我都很喜欢一句话：“富在术数，不在劳身。”
打新很多时候拼的就是信息差，能不能比别人更早发现项目、捕捉到项目方的动作，往往决定了能不能抓住早期机会。但每天新项目那么多，靠人手动刷推特、盯网站、查合约，时间和精力根本不够。
所以年初我就开始陆续写一些自动化脚本，包括自动扫新项目、项目推送、监控项目方推文、网站更新、工厂合约变化等等，希望能让机器 24 小时帮我们盯着。

我同时还喜欢另一句话，叫做”众人拾柴火焰高“，之前都是零散的脚本，一直没时间整合。上个月坦克老师 @tank_btc 问我有没有项目给他写，我就把这些东西全部发给了他，让他帮忙模块化整合，同时群友们也在持续提建议，最后做成了现在这套系统。

目前已经实现了从项目发现、动态监控到 Chrome 插件实时推送的完整流程。项目刚出现就能收到信息，后续网站、推文、合约有什么变化也能及时跟踪，省去了大量重复的信息搜集工作，也能减少因为没盯盘而错过机会的情况。

另外，插件还集成了兔子备注功能，目前有 2 万多条我们自己积累的地址备注数据。以后青年大学习的兄弟们也可以通过插件一起打备注，数据库会随着大家的使用持续完善，方便大家识别地址、追踪项目关联信息。

目前社区的工具基本都是用爱发电免费开发的，写工具的初衷也不是为了赚钱，只是为了能够收获一帮真心的朋友，还是那句话，我们社区不是最有钱的社区，但绝对是最团结的社区

text:
《为什么不做低客单价的生意和低毛利生意》

就拿我们最近的事举例：前些天我们上了 Muse 的成品号，一个 8 块钱，卖了 100 多个，进账 1000 多块。结果加我的人里，差不多 30 个来找售后，说号用不了了

官方有风控，这很正常，大家也能理解。但问题总得有人解决，要么补号，要么退款

我们懒得一个个补，最后干脆全部退款，这钱不赚了

成本 4 块，卖 8 块，看着有 50% 的毛利，可一单到手就 4 块钱。再算上补号、退款、来回回消息的时间，基本白干

Plus 也一样。市面上卷到115，一单可能 5 块钱都赚不到，还不够买一瓶水，为了这 5 块钱，价格卷到这个地步，但凡正常交点税，利润直接是负的，卖一单亏一单

更离谱的是，卖得太便宜，别人反而不信你，以为你不正规。你还得花时间解释自己不是骗子。这不是自己给自己找麻烦吗？

再看高客单价是什么体验

我们合作过十几家企业客户，20x的单子，均价在 1350 到 1750 之间。我只赚我该赚的那部分

我们有个企业客户一直用1750的价格采购20x，明显有人再吃回扣，但跟我又没关系，中间赚多少，是他的本事

最近我们在卖 Claude有质保的租用，一个月 2388。客户来了一句价都没讲，直接打款

我说要三天预售，他说好，然后就安安静静等着。等我有空了，一次性搞定，交货，结束，钱就赚到了。全程没有一句废话

这就是区别。低客单价，钱少、事多、客户斤斤计较，换个便宜一块钱的就走了。高客单价，利润高、售后少、客户信任你，也尊重你的时间

差的客户怕你赚得多，好的客户怕你没利润

当然，也不是说低客单价完全不能做。刚起步的时候可以做，练手、攒客户。或者把它当引流款，前提是全自动、零交互：付款自动发货，不用你管

但只要一样东西需要你来回沟通、需要售后、需要你本人介入，那就别做低客单价了

真正的高客单价只有两条路。一条是东西本身过硬，能帮别人赚更多的钱。客户花两千块，能赚回两万，他就不会觉得贵。另一条是环境决定了它本来就贵。同样一瓶水，在家里不要钱，小卖部卖两块，景区卖八块，到了沙漠里，能换八块金条

水还是那瓶水，变的是它出现在谁面前、对方有多需要它
有需求就能赚钱，但别赚穷人的钱，那钱真的很难赚

整活还看 V 神，这身装扮其实是在致敬 AI 圈的经典神梗 Shoggoth。 在 AI 安全语境里，多眼的绿色怪物代表着“未经对齐、危险且不可解释的底层大模型”，而那张黄色笑脸，则是经过人类反馈强化学习后，勉强贴在表面用来伪装友善的面具。

Vitalik 披着这身“表面友善，底层危险”的皮囊，其实是在讲一个严肃话题：AI 时代的信任与数据监控。

配合这个诡异的造型，他在演讲中抛出了几个很有传播力的论点：

text:
SEC关于加密资产分类常见问题解答今天新增三个关键问题，很值得看看。这三个问题进一步厘清去中心化治理、网络控制权以及代币功能性之间的关系。
这次更新的核心不是重新划分代币类别，而是回答一个长期存在的监管问题：一个加密系统究竟由谁控制？如何判断它真正实现了去中心化？

尤其值得关注的是，SEC工作人员的解释为DUNA等法律实体与去中心化治理并存提供了更明确的判断思路。DUNA（去中心化非法人非营利协会）是美国怀俄明州2024年确立的一种法律组织形式，旨在让DAO等去中心化组织能够签署合同、管理资产并承担法律责任，同时保留链上社区治理。

SEC此次解释的关键在于：是否存在中心控制方，取决于实际控制权，而不是是否设立了DUNA或基金会。

这三个问题是
Question 1.4：广泛治理系统的参与者是否构成“中央方”（central party）定义下的“群体”？
Question 1.5：什么是中央方“监督参与”？
Question 1.6：“功能性”（functional）与“去中心化”（decentralized）的关系是什么？
大家可以去sec官网看对这三个问题的详细解答

对产业而言，它们为项目设计治理结构、评估是否可能落入 digital commodity（而非证券）分类、以及与监管沟通提供了更清晰的参考框架，减少对“广泛持有者投票=集中控制”的顾虑
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
监管大动作的落地，昨晚SEC发布了名为《联邦证券法对某些类型加密资产和涉及加密资产某些交易的适用性》最终解释性指引。这是SEC联合CFTC针对加密资产监管提供长期框架的明确指导，结束了过去多年“通过执法来监管”的模式，我们所期待的加密行业监管情绪度更进一步了。

指引的核心要点
1、加密资产分类，首次给出清晰的五类划分：
1）Digital Commodities数字商品
明确提出BTC、ETH、SOL、XRP、ADA、DOGE、SHIB、AVAX、LINK 等加密资产是数字商品不属于证券，价值主要来自功能性网络运行、供需。
2）Digital Collectibles数字收藏品
如NFT艺术品、meme币、CryptoPunks等不属于证券，主要具有艺术/社交/收藏价值。
3）Digital Tools数字工具
如ENS域名、实用凭证、门票等 — 不属于证券，提供实际功能。
4）Stablecoins稳定币：
符合GENIUS Act定义的“payment stablecoin”由许可发行人发行的稳定币也不属于证券；
5）Digital Securities数字证券/代币化证券代币化股票、债券等依然属于证券

2. 非证券加密资产何时变成/不再是投资合同（Howey Test应用）
1）当发行人通过承诺“essential managerial efforts”（开发功能、里程碑、使用资金等）诱导投资者合理预期利润时，非证券资产可被视为投资合同（即证券）。
2）一旦发行人履行完毕承诺，投资合同关系终止，该资产不再受证券法约束。

这是重大转变，过去SEC常认为“永远是证券”，相当于说刚开始ico或者私募时候被视为证券，但是如果代币解锁完，社区化程度高，时候也就不被视为证券了。

3. 几类常见链上活动被明确为非证券（在满足条件时）：
1）PoW挖矿，包括矿池属于非证券；
2）协议质押PoS staking（包括自 staking、托管staking、流动性质押/liquid staking）非证券，只要是按协议规则运行、非保证收益、非出借资产。
3）Staking Receipt Tokens流动性质押凭证，如stETH如果1:1对应底层非证券资产，且按协议自动反映奖励，也属于非证券。
4）Wrapping / Wrapped Tokens跨链包装，如果是1:1可赎回、无收益承诺、无资金池化 也属于非证券。
5）Airdrops空投：如果无对价（没花钱、没提供服务/商品）的情况下 — 不满足Howey的“investment of money”要件，也非证券。

做为解释性规则，这份指引立即生效。
可以说是加密监管的起重大，为大饼、以太、主流Layer1、主流staking、主流NFT、主流空投等提供了相对清晰的“非证券”地位，同时保留了对欺诈性发行和持续承诺型项目的监管空间。

text:
NVIDIA Open-Sources Auto Ontology, a Semantic Layer for AI Agents

Your boss asks the AI agent: "What was revenue last quarter?"

It answers in 3 seconds. Clean number. Nice chart.

But it used the wrong "revenue" column. 𝗡𝗼𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲𝘀.

That's the problem NVIDIA's new open-source library, Auto Ontology, goes after. Its README puts it plainly:

"…𝘢 𝘳𝘦𝘷𝘦𝘯𝘶𝘦 𝘮𝘦𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤 𝘢𝘯𝘴𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘧𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘰𝘳𝘵𝘩 𝘯𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘪𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘯𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘦𝘳 𝘪𝘴 𝘸𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨."

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗶𝘀:

A "context layer" that sits between an AI agent and your database. It tells the agent where the data lives, what each field means, and whether to use it.

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗶𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀, 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝗯𝘆 𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗽:

• 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗰𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿: it reads your database metadata and drafts an ontology, a map of business terms like "active customer"
• 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱: agents use those terms instead of guessing from raw table names
• 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲: it checks generated SQL against certified definitions
• 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲: agents reach it through MCP, a CLI or an API
• 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗻: certified corrections go back into the map

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀:

Ask a question, get 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝗤𝗟 𝗶𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗻, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀. You can check the work, not just trust it.

𝗙𝗼𝗿 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:

• Apache 2.0, runs with Docker Compose or Helm
• Works with Databricks, Postgres, Snowflake and DuckDB
• Defaults to NVIDIA's Nemotron models, but 𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗻𝗔𝗜-𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀
• The MCP server has 𝟵 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱-𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹𝘀. There is deliberately no tool to browse raw tables, so agents must go through the business terms

𝗜𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗲𝗮𝗿𝗹𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸:

• Cube and dbt MetricFlow: semantic layers you write by hand in code
• Wren AI: an open semantic layer for AI agents, with a context layer built partly by agents
• Snowflake's Semantic View Autopilot: also drafts semantic models with AI, but only for Snowflake

What's different here: 𝗼𝗽𝗲𝗻 𝘀𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗲, 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸𝘀 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲𝘀, 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗴𝗵 𝗠𝗖𝗣.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁:

• 𝗧𝗵𝗲 "𝟵𝟬% 𝗳𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗿" 𝗰𝗹𝗮𝗶𝗺 𝗶𝘀 𝗡𝗩𝗜𝗗𝗜𝗔'𝘀 𝗼𝘄𝗻 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴, with no baseline published
• 𝗡𝗼 𝗮𝗰𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗶𝘀𝗵𝗲𝗱. NVIDIA ships an eval harness (BIRD, 1,534 questions) but no results
• That harness was tested with 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗢𝗽𝘂𝘀 𝟰.𝟴, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗡𝗲𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻
• 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗛𝗮𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗖𝗼𝗿𝗽 𝗩𝗮𝘂𝗹𝘁, 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗽𝗮𝘀𝘀𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝘂𝗻𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗿𝘆𝗽𝘁𝗲𝗱 in Postgres (per the README)
• It's young: 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝟳𝟱𝟬 𝗚𝗶𝘁𝗛𝘂𝗯 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗿𝘀, and NVIDIA isn't accepting outside contributions

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁: the hard part of AI analytics isn't writing SQL. 𝗜𝘁'𝘀 𝗮𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗼𝗻 𝘄𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗱𝘀 𝗺𝗲𝗮𝗻.

text:
RLN v0.0.10 Development Updates

1. Multi-LSP Provider Connectivity

https://t.co/tfgAKAakNp

Users can connect to multiple LSP providers simultaneously, no longer being restricted to a single service provider. By connecting to different providers, users can access different RGB assets, fee structures, and channel specifications.

The system supports both channel purchases in advance (LSPS1) and Just-in-Time (JIT) channel provisioning upon receiving payments (LSPS2).

2. LSPS2 RGB JIT Channels

https://t.co/hpS8kUW35B

LSPS2 enables users without an existing channel to receive RGB assets. Users request a JIT invoice from an LSP and share it with the payer. When the payment reaches the LSP, the LSP automatically opens a channel and forwards the assets to the user. No upfront payment is required from the recipient.

- Fees: The payer settles the invoice in BTC. The LSP deducts the channel opening fee, while the remaining BTC is included as the necessary Bitcoin funding for the RGB asset transfer and forwarded to the recipient along with the assets. The amount of RGB assets received by the user remains unchanged.

- Channel Reusability: The JIT channel remains usable throughout its lease period. As long as sufficient inbound capacity remains for the asset, subsequent transfers of the same asset can use regular RGB invoices without incurring another channel opening fee.

- BTC JIT Support: LSPS2 also supports BTC JIT channels, allowing new users without existing channels to receive BTC.

3. Production-Ready Swap Improvements

Swap is now more reliable and robust in production. Key improvements have been implemented:

- Integration with Real Swap Execution Logic and Improved Persistence Reliability: The payment hash is now used as the execution_id. Actual parameters, rather than idealized values, are used to calculate CLTV, intermediary fees, and other execution parameters. Bidirectional routing paths and fee limits are also bound to the corresponding quote records. Any parameter changes require a new quote to be generated.

- Decoupling Routing Versions from Payment Attempts: Routing version numbers are now independent of payment execution attempts. An Attempt record is created only when a payment is actually initiated. Routing plans and execution attempts are persisted separately.

- Hardened Pending-State Handling: A new reconcile interface has been introduced to support verification and reconciliation of pending transactions. The system will not blindly retry a payment unless definitive evidence of its terminal state has been obtained.

Make Bitcoin Smart.

text:
2.4 million LLM calls for a single evaluation pass on financial transaction graphs? That adds up fast 💸

With AMLworld-Compact, we bring that down to 6,021.

Here's the idea:
💡 Keep every illicit test transaction.
💡 Sample benign transactions across score-based strata.
💡 Use inverse-probability weights to estimate full-test metrics.

The before → after:
• HI-Small: 1,015,669 → 3,753 targets (~271× fewer)
• LI-Small: 1,384,810 → 2,268 targets (~611× fewer)

What does that mean for your budget?

At an assumed $0.01 per request, that's roughly $24,005 → $60 for one pass across both splits.

That's an illustrative estimate: one call per target, the same average cost per call, and no setup or retries included. Actual spend depends on the model and token usage.

Code + evaluation pipeline :

text:
Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

author: immersivetran
quoted_text:
翻译工具是个很特殊的东西

你交给它的不只是文字
是你在读什么、在研究什么、在搜什么

我每天用沉浸式翻译刷Crypto Twitter、看英文财报、翻未公开的项目文档

最近又上了 X Space实时翻译
你在Space里听海外大佬聊天，工具实时处理音频、生成双语字幕

从网页文字到视频字幕到实时语音，它能接触到的内容范围越来越大
这些东西对我来说是工作素材，对一个有心的第三方来说，可能是交易信号

所以翻译工具的隐私，对我来说不是加分项，是底线。

//

@immersivetran 九月拿了两张 ISO 认证

ISO/IEC 27001:2022 ➢➢➢ 信息安全管理体系
ISO/IEC 27701:2019➢➢➢隐私信息管理体系

这两个标准是 ISO 和 IEC 联合发的，全球认可

27001是信息安全领域认知度最高的一张证
2022年更新过一版，一共 93 项控制措施，覆盖四个层面
组织管理、人员安全、物理安全、技术安全。风险评估怎么做、访问权限怎么控、数据加密走什么策略、安全事件出了怎么响应、业务中断了怎么恢复，全在审核范围内
银行、云服务商、大厂拿它当合规门槛，没这张证很多甲方的供应商名单都进不了。

27701是27001的隐私扩展，2019年才出的
直接对标 GDPR（欧盟通用数据保护条例）、CCPA（加州消费者隐私法）、PIPL（中国个人信息保护法）这一级别的隐私法规
管的东西比27001细得多

个人信息怎么收集、用于什么目的、存多久、跟谁共享、用户要求删除时怎么处理，都有具体要求
还要区分数据控制者和数据处理者，不同角色义务不同
全球拿到这张证的公司比27001少很多，隐私管理体系的落地难度更高

拿认证不是自己说了算
得请第三方审计机构进场查，流程、制度、技术控制一项项过，缺一环都拿不到

两张一起拿，在翻译工具这个品类里不常见

但让我多看一眼的不是证书
是他们讲了两件事。

//

第一件
2025年8月，沉浸式翻译的网页快照分享功能出过事。部分公开页面被搜索引擎收录，用户浏览内容有暴露风险。他们下线了功能，然后重新梳理了整套数据和隐私机制。

大多数公司碰到这种事的做法是悄悄修完假装没发生过。他们把这件事写进了ISO认证的公开说明里
这个姿态我认

第二件
他们拒绝了一家大型科技公司出高价购买用户数据

翻译工具天然能接触到海量用户信息
你读了什么、翻了什么、对什么感兴趣
一个创业公司面对这种变现机会说不，需要的不只是价值观，还有底气。

//

技术层面也交了作业
传输走HTTPS + TLS加密，内部访问最小权限，系统持续监控，有灾备和应急响应。这些是 ISO审核的硬门槛，过了说明基本线到位。

但证书是快照，不是永久保证
ISO每年复审，安全是个持续投入的事
他们自己也说了
不是毕业证，是起点

//

沉浸式翻译现在用户过3000万
用户越多，数据越敏感，隐私这条线的压力只会越来越大。

功能上我写过一篇了。这次想说的是另一半
用得爽和用得放心，是两件事

一个拿出ISO双认证、敢公开讲自己踩过的坑、面对数据变现选择不赚的团队，至少在用得放心这件事上，给出了可以验证的答案。

工具继续用
隐私这条线，继续观察

为何MRVL 用股票收购 $LITE 消息一出大跌？ 为什么LITE也大跌？目前这个收购案谈到了哪里？成功率如何？MRVL 又为什么需要 LITE?

这几天的新闻和股价大幅下跌中朋友们是不是也和我一样，有这些疑问。

事实上我最开始并不看好这笔交易，因为 $MRVL 账上现金太少，而两家的市值接近，并没有看到达成交易的合理性和可行性。

但是随着新闻不断发布，全股收购方案一出，两家股票大跌，带崩了整个光通讯板块。

1️⃣为何大跌？
全股票交易导致严重稀释：
固定换股比例是每1股LITE换4.5股MRVL。交易后现有MRVL股东持股约67%，LITE股东约33%。这相当于发行大量新股，现有股东股权被明显摊薄。 

2️⃣全股交易的连锁反应
MRVL跌，LITE换股价值就同步跌。宣布当日MRVL跌约12-13%，LITE跌约15-19%；传闻出现后MRVL已累计跌幅更大。

3️⃣规模和估值风险
这笔交易规模超过MRVL市值一半以上，是其之前收购Inphi的10倍以上。
按10月28日得股价计算，隐含LITE每股约1132美元、溢价约23.9%。估值约33倍未来12个月核心经营利润，远高于行业中位数约16倍。
再加上业务整合和市场环境的变化，这笔交易的风险和不确定性让不少人联想到2000年互联网泡沫时期全股票大并购的教训。

收购案协议已于2026年11月1日前后签署，双方董事会一致批准，正式宣布日期是11月2日。 
接下来需要完成事项：
✅双方股东大会批准、
✅美国HSR反垄断等待期结束，以及其他必要监管批准，包括中国SAMR审查被广泛视为关键变量。

text:
I didn't plan to return to X with a complaint. But then @Cbb0fe told us that if we're in crypto and not trading prediction markets on HIP-4, we're financially irresponsible. Nobody wants that, so I went and had a proper look at @HyperliquidX.

I'd genuinely love to see their prediction markets take off. Fees are an order of magnitude lower than Polymarket and Kalshi, which should be a huge draw. But traction has been slow. I have a few thoughts on how they could fix that, but the team is smart and I'm sure they know what needs to be done. I strongly suspect HIP-4 just isn't a priority after the ICE deal.

What I didn't expect was that a deeper look at Hyperliquid itself would turn up the same problems people complain about on Polymarket: unfair prioritisation of larger players, poor communication, and systems that struggle under load. I'm new here and maybe it's growing pains, but here's what I've seen so far.

Since last Friday a big share of my orders come back with "L1 is congested. Rate limited based on master account maker share." On Monday it was about a third of everything I sent. And it's not only new orders. Cancels get blocked too, so you get to watch your stale quote get picked off while the chain won't let you pull it.

The team has never actually acknowledged the issue. No incident page, no announcement, nothing. Even Polymarket puts a warning banner in its UI when the chain is congested. All we got was a reminder in Discord to batch orders. Batching shaves a little off the weight, but it doesn't change the fact that during congestion your whole allowance is pegged to 2x yesterday's maker share.

That's the part that matters. Fee tiers run on a 14-day rolling window. If you're capped by yesterday's maker share, you can't trade enough to climb a tier, so your share stays small, and your cap stays small. The biggest incumbents get the block space and everyone else gets the error message.

And the team has been silent. Maybe nobody wants bad press the week after the ICE headlines, which I understand. But locking smaller makers out of your own book is worse press than an honest post-mortem.

Acknowledge it. Publish how the congestion limit works. Give new makers a way to grow.

author: TPN_Labs
quoted_text:
Bittensor SN65 is a contest to make models smaller, and the winners just got a front door.

Each round the network names a base model and a memory ceiling. Miners send in shrunken versions that still have to clear fixed benchmark scores, and validators rerun every score themselves along with a KL divergence check (how far the small model's next-token guesses drift from the original). Numbers you can't reproduce get thrown out before ranking.

@TPN_Labs turned that output into Gratis. It reads your RAM, tells you which models fit with room to spare, downloads one, then runs offline on your own chip. Miners supply the models, the app puts them in front of people who will never open a terminal.

Most subnets stop at a Hugging Face repo and call it shipped. A file sitting in a repo is inventory. A download button is a product.

What else in the AI stack gets better once strangers are paid to beat a fixed target?

https://t.co/BX6FlgzJpc

text:
Binance Details $6.34B Hack: Fake Job Interviews Used to Plant Malware, Internal AI Tool Exploited

Binance released an initial report on its October 29 hack, revealing that attackers used fake job interviews and malware to compromise an engineer's device in September. They later exploited an internal AI tool to gain access to wallet engineers, then used stolen credentials to compromise a wallet signing service and abuse Ethereum's EIP-7702 authorization mechanism. 

Binance said withdrawal suspensions alone could not stop the malicious on-chain authorizations, which required a separate revocation process. Of the $6.34 billion in affected assets, approximately $2.85 billion has been frozen or intercepted. Binance said 98% of affected token assets had been replenished as of October 31, with sufficient funds set aside to cover all losses. The investigation remains ongoing.

text:
There's this saying back when I was doing Private Equity that

"Investment is like marriage"

That was certainly true in PE where an investment could last years and as an investor you're essentially required to support your portcos as much as you can

What's interesting is that crypto is starting to feel like marriage

Crypto used to feel like one night stand - a one and done kinda experience where you get in fast, get out fast, and then rotate onto the next trade

Now it's the other way around, "onchain businesses" are treating token holders like equity holders. And because of that, the onchain businesses are starting to be treated, valued, and priced like actual businesses. Onchain exchanges, inference platforms, yield venues, lending marketplaces 

While valuation multiples remain compressed, it's starting to make sense to value these "companies" based on their growth trajectory, based on their growth as a business and not on how hyped they can make it to be.

It feels like the bride and the groom are aligned and on the same page instead of one wanting to extract from the other as fast as possible

Pretty bullish

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
对于下周的中期选举，结果很重要但结束可能更重要。聊聊我的理解：1、现阶段概率最大的还是民主党横扫拿下参众两院；
小概率事件是共和党能保住参议院，变成分裂国会；

2、历来中期选举前市场动荡很大，过去几次中期选举皆是如此。这也是8月底在168X上https://t.co/MrasWYxXvC聊到的：中期选举前动荡加大。核心还是政治的不确定性，这个不确定性在于国会的归属会影响市场对于政策走向的判断，两院归属不确定自然也就无法对政策走向有相当明了的推演预判，自然会天然避险；

一旦结果出来了、市场就能知道后续政策大概率走向，充分反应后，选举的扰动就会褪去。

说说两个选举结果的影响
3、先说小概率的“分裂国会”情景
这种自然是大家期望的，一方面民主党掌控众议院对川普的疯癫能有一定的限制，另一方面川普对加密和AI产业的政策力度还能保持。
还能出现：
民主党控制众院 → 限制激进财政政策 → 赤字扩张放缓 → 长端利率压力下降 → 美股受益。
这种市场自然乐于见到。

4、而更大概率的“民主党横扫”情景
很多人会担心民主党掌控国会两院后对让美国对AI和加密领域的政策不仅停滞而且还会开倒车。
但有几点需要明确：
1）民主党掌控两院，政府行政权还在共和党手里，川普还是总统。很多人一说民主党掌控两院就是上台了，其实并不是。
如果民主党要废除既有法律、改变税制或推动新的大规模产业限制，通常需要两院通过新法，再交总统处理。川普可以否决。

要推翻否决，需要两院分别达到三分之二的支持。普通的国会多数，距离这个门槛很远。因此，“民主党夺两院，所以特朗普的法律自动失效”在制度上不成立。

已经成形的法案继续落地、行政权在手里，政府机构还在是共和党掌控、。

2）现在担忧很大的民主党掌控国会会让AI基建倒退
目前民主党在AI问题上有监管和征税两个方向，有民主党议员提案禁止数据中心建设和AI治理框架、但是否决权还在川普手里、这些法案都难以推进，更多是在为选后的听证和议程铺路，扰动情绪。

两党有共识的是数据中心的电网成本分摊，也是选后最有可能落地的AI相关立法。 之前众议院9月16日以417比3通过《Ratepayer Protection Act》，要求各州监管机构考虑让100兆瓦以上的大负荷用户承担其带来的全部发电和电网升级增量成本，但并不强制各州采用。
其实共和党对这方面也提出了这些要求。

但有一点，民主党应该也清楚在AI这场国家军备竞赛的意义和重要性，他们也很难说开倒车。更多的是纠偏、之前共和党的很多政策过激过度、控制步子迈得幅度、但并不是说就止步不前甚至落后，民主党也接受不了美国在AI上落后的代价。

3）再说加密
其实9月中清晰法案受阻、个人角度其实已经不指望未来两件有国会层面的加密立法，而是更看重sec和cftc在各自行政权限范围内给到了最大的政策范围。

之前这里https://t.co/xBS30IWyFe有聊过，构建行政版清晰框架。其实也够用了，未来两年SEC和CFTC主席都是川普提名的共和党人。

4）民主党横扫掌控两院能做到什么？
民主党夺取众院，已经能够限制相当一部分新增立法；
再拿下参院，新增的关键影响是人事确认、参院委员会议程，以及更强的监督与谈判能力。
能限制很大程度上限制共和党的新立法能力和进程，对很多政策和人发起国会调查和听证，但也限于此毕竟司法部未来来两年还在川普手里。

所以总的来说：
中期选举结束比结果可能更重要些，选举结束无论结果如何市场都能根据新的国会权力格局来做推演未来政策可能性、新的边界和程度会如何？而现在这些都悬在空中。

前天这里https://t.co/HK9K8cStzD也聊到，中午选举应该是一个关键的时间节点、之后很多方面会清晰明确起来。

quoted_text:
【讨个请教】各位 Agent 大神是怎么管理如此多的 Session x Agent 对话的消息的？

我现在同时会有多个Session x Antigravity/Claude Code/Codex。

为了知道每个任务进度，我目前采用的是飞书消息，设定了全局的规则当某个 Session 完成的时候，给我发消息。

但目前我有两个痛点：
1. 飞书消息并不能很的回溯到对应 Agent的Session（指直接跳转），也不能标记任务状态
2. 当有多个Session同时完成时，我像个指针在遍历分时多任务。

2026年底了，有没有一些优雅的方案，我希望本地有一个类似 Grok Bot 的主 Bot 帮我管理对话、进度和派发的产品（但不是Grok Bot），我不想像一个指针在一直遍历各个对话。

author: HyperliquidR
quoted_text:
The US route to Hyperliquid just got more concrete.

Hyperliquid confirms Payward's plan to be the first CFTC-regulated deployer on HIP-3*, an optional deployer allowlist. Bitnomial (DCM and DCO) would deploy and clear the markets, NinjaTrader Clearing (FCM) would carry US accounts, and Hyperliquid's onchain OB would do the matching, without Hyperliquid itself having to register.

What's still open before the first listing:
• HIP-3* on mainnet
• Bitnomial listing the contracts, by self-certification or CFTC approval (“subject to regulatory approval”)
• How clearing splits between HyperCore, which already margins and liquidates positions in code, and Bitnomial, the registered clearinghouse?
• Which markets can go live: crypto, gold, silver and US equity index perpetual futures already trade in the US, but single-stock perpetuals aren't live yet

With CFTC Chair Selig working to bring Hyperliquid onshore, I'd argue they'll find a way to bring Hyperliquid home.

Permissionless HIP-3 stays unchanged. Payward is first, and if it's approved, I don't expect it to be the last.

Hyperliquid.

text: World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.
author: justinsuntron
quoted_text:
Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

author: dapangdun
quoted_text:
RLN v0.0.10 Development Updates

1. Multi-LSP Provider Connectivity

https://t.co/tfgAKAakNp

Users can connect to multiple LSP providers simultaneously, no longer being restricted to a single service provider. By connecting to different providers, users can access different RGB assets, fee structures, and channel specifications.

The system supports both channel purchases in advance (LSPS1) and Just-in-Time (JIT) channel provisioning upon receiving payments (LSPS2).

2. LSPS2 RGB JIT Channels

https://t.co/hpS8kUW35B

LSPS2 enables users without an existing channel to receive RGB assets. Users request a JIT invoice from an LSP and share it with the payer. When the payment reaches the LSP, the LSP automatically opens a channel and forwards the assets to the user. No upfront payment is required from the recipient.

- Fees: The payer settles the invoice in BTC. The LSP deducts the channel opening fee, while the remaining BTC is included as the necessary Bitcoin funding for the RGB asset transfer and forwarded to the recipient along with the assets. The amount of RGB assets received by the user remains unchanged.

- Channel Reusability: The JIT channel remains usable throughout its lease period. As long as sufficient inbound capacity remains for the asset, subsequent transfers of the same asset can use regular RGB invoices without incurring another channel opening fee.

- BTC JIT Support: LSPS2 also supports BTC JIT channels, allowing new users without existing channels to receive BTC.

3. Production-Ready Swap Improvements

Swap is now more reliable and robust in production. Key improvements have been implemented:

- Integration with Real Swap Execution Logic and Improved Persistence Reliability: The payment hash is now used as the execution_id. Actual parameters, rather than idealized values, are used to calculate CLTV, intermediary fees, and other execution parameters. Bidirectional routing paths and fee limits are also bound to the corresponding quote records. Any parameter changes require a new quote to be generated.

- Decoupling Routing Versions from Payment Attempts: Routing version numbers are now independent of payment execution attempts. An Attempt record is created only when a payment is actually initiated. Routing plans and execution attempts are persisted separately.

- Hardened Pending-State Handling: A new reconcile interface has been introduced to support verification and reconciliation of pending transactions. The system will not blindly retry a payment unless definitive evidence of its terminal state has been obtained.

Make Bitcoin Smart.

从投资的视角来看上币是很简单的逻辑：币安需要什么类型的项目提供就好了，抓住交易所最大的需求。

就比如说大家诟病的hook这些，是币安在22年通过Stepn获取了大量用户，尝到了通过山寨币拉新的甜头，那么找/攒同类型的项目一定比其他类型的项目更容易上。包括后面Layer2的Strk，Ton生态的Cati，Sol生态的Jto都是同样的道理，顺势而为罢了。只是有些生态被证伪，跌的比较惨，后来山寨币整体被证伪，那就一起死了。

Mobile money and bank rails still don't always speak the same language.
A farmer may be paid into a mobile wallet, a supplier into a bank account, and an agent from either. Each rail has its own formats, references and confirmation messages, so a payment that feels simple to the customer can be complicated underneath.
Making a payment network agnostic means it does not matter which rail the money travels on. The reference stays the same, the invoice is matched in the same way, and the institution sees one clear record instead of several that have to be reconciled by hand.
In this short video, we explain what interoperability really takes, beyond simply connecting two systems.

text:
Interesting.

Revolut reportedly only started seeing meaningful AI productivity gains after moving away from expensive OpenAI and Anthropic models to self-hosted GLM.

Decagon reportedly runs ~90% of its workloads on open weight models.

Why? Because when you're running AI agents in production for e.g. customer service, cost and latency matter enormously. You don't need a frontier model with PhD-level reasoning or even a model that knows the capital of Finland to handle every customer interaction.

We're seeing similar dynamics across hypergrowth AI startups and increasingly the large enterprises we work with.

But most importantly, the future isn't binary.

When use cases are new, you want the smartest general-purpose model available. But once workflows mature and become predictable, smaller, faster, specialized models increasingly win.

I wouldn't be surprised if 80–90% of routine enterprise AI workflows eventually run on open-weight and smaller models.

This doesn't mean frontier labs lose. 

It means the market is splitting into two massive opportunities: frontier intelligence and specialized execution at scale.

text:
When I traded FX, you didn’t ask when the market was open. It was always open somewhere. Sydney handed to Tokyo, Tokyo to London, London to New York, and the price kept moving with the news. That's what a market looks like when demand is global and no single exchange owns it.

US stocks are now heading down the same road. Half of the volume in the most traded US stock perps now happens when the Nasdaq is closed.

Demand for US stocks has been global for a long time, but access wasn't. If you live in Seoul, Lagos or Buenos Aires, the session that matters runs through your night, and reaching it means a local broker, a wrapper and a lot of friction. Perps removed that friction. They're open around the clock, available anywhere, and work for any asset with a price. That's the job the ETF did for the last generation of investors, and it's why global demand went there first.

Once access goes 24/7, price discovery follows. News doesn't wait for the open, earnings land after the close, and the first reaction now prints on whatever venue is open. The home exchange is still the deepest market, and the open is still the busiest hour of the day. It's just no longer the only place a stock's price gets formed, and that won't reverse.

That changes the questions that matter. When the same stock has a live price on several venues at 2am, which one do you mark to, settle on, or lend against? The market data stack was built for one venue and one closing price. It now has to work for many.

"My IP is in danger and I'm getting no value."

When customers come to our sovereign boot camps, I often hear: “What I just heard is completely opposite of what I thought Palantir is and stands for. This is amazing.”

I can’t stress enough how many times I have this exact conversation with customers. They see a parallel to how the software industrial complex has screwed them over for the last 30 years.

They spend $10-100s of millions of dollars to buy and implement software, yet see no net value increase, even as everyone says they need it to run their business. Then the software worsens, prices rise, and they are left with technical debt. Now it’s outdated, and they must spend boatloads of money to upgrade as it reaches EOL.

This story is as old as the software industry.

Everyone sees models and model companies behaving as the latest incarnation of this. They spend time and money to “be more productive” because everyone is doing it and they don’t want to be left behind. At the risk of their IP, they implement AI models but see no bottom-line improvement, while being told they just haven’t done it right yet.

In reality, their dollars and IP are migrating to Silicon Valley, and they are waking up to this.

At Palantir, we provide IP protection AND better models than frontier labs that you own. I would argue that Sovereignty goes much further than just model weights. You need to look at Sovereignty at all layers of your software and business stack. That is what we are doing: holistically helping customers own their sovereignty across the whole stack.

The speed that we are doing this is like nothing I have ever seen.  We started this in June 4th when we posted a full-page ad in the WSJ that just said “Protect your sovereignty”. text:
Josh Gruenstein of Tutor Intelligence says the machine-run factory most people picture is just the top .01%, and humans still box almost everything you buy:

"Most people have this mental picture of what the industrial base or manufacturing logistics looks like in the United States... You see these Rube Goldbergian machines of levers, and you don't see any humans in those pictures, right?"

"That's the top .01% of American manufacturing logistics. What's below that? You walk into these million square foot facilities and you see a bunch of people standing around on conveyor belts or folding tables doing things by hand."

"It's kind of shocking for anybody who doesn't come from this industry and community."

"A huge amount of work, which is back-breaking work that's really hard to hire for. There's a three-month turnover where your average age of the worker doing that work is 55 years old and about to retire."

"Basically anything you ever bought that came in a box, a human had to put that in a box, which is a crazy revelation for most people... Even iPhones, you would assume it's a robot putting that packaging together. No, it's a person even at the highest level of scale."

@joshgruenstein @tutorintel

text:
Huge congrats to Succinct’s Rahul Dalal, one of the cryptographers behind FlashProve, @AnthropicAI’s provable inference system built on zkSNARKs.

Why: Today, AI runs on a “just trust me” model. Users can’t verify that a response came from the model they chose, or that an attacker didn’t tamper with it along the way. As AI takes on higher-stakes work, that create tension for users, labs, and regulators alike.

What: Researchers from Anthropic, EPFL, MIT, and @SuccinctLabs built FlashProve, a system that lets a model provider commit to a specific model and then prove each response was produced by it, without revealing the weights. Under the hood, it uses zkSNARKs, the same cryptographic technology Succinct uses to secure $13.5B in deposits on Ethereum L2s.

So What: FlashProve proved Llama 4 Maverick, a 400B-parameter LLM, at 110 tokens/sec on a single H100 GPU, with ~19 MB proofs. That puts proving at roughly 70 to 95x the cost of running the model. The previous standard for the same model was ~0.02 tokens/sec.

What’s Next: FlashProve is still a research prototype, but it’s a step change toward the question we asked with Flock earlier this year: how close can proving get to computing? The closer it gets, the less reason there is to release any output without a proof attached.

Congrats again to Rahul and the FlashProve team, and great to see @Starknet, @Mantle_Official (proven by Succinct), and several zkML projects cited.

The @CFTC has approved equity perp contracts for the 4 exchanges that have filed requests to approve them:

- KalshiEX LLC
- Coinbase Derivatives
- Bitnomial (Kraken)
- Nadex/OG.com 

All 4 of these exchanges are:
1. CFTC registered exchanges
2. DCMs that clear trades with registered DCOs
3. Also registered with the SEC
4. That previously filed requests for approval of equity-perp contracts. 

The 4 exchanges have internal standards (which they've formalized and filed with the CFTC) for which equity-perp they can list on their own exchange. 

Things like 
- Equity is publicly traded
- Sufficient float, trading volume
- Reliable pricing to be able to calc funding payments
- Market structure resilient to manipulation

text:
Crypto KOL marketing isn't dead.

It's just grossly misunderstood and 90% of companies do it horribly. As someone that's worked in this exact arena, both as a marketer and a creator, let me explain.

First, what is a KOL?
Well it stands for 'key opinion leader' but that's bullshit.

Basically, it's a fancy word for crypto native influencer. These influencers are typically micro, and 90% of them do nothing onchain.

10% do though, and they are by far the best ones.
What about the other 90%? Are they useless? 
Most of the time, but not always.

To understand it, you need to understand your product and who you are delivering to.

Who is your ideal customer?
What phase is your business in?
How will an influencer campaign get you there?

If the goal is distribution with a lot of shares, you're already fumbling.

Why?

It's not targeted, and crypto is a very wide sector. 

So, if you're starting from 0, here's what you do.

Find 1 creator you like, that creates posts similar to your business.

Then, with that same account profile, find 10 more accounts like them.

It can't just be the biggest folks in the world, or folks with a lot of engagement, or folks with a ton of brand deals. All that can be faked, and the more deals someone has the more diluted their engagement is.

You wouldn't hire an employee without doing some research, so look at who's engaging with them. The quality of it. If it looks like a bot network or actual influence.

Now, you've got your creators.
You need to have a good product, a defined messaging, and a way to hook the users once you get the mindshare.

It's not the creators fault your product fucking sucks or the campaign brief you gave them wasn't great. It's yours.

But let's say that goes well, and now you have a product in market with a solid user base. What now?

This is what we call our 1-100 marketing.
And you do that anywhere but CT. 

You already have mindshare here, and you can't just keep throwing budget. It will diminish mindshare.

Go on traditional channels. Do traditional ads. Do founder led marketing. Anything but here.

Once you go to 100, come back to CT. 
You have more budget. Sexier metrics. And can go from 100 -> 1000 way easier.
