quoted_text:
Long post worth the read. I have a close friend who flies private jets. He flew Lear 60 for over 15 years and now flies a Gulfstream. This is a copy and paste of his response to me asking him if he thought Ice was the issue. 

“We always fly in ridiculous cold temperatures.” 

“Usually you get the bad ice when the temperatures are like 0 to negative 20.  Believe it or not,  there's a point where it gets too cold for ice.   At negative 40, you pretty much can't get ice.   Besides that,  the airplane is equipped with hot wings and hot tail.”

“I flew the Lear 60 for like 15 years.   It's a no joke airplane and probably the most dangerous airplane I've ever flown.   It has a super critical wing.   The airflow has to be perfect.   When it gets into rough air and turbulence,  it will easily stall.   It has stalled on me at 41,000 feet just because we got into some turbulence.   (On the way to Palm Beach as a matter of fact. ) we recovered and got her flying again around 30,000 ft.   Scary

But here's the problem.   This airplane has a terrible coffin corner.   (At high altitudes)  what that means is,  you fly in a really narrow window where if you lose 20 knots,  it stalls.   And if you gain 20 knots,  it goes into overspeed.   The air goes supersonic over the wing and it goes into a high speed stall,  or worse,  a Mach tuck.   

So if you stall,  the normal recovery is to push the yoke forward to lower the nose and gain air speed again.   At low altitude,  you can push really hard and recover quickly.   But in the 60... if you push hard,  it will gain air speed and go into a high speed stall,  it doesn't take much.   It's very sensitive.  The 60 has super short wings that don't make much lift.   So then you high speed stall,  and the computer is yelling at you... OVERSPEED!   So then you pull back and enter a low speed stall.   And you go back and forth trying to keep it in the air speed window.   

This whole thing is pretty scary.   And you should recover basically by using your finger tips using super small corrections.   You can't over do it.   If you try to muscle the recovery, she gets mad and will become unrecoverable.  If she enters a mach tuck.  You're done.”

“I taught the Lear 60 to other pilots and mentored them.   I told them... this airplane has a soul and it's trying to kill you.   Do not ever try to top the weather.   Don't go over a thunderstorm.   Go around it.   If it means a half hour longer,  then do it.   Going over the thunderstorm will go into turbulence that you might not recover from.   

These pilots went right over a thunderstorm.   I think it stalled which caused them to drop down into the thunderstorm and ended up in mach tuck.   They picked up so much speed that it ripped off the horizontal stabilizer.   At that point... chuck Yeager can't fix it.   

These same pilots did something similar a couple months ago.   ATC got mad at them.   They poked the bear one too many times.   

This is not a beginner airplane.   The Gulfstream would never do this.   It has HUGE margins of error and won't stall like that.   But then again... it's got HUGE wings.   It's a pussy cat.  

The Gulfstream is like driving a 4 wheeler.   The Lear 60 is like riding a uni cycle.”

text:
Really happy to see the response to the Darkbloom update :)

A few people asked: “Won’t the new sandbox providers just undercut you?”

The simple answer: we’re giving your agents a Mac.

We aren’t stopping at 2-4 vCPUs. We want to offer 8, 16 or 32 physical CPU cores, plus Apple GPUs, for agents doing research and complex work.

Unlike inference alone, these workloads can put much more of the machine to use. We think there’s a real opportunity to compete on both price and performance here.

My bet is that the work we give agents will keep getting more compute-intensive. Bigger builds, more experiments, simulations, video editing, rendering. There’s a lot beyond running a few commands and managing your calendar in a terminal.

Think about an agent working in Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro, or using open-source creative tools. It needs access to the software, the environment and enough compute to actually do the work.

That’s what gets me excited about this. I want to see what agents can do when we give them a powerful Mac to work with.

That’s what we’re building towards with Darkbloom Sandboxes.

Cheers to the GOAT who made these chips! ❤️
author: twid
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
so I fundamentally disagree with this take. 

it's important we discuss it in light of the Brazil election being mispriced, and potentially some big prediction market misses today in the midterms (we will see). 

first of all, can a prediction market be wrong? yes. a PM can be mispriced relative to the "true" probability. 

was the 80c price for Bolso ahead of the election "wrong"? yes. the polls showed a dead heat. the market on the PM was showing tons of conviction the wrong way around. 80 cents was wrong. 

saying "20c odds happen one in five times so 20c was not wrong" is unfalsifiable. a PM can never be mispriced according to that logic. 

second, electoral PMs are not the same as dice rolls or other sources of "genuine" randomness. 

elections are uncertain in the epistemic sense - it's hard to gather all the data beforehand and price them. this is not the same kind of uncertainty you get from rolling a fair die. unlike the die, there is always some kind of inherent underlying political reality to be discovered. 

the "true probability" of an election given perfect knowledge is going to be 100/0 one way. of course, no one has perfect knowledge, which is in theory the value prop of PMs; giving sharps the financial incentive to go out there and discover that knowledge and furnish it in the form of prices. 

it's not reasonable to say "underdogs sometimes win, so a 20c probability that happens is automatically valid". you could use that to justify any nonzero probability even down to 0.1c. 

elections are not card draws or dice rolls. they are events that condense political realities into a single number. PMs are meant to pay people to discover that number. the PM in the case of Brazil (and maybe the midterms – who knows) failed to do this. so the PM was "wrong", in the sense that it wasn't useful. in fact, it was was actively worse than what the polls were suggesting. that makes it wrong.

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

text:
A job description can make one role sound like five different jobs.

You might see a Web3 marketing position asking for content creation, community management, analytics, partnerships, event coordination and even basic design skills.

But that doesn't necessarily mean you'll be doing all six every day.

Some responsibilities are central to the role. Others come up occasionally, relate to future projects or describe skills the company would ideally like the candidate to have.

The challenge is that job descriptions don't always make those distinctions clear.

Before ruling yourself out because you don't meet every requirement, look at which responsibilities are emphasized, which skills are marked as essential and what the company expects you to own.

And if you reach the interview stage, ask what the person in this role will actually spend most of their time doing.

The goal isn't just to find out whether you're qualified. It's to understand the job you're applying for.

quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
拆开说一下 arcus 和 lighter 无损对冲的一轮大概的完整对冲流程吧（全程必须 WS）：

1、 开仓：Arcus 只挂 maker 单 → 手续费 0
2、 一成交，Lighter 立刻用 IOC 吃单对冲 → 手续费 0（Standard 账户）
3、 平仓：Arcus 继续挂单平 → 0；Lighter 吃单对冲 → 0
4、 只有止损时，Arcus 用市价单平仓 → 收 1.8bp（止损可先不看）

手续费是 0，那磨损花在哪？我把实测的数据一次对冲按时间串起来看：

📍 一次对冲的时间线（以 Arcus 挂单被吃的那一刻为第 0 毫秒）可看下图
① 第 0 毫秒：Arcus 挂单被吃，我们收到成交推送
② 第 8 毫秒：程序发出 Lighter 对冲单
③ 第 40–150 毫秒：Lighter 收到这张单
④ 第 300–400 毫秒：Lighter 真正成交，成交价在这一刻定下来（所以我们耗时在 50-100ms 之内但又限制于 lighter 的 300ms）
⑤ 第 600 毫秒：程序查询到"已成交"（价格早在第 ④ 步就定了，晚看到不影响价格）

隐性成本就落在这条时间线上：
🟢 点差（撮合时付）：SPY 约 0.3–0.5bp（不固定），每次付一半左右
🟡 盘口深度（撮合时付）：单轮 0.5 万约 0.16–0.4bp，1 万约 0.24–0.67bp，规模越大越贵（印证为什么我上仓位后磨损一下就大了起来）
🔴 那 300ms 里的价格移动（从发单到撮合）：平静夜里 0–0.3bp，行情一动就是 1–2bp，个股可达 3–9bp
🔴 分笔成交排队（约 10% 的单）：Arcus 挂单分几笔成交时，后一张对冲单要等前一张确认，多晚 340–750ms 才发出，这段时间仓位没有对冲

为什么偏偏是那 300ms（lighter 标准账户固定延迟） 最贵？因为挂单被吃的那一刻，价格往往正在动。有人吃我们的单，多半是因为他看到价格要变了；我们晚 300ms 才在 Lighter 成交，价格已经跟着走了一段。

结论：真正的成本不是手续费，也不是程序慢，而是"被吃的时机 + 交易所的 300ms 固定延迟"。这 300ms 我们降不了（Premium 能降到 200ms，但吃单费 2.8bp，比省下的还贵），能优化的只有分笔成交时的排队时间。

所以我们只在夜间加成时段做 SPY 这种波动小的标的，个股先不碰。另外，Arcus 高等级的 maker 费率是负的（返佣 0.2–0.3bp），量做上去以后，挂单反而能挣钱，其实写到这里我反而有了另外一个想法。。。这里应该小伙伴们都懂吧？！

近期说下我的 Arcus 与 Lighter 对冲的状况，其实已经能做到无损刷了，但交易量很低

策略：SPY 在 Arcus 挂单、成交后立刻在 Lighter 吃单对冲，赚两边基差回归，只在积分加成时段开仓。目前只保留了价差挂单，停止了资金费率持仓模式。目前主要磨损是"挂单被吃之后的那 几百毫秒"（这个还是和延迟有关）

针对性改了三处：
1、 只在加成时段开仓：常规时段的量几乎不计分，磨损却是加成时段的 3 倍
2、 基差锚从 10 分钟中位改成 2 小时中位：减少持仓期间的漂移
3、 回本出场：满持仍亏时不再认亏，等回本 80% 再平，最长等 4 小时

改版后 5 轮（还在积累样本）：
🟢 单轮 0.5 万：3 轮，赚 3.3U/10万，对冲滑点 0–0.66bp

🟡 单轮 1 万：2 轮，亏 7.5U/10万（盘口深度成本 + 当晚波动，锚也没攒满，干扰较多）

合计：7 万成交，磨损 2.9U/10万，自从换了单轮两侧 1 万的交易，磨损一下就上来，不过这个不能说明问题，需要持续观察。

目前尴尬点就是：你要走量模式就必然有磨损，如果你要 0 磨损刷量，那就需要时间，鱼和熊掌不可兼得。

text:
AirBnB just started  offering weather Prediction Markets to it's users.

Users can hedge bad weather at their destination by betting on rain levels.

this is a trillion dollar usecase.

here is how it works:

- users choose to pay a small "insurance fee" (stake) when booking
- payout is determined automatically based on the odds of rain
- If it rains, payout is automatically credited to their account

No claim, No verification, 100% automated.

Essentially, this is a prediction market bet disguised as insurance.

This is called a "Parametric insurance".

And it's what will take prediction markets from the $600B gambling industry to the $8T insurance industry.

Right now AirBnB is settling the bet through Chubb, a legacy insurance company, but they explicitly do NOT disclose their oracle anywhere.

I wouldn't be surprised if they were already using @Kalshi behind the scenes.

It would be incredibly easy for them to use Kalshi to :
- receive accurate weather odds
- handle market resolution
- even settle payouts

All the insurer would do is charge a premium over the odds and collect the difference.

If this usecase takes on, @Kalshi & @Polymarket could become the backbone of a trillion dollars industry.

🟡 单轮 1 万：2 轮，亏 7.5U/10万（盘口深度成本 + 当晚波动，锚也没攒满，干扰较多）

合计：7 万成交，磨损 2.9U/10万，自从换了单轮两侧 1 万的交易，磨损一下就上来，不过这个不能说明问题，需要持续观察。

目前尴尬点就是：你要走量模式就必然有磨损，如果你要 0 磨损刷量，那就需要时间，鱼和熊掌不可兼得。
author: mycndota
quoted_text:
Arcus 出分了，上周 Arcus 积分 25.64 分，总共刷了 72.3 万，成本比较混杂，有 BUG 造成、新旧引擎的切换。

现在环境越拉越不好搞了，var 之后我估计越来越难，所以从上周开始我就研究套利、费率套利 或 超低磨损来刷 perps，重写了整套框架，目前第一目标终于达成，目前是两个策略并行：价差套利（盈利/低磨损刷）+费率套利模式（盈利/无损模式刷）

1、 价差套利：磨损终于完成第一目标（最初目标是 4U/10W，目前达到了 3U/10W，如果套利就交易太少，所以放开 些门槛）

策略：Arcus 挂单 + Lighter 吃单对冲。思路重写成 WS 驱动：挂单价按 Lighter 实时价锚定，成交推送一到就立刻对冲。

执行层：
🟢 发现成交到发出对冲单约 7ms，Lighter 成交约 0.6 秒（其中 300ms 是 Standard 账户的固定延迟）
🟢 正常轮次每轮 +0.39 ~ +0.77bp
🟡 对冲平均滑点约 0.9bp，行情冲刺时会到 2–3bp
🔴 带仓跨过美股开盘，一轮亏 5.3bp，已改为开盘前 1 小时不开新仓

标的的影响最大：
🟢 SPY：Lighter 点差约 0.5bp
🟡 NVDA / QQQ：Lighter 点差 0.9–1.1bp，磨损明显更高
🔴 加密币：Arcus 挂单费 1.5bp（前两天刚刚涨的），一轮光手续费就 3bp，直接排除

结论：延迟已经不是瓶颈，剩下的是被挑单和标的选择。问题是量太低，约 90% 的时间在空仓等机会，所以降低了一些门禁。

1️⃣ 双向报价：基差偏高、偏低两侧都挂单
2️⃣ 加大单轮名义额（Lighter 盘口深度够，吃单成本 +0.1–0.2bp）
3️⃣ 动量回避：Lighter 2 秒内单边变动 ≥1bp 就撤单

📉 预估：磨损守在 3U/10万，量放大 3–5 倍（能盈利但成交太低，所以先低磨跑跑看）。还在积累样本。

---

2、 资金费模式：Arcus 个股的资金费普遍比 Lighter 高 7–10%

策略：空 Arcus、多 Lighter，对冲持有，按小时收两边的资金费差，不靠价差赚钱。

7 天数据（年化，Arcus 减 Lighter，每小时对齐）：
🟢 AMZN 8.9%（95% 的小时为正，流动性最好）
🟢 COIN 9.6% / GOOGL 7.5% / META 7.1%
🟡 AMD / SNDK：7 天均值 9–11%，但正费差小时只有约 68%，不稳定
🔴 SPY / QQQ / NVDA：约 0 甚至为负，这类标的不适合做资金费（这个就适合刷量模式）

实收和预期有差距：AMZN 建仓后头 5 小时，Arcus 收入 > Lighter 支出，但净差只有年化约 0.9%，正好碰上费率低谷。资金费按小时波动，只看某一小时会误判，所以选品看 7 天、72 小时、24 小时三个窗口里最低的那个。

选品规则：
1️⃣ 得分 = 三个窗口里最低的费差，奖励稳定
2️⃣ 过滤：正费差小时 ≥75%、Lighter 日成交 ≥ $5M、3 天内有财报的排除
3️⃣ 换仓：新标的连续 2 天比现有高 3% 以上（年化）才换，换一次约 2–4bp

📉 预估：费差回到均值时年化约 8%，按名义额计。实收要看接下来几天，这个是实打实的盈利，如果想多刷量也能做到无损模式。

跑几天后再发实测数据。

text: Clanker: Reboot.
author: LamIsRealGoat
quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
Enjoyed talking with @RektHQ for this one. None of October's key incidents broke any cryptography. Keys were generated badly, stored badly, or decrypted by someone who shouldn't have had access.

That's the real risk for crypto. If a valid signature is all it takes to spend, a Web2 breach becomes an onchain loss.

So at @NewtonLabs we split signing from authorization. Our Safe demo publishes the owner key, and it still can't move funds without a one-time code tied to the recipient and amount.

Rekt's fair pushback is that this moves trust rather than removing it. True. So the next questions are who writes the policy, who can change it, and how much any one role controls.
author: NewtonLabs
quoted_text:
Real exploits. Stolen secrets. AI claims bigger than the public proof. October’s security failures were serious, but they did not establish an internet-wide collapse. For crypto, the harder question is what stops a transfer once an attacker has the key.

quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

text:
Thoughts from my Shanghai field trip

Sentiment among Greater China investors was far worse than I expected. Unlike the US market, A shares had not seen a single rebound since July. Still holding Chinese and Hong Kong AI stocks that had crashed and Korean memory stocks that had collapsed, investors kept pressing me on when memory would bounce back.

Many investors said the AI trade was over, and a few said they doubted whether even 2027 capex, not just 2028, would go ahead as planned.

Overall, the bearish sentiment was so strong that even I, a bull before coming to China, started to waver.

It got to the point where, faced with the bear case that memory prices could start falling in the third quarter of next year, I took it seriously and couldn't refute it.

As the conversations went on, I gradually began to understand where their pessimism was coming from. In the end, they were all asking the same question.

So what comes after AI coding? What will be the next engine of ARR for Anthropic and OpenAI?

Several candidates came up. AI4S, AI chip design, and so on... But none of them clearly convinced investors.

I couldn't offer a clear answer either. Sure, there are rumors that Anthropic has made major breakthroughs in both AI4S and AI chip design, but what we actually want to know is when any of that turns into money.

With AI4S, there could be beneficiaries right away, such as companies that sell lab monkeys or diagnostic kits. In fact, there already are. But while we can trade those names in the short term, what we ultimately want to know is whether Anthropic can make money by developing drugs. That is still several years away.

As for AI chip design, the TAM itself is hard to calculate, and even if you do calculate it, it is hard to monetize. That makes it difficult for the market to believe in.

Honestly, this feels like the hardest market in history. If a company isn't making money, selling makes sense. But right now the market sells even when companies are making money, even when they beat, and even when they say demand will stay solid all the way through 2028 and 2029.

So my recommendation to investors was to buy memory, and within memory, DRAM. Not because I have conviction in the DRAM cycle, but because I see it as a relatively defensive choice within the AI trade.

Memory stocks are now trading close to 1x P/B on 2027 BPS. Historically, memory stocks have staged technical rebounds when they fell below 1x P/B.

And even if the broader market falls further from here, the three DRAM makers will keep buying back their own shares. I thought that would guarantee a certain level of buying and concluded the stocks would have downside support.

Of course, I don't know whether memory stocks can break above their previous highs. That depends on whether sentiment across the broader market recovers. But I think there is a fairly good chance that memory outperforms the rest of the AI trade.

text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
.@BillAckman on Squawk Box: the market is back in casino mode. The margin limits put in place after the Great Depression, when investors could borrow 95% to buy stocks, have been quietly gutted by total return swaps and derivatives. One soft quarterly guide can knock 30% off a stock, only for it to grind back over the following weeks.

Much of today's volatility is mechanical, not fundamental. Short-term leverage forces the selling. Patient capital collects the discount. Ackman points to Pershing's buys of $MSFT on the capex and SaaSpocalypse scare, $AMZN, $META after its big capex announcement, and $GOOGL after the ChatGPT launch as the trade. That is a direct challenge to pod shops and levered swap books, and an open invitation for long-only money to buy their forced selling.

"We've basically eviscerated those rules with some version of total return swaps, derivatives. And we're back to the casino type markets when there was 95% leverage."

text:
我的体感是岗位少，真正的求职者也很少。

昨天客串了一下公司的 HR，简单聊了 5 个小朋友，只有 1 个是我比较满意的，已经约了再聊一次。

给到的是一个比较基础的内容运营岗，图文 + 视频，在 AI 工具的加持下，其实算是一份比较简单的工作。

首先是简历。大家给到的简历其实都写得太满了，在给到工作职责后，需要我去找哪些经历和技能是满足要求的，观感其实很不好。比较建议各位准备一份基础简历，然后根据工作职责去做筛选和填充，至少面试邀约率可以提高很多。

其次是关于面试是否需要露脸。我其实不是特别在意，一来大多数人还是会在简历上贴照片，二来也不是一个需要看脸的岗位。但是在一些人开了视频、一些人没有开视频的情况下，就会有对比。这个我觉得也不是强制性的，只是给到了一个准备角度吧。

再者就是面试前的准备工作。给到的薪资是完全匹配工作职责的，但是整体的过程中能看出大多数还是比较不重视的，比如没有提前了解项目，没有提前给到一些案例或者作品集，没有准备想了解的问题，感觉我说的比他们说的还多。其实好几个都是 2 min 就可以结束的面试，硬生生带着走了 10 min，为了不尴尬。

据我了解，大多数人在 web3 都是身兼数职，我自己是也不排斥的，只要可以按时定量交付工作，没人会来找你茬儿的，除非工作之间有互斥性或者提前说明不能兼职的，还是希望大家在有面试机会的时候认真对待吧。

最后就是对这个岗位有兴趣的可以找我了解一下哦。

text:
The $6.4B Binance theft by North Korean actors began with a fake job interview, per Binance's initial findings.

We have attributed more than $14.3M in losses over the past 18 months to similar DPRK-linked faked interview and malware schemes.

These schemes have spanned a wide range of targets, from individual crypto holders and private wallets to organizations, protocols, and DAOs.

Our analysis suggests these earlier compromises allowed North Korean actors to refine their methods on small targets before deploying them against higher-value targets.

Per Binance, attackers spent weeks building trust with an employee, first approaching the employee through a legitimate job platform with a fake job opportunity.

After two rounds of interviews with a fictitious company, the Binance employee was asked to download an interview assignment that contained malicious code. 

From there, they deployed malware and exploited access to an internal AI tool to move deeper into Binance's system.

We have observed multiple similar cases in which victims had wallet private keys stolen from cloud storage following a malicious interview.

Our research also indicates that North Korean actors have used fake employment schemes for other cyber attacks. 

For instance, they have used such schemes to conceal malware in public blockchains. We’ve found a fivefold surge in these blockchain-assisted cyberattacks over the past year

The same actors can exploit recruitment platforms, compromise corporate infrastructure, infiltrate legitimate businesses and use crypto to move the resulting proceeds.

Chainalysis closely monitors how DPRK actors use crypto to generate revenue, move and consolidate funds, and launder illicit proceeds.

Combined with traditional cybersecurity measures and threat intelligence, blockchain analysis can help organizations and investigators identify and freeze stolen funds. 

It can also map DPRK's expanding financial networks and uncover procurement and payment patterns that can support sanctions investigations and enforcement.

The Binance investigation remains ongoing and we expect stolen funds to continue moving in the coming days.

text:
🚨 NVIDIA JUST OPEN-SOURCED A SEMANTIC LAYER FOR AI AGENTS

It’s called Auto Ontology, and it tackles a problem that better SQL alone won’t fix.

An agent can query the right database and still return the wrong answer.

Why?

Because “revenue” might mean something different in every system.

Auto Ontology is a Python framework that builds shared context over enterprise metadata:

→ Entities and business metrics
→ Relationships between data
→ Certified definitions and lineage
→ Provenance behind answers

It can generate ontologies from metadata, connect existing semantic models, and reconcile conflicting definitions.

For structured data, it also supports natural-language-to-SQL with validation against the ontology.

Agents can access that context through MCP, CLI, or API.

The useful shift: giving agents access to business meaning alongside the data.

Open source under Apache 2.0.

text:
We’re bullish on tokenized stocks because moving equities onchain doesn’t just mirror its value, it unlocks entirely new ways to deploy the capital beneath them.

At @paboxoxyz, that begins with borrowing against stock tokens: tap liquidity without giving up exposure to the underlying stock, with real interest and liquidation risk, plus off‑market mechanics designed from zero specifically for tokenized equities.

It’s awesome and genuinely fun, but we know it’s not enough.

So we’re pushing into the next edge: using liquidity provider (LP) positions as collateral via @Uniswap v4 Hooks.

The setup is hard to ignore. As of writing, there’s already $161M+ in LP positions tied to tokenized stocks, yet composability is still missing.

An LP market could make this possible.

A liquidity provider could borrow against their position without pulling it from the pool, keeping their shot at earning trading fees while unlocking capital at the same time.

But we’re not rushing it.

Doing this right takes more than slapping a price tag on an LP token: the asset mix shifts, fees can underperform, and stock‑market closures make valuation messy, exactly the problems we’re working through.

This is the exploration we’re most excited about.

Our thesis is straightforward: tokenized stocks aren’t just “single stock” assets. Whatever form they evolve into becomes far more powerful once it can plug into trading, liquidity provision, and credit.

We’re building in that direction.

text:
So I know you've all been waiting for my take on weight-space programming, and honestly, I don't know whether to be excited, annoyed, or jealous. Or all three at once.

The gist: researchers at MIT CSAIL (led by Omar Khattab, the man behind some seriously cool ideas) ran a few really simple experiments where they let Astra look at a small model's weights and update them, and it fixed them by hand. No training, no gradients. 
The result: the small model suddenly got much better, not just at math, but also at instruction following, and even at writing its own game-playing network. It also figured out which game a network had been trained on, just by looking at its weights.

Excited: this is such a cool idea. Instead of training a model for weeks, you just edit its weights directly, like gene editing for neural networks. It's the dream we've always had: knowing how to edit specific weights.

Annoyed: most of the magic here leans on existing interpretability tools which work only for small models, on being able to read things off the first or last layer, and on the fact that tasks like these already exist in the training data. So how much of this is just good PR for an old idea?

Jealous: because I've tried things in this direction, and they worked a lot worse. A LOT worse.

Bottom line: it's complicated.

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

What we’ve been working on

Since our last update on October 8th, we’ve been focused on improving the infrastructure behind robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870.

Distributions were paused from October 18th to the 29th while the system was rebuilt. Protocol fees continued to accrue throughout that period and were deployed into stocks once the new setup went live.

Since October 29th, three distribution cycles have completed, sending roughly $23,600 in stocks to 4,163 wallets.

The upgraded setup includes:

• Fixed 36-hour cycles for a consistent distribution schedule.
• Former holders made whole, with around $3,680 in banked stocks distributed to 5,366 addresses that had fallen below the 10,000 robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 threshold.
• Built-in price protection, with stock purchases and ETH → USDG conversions limited to within 1.5% of trusted prices.

The result is a more predictable, secure and scalable distribution system.

Closing the volume gap

A significant portion of robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 trading volume currently routes through pools that do not use the official fee hook, meaning those trades do not contribute to the 3% fee funding stock distributions.

We have already addressed one side of this issue.
Pools holding robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 were previously able to appear as holders and receive distributions. Those pools are now excluded, receive $0, and new pools are checked before every cycle.

The remaining fee-bypass issue requires a deeper change and is already in development. We’ll have more to share on the full approach soon.

The objective is simple: robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870 trading activity should contribute to the protocol economics it was designed to support.

Expanding the Index ecosystem

A large part of our recent product work has also gone into Blend.

Blend introduces permissionless onchain Baskets backed by tokenized assets. Each Basket represents defined quantities of its underlying assets in a single share and can be bought, sold, redeemed and integrated into other applications.

For robinhood:0x56910d4409f3a0c78c64dd8d0545ff0705389870, Blend adds another source of protocol activity and revenue, expanding the ways onchain activity can ultimately flow back into stocks.

What comes next

The distribution infrastructure is stronger, the fee-routing issue is being addressed, and Blend is expanding the ways tokenized assets can be used across the Robinhood ecosystem.

Our focus remains the same: build useful infrastructure around onchain stocks and return more of the value generated by that infrastructure back into the Index ecosystem.

Stocks for everyone.

@AnthropicAI’s impressive work on FlashProve is a real signal for the value of @prlnet’s technology in the toolbox of  provable inference (PI).

FlashProve proves inference correctness post-hoc. Moving it to real-time proof-of-inference requires time-stamping, which is what blockchains were made for.. 

The reality is that AI verification often cares about what a datacenter DIDN’T run. Correct inference proofs don’t rule out parallel, unmonitored workloads. @prlnet’s Pearl-GEMM protocol anchors the output to computation (FLOPs). Paired with PI, it could help bound capacity available for unauthorized training, and provide a “model-tracing” audit for agentic workloads.

Pearl is uniquely positioned to build the work-accounting layer of PI infrastructure.

I am happy to share FlashProve: our performant open-source prototype for provable inference. We believe that this has significant implications for security, pacing AI development, integrity guarantees, and more. 

FlashProve allows a provider to commit to model weights, and then prove that replies originate from the committed model.  The proof leaks no information about the weights, and the verifier can efficiently verify it on consumer hardware. 

Our library is performant, proving a 400B parameter MoE model at 100 tok/s. We have open-sourced the associated code and Lean formalization. We hope that it catalyzes further progress in verification of inference, and look forward to seeing it.

text:
Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

text:
running a company nowadays feels kinda dystopian

my team is 50+ people in 12 countries, but i talk to my agents more than my human teammates

- voice note to grokbot
- mattpocock/skills /grill-me so the agent interrogates the idea before anything gets built
- spec drops into linear through the linear mcp
- exa + firecrawl agent reads every competitor site, pricing page and changelog
- https://t.co/a5ARFnvSnA to find ideas and trends
- apify pulls g2, reddit and app store reviews
- prompt: "find the 10 complaints that show up most and quote the users"
- context7 so the agent reads the latest docs before it touches any api

the design

- claude code + paper mcp
- 4 versions of every screen before a single line of code
- pick pieces from 2, it merges them. diverge then converge
- frontend-design skill from anthropic/skills + our own design system skill
- cleanshot screenshots of any ui i like go straight in with "make it feel like this"

the build

- pingdotgg/t3code as the control surface for every agent, from my phone too
- stablyai/orca runs a fleet of agents in parallel, each in its own git worktree
- graphify maps the whole codebase into a knowledge graph so agents navigate instead of guess
- headroom compresses tool outputs before they hit the model, so tokens go 20-95% further
- lsp plugins so the agent sees types and errors like an ide does
- security guidance hook flags risky edits before they land
- supabase mcp for the database, stripe for billing
- github mcp opens the pr, vercel spins up a preview
- loops run overnight, i check what shipped over coffee

the user testing

- lightpanda as the headless browser, way lighter than chromium so you can run hundreds at once
- agents click every flow on the preview like a first-time user
- one persona is impatient, one is confused, one is on a phone
- playwright + chrome devtools mcp for regression tests

the bugs

- sentry mcp catches the error
- agent reads the stack trace and opens a fix pr in under 10 minutes
- human just approves

the data

- posthog mcp cron at 7am on yesterday's funnel
- any step that drops more than 10%, the agent watches 20 session replays and tells me why
- stripe mcp pulls every cancellation reason into one doc every monday

the agents' tools

- orgo so every agent gets its own computer
- agentmail so every agent gets its own inbox
- agentphone so i can call them from the car
- composio connect-apps for every other connector
- akitaonrails/ai-memory, a git-backed markdown wiki so they remember what we decided last week

the skills

- wshobson/agents so skills work across claude code, codex and opencode
- my writing voice
- our design system
- how we write specs
- skill creator so the agents write new skills themselves

some helpful tricks

- one agent per platform. the x agent never touches email
- cheap model for triage, opus for anything that ships
- every output gets scored 1-10 by an llm judge. under 8 goes back
- every agent writes a 5-line log at night so i can read the whole company in 2 minutes
- every agent mistake becomes a new skill, so it only happens once

the team

- humans get version 5, not my voice note which they are happy about lol 
- their job is creative feedback, relationships and telling the agents what they got wrong

a human pm reviews the funnel once a week. this reviews it every morning

running a company is now voice notes and inference

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

当时的玩法是，让交易员和投行家自己用 Claude Code 写工具，拿来盯客户交易流、建仓位模型，搓出个半成品之后，再丢给工程师去收尾。

结果到了 10 月，高盛重新评估完生产力和安全风险，直接踩了刹车。

全公司 4.6 万人，现在只有那 1.2 万名工程师和量化研究员还能继续用，剩下 3.4 万人全部退回只能对话的内部普通 AI 助手。

干过软件工程的人看到“业务人员写半成品，丢给工程师收尾”这句话，大概就能脑补出现场有多酸爽了。

我觉得很多公司推全员写代码，最后都会撞上同一笔糊涂账。

外行用 AI 两小时搓出来的脚本，看着能跑出结果，但权限隔离、异常处理、合规审计全是空的。

工程师接手这种代码，先看懂逻辑、再去排雷重构花掉的时间，往往比从头写一个还要久。

表面上看，一个交易员觉得自己效率起飞了；实际上，后面几个工程师的排期全被拖慢，公司还得替那些野路子脚本担着合规和安全的雷。

这玩意儿如果只是在自己电脑上跑个一次性数据、做个图表，自己写自己看，那确实爽。

一旦要进正式生产环境、要长期维护、要跟核心系统接在一起，工程能力依然是绕不开的硬门槛。

对外，高盛在帮英伟达张罗 5000 亿美元的算力融资平台，帮 Anthropic 做最高 1000 亿美元的上市承销。

对内，算完真实投入产出比，默默把写代码的锤子从外行手里收走，只留给那 26% 真正懂施工的人。

真服了，华尔街算起自家的账来，身体比谁都诚实。

要不我去开个“Vibe Coding 善后班”算了，专门研究怎么在不伤感情的前提下，把老板用 AI 写出来的半成品悄悄删掉重写。

Goldman Sachs has spent two years pushing AI out to its roughly 46,000 employees, not just its 12,000 engineers

The approach used several model providers at once: an in-house assistant built on models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet, plus Anthropic's Claude Code and Microsoft's GitHub for bankers who wanted to build their own tools

As recently as July, CIO Marco Argenti was promoting "vibe coding" by traders and bankers, who built tools with AI and passed them to engineers to finish

In October, Goldman reversed course. Per reporting from Bloomberg, updated internal guidance now limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers after a review of productivity and risk, and some traders are frustrated

A week before the story ran, Anthropic filed publicly for its IPO with Goldman as one of two lead underwriters

Here are the five moves that took Goldman from vibe coding to engineers only

1. GS AI Assistant

In June 2025, Goldman took its internal chatbot firmwide after a pilot with about 10,000 users, out of a workforce of roughly 46,500

The assistant runs inside Goldman's compliance perimeter and gives staff access to models including ChatGPT and Gemini

Argenti rolled out GitHub Copilot and Gemini Code Assist, and Goldman became the first major bank to use Cognition's autonomous coding agent, Devin

By August 2026, hundreds of Devin agents were working alongside roughly 12,000 human developers, and Argenti said the deployment could grow into the thousands

2. Claude in the back office

In February, Argenti told CNBC that Anthropic engineers had been embedded inside Goldman for six months, building autonomous agents on Claude

The first targets were trade and transaction accounting and client vetting and onboarding. 

3. Hong Kong

In late April, the Financial Times reported that Goldman had cut off Anthropic's models for its Hong Kong bankers
Staff there had used Claude through the bank's internal AI platform and had lost access in the preceding weeks

The FT said the cause was a strict reading of Goldman's contract with Anthropic, made after consulting the company. 

Anthropic told the FT that Claude had never been officially supported in Hong Kong
Gemini and ChatGPT stayed on the platform, so the restriction applied to Claude only and was not a ban on AI

4. Nvidia and Anthropic

While the internal rules were tightening, Goldman's AI banking business was growing

It is underwriting Anthropic's IPO and helping Nvidia arrange large debt deals

In August, Nvidia signed memoranda of understanding with KKR, Goldman, Brookfield, Blackstone, BlackRock and Apollo to set up compute financing platforms

The goal is to bring in more than $500 billion of outside capital over time. Solomon has said Jensen Huang brought the idea to Goldman

On October 26, Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ANT, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley as lead underwriters
IFR reported the offering could raise $75 billion to $100 billion through a syndicate of more than 20 banks

5. Engineers only

The October guidance limits Claude Code and GitHub to engineers. Strats, who work across trading, quant research and engineering, are exempt

Traders had been using the tools to monitor client trading flows, model market moves and positions, and produce written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg

A Goldman spokesperson said the bank makes AI tools available across the firm to find use cases

After a trial period weighing productivity and risk, it gives them to the people best placed to use them long term

Bloomberg noted that banks are spending millions of dollars on AI tools while also managing cybersecurity risk, cost and productivity

Non-engineers who relied on Claude Code or GitHub now need to request other tools or use the GS AI Assistant instead

That leaves Claude Code with roughly 26% of Goldman's headcoun

text:
The post-quantum path @Starknet is taking is revealing more serious loopholes in blockchain design than I thought. 

StarkWare built a framework from NIST's 'general crypto-agility guidance' to test how agile blockchains are, and only one chain scored 8/8. 

Bitcoin itself passes 7 of the 8 tests, tied for second among the 10 chains scored, yet it faces one of the hardest migrations.

NIST wrote the guidance but doesn't rate chains, so StarkWare built the 8 questions and scored the networks itself. 

It's a bit technical, but let's review it.

➥ Based on NIST's guidance on crypto agility, the 8 questions ask whether a chain can replace its cryptography and keep running:

1. Can an existing account switch to a new signature without a network upgrade?
2. Can its formats handle bigger keys and signatures?
3. Can one cryptographic part be replaced without redesigning the rest?
4. Can old and new signing run side by side undedr migration?
5. Has the transition been tested?
6. Can an attacker be stopped from forcing a weaker algorithm?
7. Can the old algorithm be switched off after migration?
8. Can existing data be migrated?

A point only counts if the path works today under current rules. Anything that needs a future upgrade scores zero.

Across 10 networks the scores are @Starknet 8, @Bitcoin 7, @Algorand 7, @NEARProtocol 7, @QRLedger 6, @Zcash 6, @ethereum 3, @solana 2, @Optimism 2 and @RobinhoodCrypto 1.

➥ The test that separates Starknet from the 7s is the first one. 

On Starknet every account is a smart contract, so a wallet can replace its signature check and keep its address and funds. StarkWare confirmed this with @ready_co. 

A coin on the Bitcoin network has to move to a new address to use new cryptography, and NEAR and Algorand accounts can only choose schemes the protocol has already switched on, nothing more.

What I respect most is what the score does not claim. It is not a security rating. 

QRLedger scores 6 yet shows lower exposure on the same Hub, because its signatures are already hash-based. 

Starknet's standard accounts still sign with elliptic curves, and its post-quantum Falcon-512 account is an unaudited mainnet demo that ordinary users can't adopt yet. 

So my takeaway is that being able to change and having already changed are two different things, and a chain needs both. 

Next, I'll break down where Starknet stands on the second. For now, what's your take on this?

You could buy 100 shares of $SPCX right now for $14,177. Or you could buy the $120 call LEAP expiring January 2028 for $4,620. Leveraged exposure to the same 100 shares. ~67% less capital. Over 440 days of runway.

Premium: ~$46.20 ($4,620 per contract)
Breakeven: $166.20

At expiration:
If $SPCX hits $200, this LEAP returns ~73%
If $SPCX hits $250, this LEAP returns ~181%

- Revenue grew 161% to $14.6B last quarter, and SpaceX swung to $4.4B of net income from a $1.05B loss a year ago

quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

text:
PULSE (also called Delta weight sync) has become one of the most important ideas in RL infrastructure this year. Our paper, posted on February 3, explained why it loses nothing. At RL learning rates, about 99% of each step's weight updates disappear in the BF16 cast, so the inference workers never see them.

Since then, @huggingface has built Delta Weight Sync for TRL and vLLM on that argument. @FireworksAI_HQ cites PULSE, and its ARCv3 compressor now makes the updates even smaller.

This week @humansand reported pausing inference for only about 220 milliseconds per update on Blackwell GPUs.

PULSE has now been accepted at AXIOM, a @NeurIPSConf 2026 workshop.

quoted_text:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!

This is to run all my websites/apps serving per year:
- 20,000 paying customers
- 252 million visitors
- 2.4 billion requests
- 2.4 petabyte (PB) in bandwidth

(~$8,000/mo if you add the $7,000/mo GPU bill and $800/mo R2 storage I pay for Photo AI, I exclude it above because it's one project that's so much more expensive in size than all the other sites together, but included in the chart below)

Claude Code helped me to find smart ways to save more money, AI is just really really really good at finding cost savings by itself, which is not so great for the economy short-term, but long term it trims all the fat and opens up spending for better investments I think

Anyway here's what it saved me in money, almost $34,000/mo:

- $29,000/mo - switched to better and cheaper video models on Photo AI, video was very expensive and since I didn't update it ever it stayed expensive, also routed some image jobs to Google Cloud where I have some Google Cloud Credits, and also routed some jobs to Sume which sells AI models at market cost, very cool! This made my GPU bill go from $36,000/mo to $7,000/mo

- $3,000/mo - consolidated my servers, cancelled Digital Ocean and Linode and moved everything to Hetzner saving about $3,000/mo

- $1100/mo - analyzed my Backblaze B2 server backups, I had infinite versioning and lifecycle policies, that's reduced now to 30 days, this literally pushed the bill from $1,200/mo to $26/mo, about 50x cheaper! I had essentially versions of files for all my servers for over a decade, crazy!

- $400/mo - similarly added Lifecycle Policies to my Cloudflare R2 bucket for Photo AI, pics are automatically put in cheaper Infrequent Access after 90 days, there was years of photos in there so this reduced the R2 bill from $1,200/mo to $800/mo

- $118/mo - Claude analyzed all my Cloudflare Domain registrations, lots of domains I didn't use and didn't make sense to keep paying for, lots of things that also don't really make sense anymore in a post-AGI world, renewals for .io TLD are now $50/year which adds up fast!

- $100/mo - Claude also analyzed my Claude subscription (yes!) and discovered I don't even use the Max 20x plan limits, so I downgraded from $200/mo to $100/mo

Even including Photo AI, I have now cut my costs by 90% from last year, getting me close to my biz expenses amount from a decade ago when I started building things

Costs slowly creep up over the years and you don't realize all the things you're spending on but AI is nice to help you figure all that out (also in your personal life!)

text:
people underestimate how much GPU networking and storage actually costs

networking easily adds an extra 10% to the cost of a cluster

external storage, like WEKA or VAST, is an extra $1M+ to setup - plus a monthly recurring fee

one of the many reasons compute markets are still early is because GPU clusters are nuanced

many people see a $5 B300 and think it's a fungible commodity, but these details are everything
author: mernit
quoted_text:
People tend to assume that the more GPUs you rent, the cheaper each GPU gets, but that's not really how the market works

Prices often bottom out around 32–64 GPUs, then rise as larger, interconnected clusters become harder to find and more expensive to operate.

At a certain size (~2,000 GPUs+), network designs even require an additional layer of switches, which can create massive incremental cost

Cluster size deserves a lot more attention in compute pricing negotiations

text:
Andrew Huberman says Rick Rubin knows exactly when his mind is sharpest, and the two of them are trying to build tools to unlock that focus more quickly and deeply:

"My friend Rick Rubin... his work block generally is in the afternoon. That's when his mind is sharpest, and then he tapers off in the evening. But he's working extremely hard in those hours, and he knows when those fall."

"If you're in one of those windows and you allow your attention to be captured by something that's not worthwhile... the productivity that comes in those three or four hours is exponentially greater than the productivity that comes from doing that work at some point later."

"We don't really have formal protocols for task switching, but this is extremely important for company founders and employees across the board, right?"

"Rick and I have been kicking around some tools that are not meditations... that would allow you to kind of program your mind for what comes next."

"If you think about it, it's 2026. Why in the world are we sitting down to do work and just going, 'Okay, now I'm gonna be focused, and now I'm gonna be creative.'"

text:
Introducing Mallard 🦆: Git for the age of AI agents.

@li_fuyao  and I started Mallard to make it easier to share our agent sessions and build things together.
We spend much of our working day talking to Claude and Codex. Those conversations include the ideas, designs, and decisions behind our work. However they often stay on one machine, without backups or an easy way to share them.

3 months. 10 accounts on 20× plans. 100 billion tokens later, Mallard finally hatched.

- Share and back up agent sessions using Cloudflare R2, Dropbox, or Mallard Cloud.

- Explore the discussions and design decisions behind PRs, including Mallard’s hatching logs.

- Pull and resume sessions in Codex or Claude Code with the original context.

For teams, Anthropic internally uses cloud VMs and Claude Tag so that teammates can work in shared agent conversations and pick up where others left off. Mallard lets teams achieve the same goal at almost zero cost, without any cloud VMs.

I want Mallard to be free and easy to use for everyone, rich or poor.

We built a lightweight version of GIT and reworked our storage protocol, removing CAS so Mallard can work with any cloud storage that supports LIST and PUT APIs. Bring your own storage or use Mallard Cloud. No Git server or expensive sandbox required.

We also added one-click sign-in for Dropbox and Cloudflare R2, so anyone can connect their own cloud storage to Mallard in just a few clicks.

We don’t think the internet, recommendation algorithms, or AI should be in the hands of just a few people. We hope Mallard helps more people share their work, find an audience, and have their voices heard.

Free and MIT licensed. Available on macOS and Windows.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime.

Further to my post about @NYSE working to bring @HyperliquidX onshore, major credit to @ChairmanSelig and the Trump administration for making all of this experimentation possible. 

There’s only one way of finding out if something is useful to the marketplace and I’m excited for us to find out. I do have some questions:

1. What is the benefit of trading perps on-chain on a regulated exchange? Isn’t the main benefit of trading on-chain to operate in a trustless (aka non-kyc’d) environment in order to minimize friction, and/or to be able to enter into atomic transactions in order to receive what you are buying in realtime? Since a perp is not an asset, that obviously isn’t helpful. 

2. @standuquesne - are you aware that if you trade on Hyperliquid, the world will be able to track your positions and trades in real time? Do you see that as a benefit?

3. Hyperliquid has priority fees - a mechanism that enables market participants to pay to see information first, or even prioritize orders in front of the queue. Is this consistent with CFTC core principles?

4. Will it be possible to combine the liquidity of the offshore order-book with the onshore order-book?

5. If not, wouldn’t it be better to list perps in a traditional (centralized) order-book on a regulated exchange and not have the inefficiencies that on-chain matching introduces?

text:
Taylor Hornby (@DefuseSec) on the state of AI-assisted software audits: 

Current models are great at auditing, and everyone needs to be doing it. The two biggest problems that still need solving are: 

(a) models are not good at properly understanding an issue’s severity, so there is still a lot of manual work to validate what the AI finds (this is the next thing I want to work on), and 

(b) defenders need access to the best models without cyber safeguards in order to audit their own code. 

Frontier labs need to do a better job of letting legitimate security research and auditing through the safeguards, and of providing AI audits and patching support to open-source projects. Anthropic’s Fable safeguards’ initial refusals to work on pretty much anything cryptography-related may have ultimately done more harm than good, since they blocked legitimate defensive research. 

The situation has gotten better now that Anthropic has allowed users in their Cyber Verification Program to run Mythos on security tasks.

刚看到币安官推发布了安全调查报告，看完让人后背发凉，我根据我的理解梳理一下

9 月份：软件工程师 B 在一个正规的求职平台上，被一个「项目总监」联系，主动挖他。我猜大概率就是 LinkedIn 了，暴露了 B 是币安在职员工。

项目总监安排了两轮面试：一面是所谓 HR 视频面试，取得 B 的信任；二面是虚构公司的 CEO，通过 IM 进行，并且让 B 下载了一个包含恶意代码库的「作业」到他的工作电脑上。这个代码库的恶意代码，在安装过程中就执行了，引发了一系列未经授权的活动。而且这是一个 0-day 恶意软件，当时币安的终端安全软件都没检测出来，黑客还刻意清除了入侵痕迹，加大了发现和调查的难度。

10 月 20 号：黑客从 B 的电脑出发，借助币安公司内部的 AI 工具，控制了钱包运维工程师 A 和钱包软件工程师 C 的电脑。

控制 A 的电脑之后，黑客在上面发现了容器部署权限令牌。

10 月 29 日：黑客登录员工 C 的电脑，用从 A 那里偷来的凭证部署容器、运行恶意脚本，从而拿到内部钱包签名服务的访问权，在正常提现流程之外发起了转账。之后黑客又利用 EIP-7702 授权，批量转走了 ETH 链上的资产。

更早之前 6 月份的时候，A 其实在搜索引擎上搜热门 AI 编程工具后，就下载了被篡改的 Homebrew 安装包，但这次事件被安全团队及时发现了，没有酿成大祸。但工程师 A 的岗位及其钱包基础设施团队的相关同事，当时就已暴露给黑客

总结来说，这是一场多阶段攻击：结合了假面试、恶意软件下载、内部 AI 工具被利用、终端设备被入侵，以及高级的交易授权手法。

LinkedIn 暴露币安员工身份只是表象；A 下载被篡改的工具，让黑客锁定了钱包团队 + B 在工作电脑上运行「面试作业」直接打开大门，这才是根源；内部 AI 工具成了横向渗透的跳板，让黑客从一台电脑扩散到三个核心钱包工程师；而 EIP-7702 授权加上 MPC 钱包难以快速撤销，让事件在近 4 小时内没被完全控住，是催化剂

text:
使用 Claude 团队版（Team）和企业版（Enterprise）的员工，登录 Claude 后，公司已开通的插件现在可以自动连上，不用再一个个登录、点授权。

Anthropic 的开发者账号 ClaudeDevs 在 11 月 3 日宣布了这项功能，目前是测试版。

先说几个基础概念。

插件是给 Claude 加装的扩展，让它能直接操作别的软件，比如读 Notion 里的文档、查 Datadog 的监控数据。插件背后通常连着一个 MCP 服务器。

MCP（模型上下文协议）是 Anthropic 提出的一套公开标准，规定 AI 怎样和外部软件对接，类似一个通用接口。

以前麻烦在授权。

每连一个插件，用户都要跳到那个软件的网页登录，再点“允许 Claude 访问我的数据”。这一步叫 OAuth 授权，用微信账号登录某个 App 时弹出的确认页面就是同一类流程。公司用了十几个工具，员工就要重复十几次。

新办法有两种。

1. 通过公司的身份提供方。

很多公司用一套统一账号系统管理员工登录，比如 Okta，一个账号登录所有工作软件，这类系统叫身份提供方（IdP）。管理员在这里统一设置哪些员工能用哪些插件。

员工用公司账号登录 Claude 后，Claude 向身份提供方要一份带签名的身份证明，拿去插件那边换取访问权限，员工全程看不到这一步。这套做法叫企业托管授权（EMA），是 MCP 的一个公开扩展，其他 AI 软件也可以采用。

2. 由 Claude 直接担保。

如果公司的身份提供方还不支持 EMA，Claude 可以直接替已登录的员工证明身份。前提是插件开发方接受 Claude 作为“可信签发方”，也就是承认 Claude 开出的身份证明有效。管理员为某个插件开通后，公司里符合条件的员工就能自动连接。

对员工来说，入职后打开 Claude，公司常用的工具已经连好，连接到期后会在后台续上，不用重新授权。

对公司 IT 来说，在身份提供方那边就能统一开通和收回权限，员工离职时不必逐个软件去撤销。

“Claude 作为可信签发方”的自动连接，目前支持这 14 家的插件：

1. Amplitude（产品数据分析）
2. https://t.co/9lHoGFV9OB（销售线索）
3. Atlassian（Jira、Confluence 等协作工具）
4. Datadog（服务器监控）
5. Dropbox（网盘）

text:
Some dreams don’t disappear. They just get rewritten by the people who need you more.
I spent years of my youth chasing a life as a guitarist. Fingerstyle was my passion. I put in the hours, earned respect for the craft, and thought music would be what my life revolved around. Then my daughter Madeline was born, and everything changed.
She’s 13 now. She’s had seizures since she was six months old. She’s non-verbal, and her development has been severely delayed. I remember crying the first time she walked... she was eight. I wasn’t sure she ever would. I still have this recurring dream where I hear her say “I love you.” Most people take those words for granted. I still hope to hear them one day. In the meantime she shows me in her own way. She’ll sit next to me, grab my hand, give me big wet kisses on the cheek, and laugh. Those moments are everything.
Early on, my wife and I had to make a hard decision about our lives and hers. Madeline needs care around the clock...lifting, bathing, feeding, managing seizures, everything. It takes a tremendous amount of physical strength and constant presence. My wife had the opportunity to become a special education teacher. We decided she would be the one to work, and I would stay home to care for Madeline. It wasn’t an easy choice. It meant one income, giving up the career path I thought I’d have, and accepting that our roles would look very different from what most people expect. We believed it was the best way to give Madeline what she needs and still provide for our other three kids. Looking back, it was the right decision for our family, even if the cost has been high.
The truth is, this life is beautiful and brutal at the same time. I’ve been changing diapers for 13 years straight with no end in sight. With only one of us able to work, the financial strain has been constant. I’ve given up meals so my family could eat. I’ve set aside the life I thought I was building so I could be present for the one I actually have. I’m not perfect. I’m tired. I’m scared about the future... about who will care for Madeline when I’m gone, about how we’ll keep everything together. I don’t always have answers. I’ve learned to accept the tears that come with this life. Some things are simply outside our control.
What we lack in money we try to make up for in love. My wife and I have given everything we have to give. Right now, though, the financial weight has become too much. We’re asking for help so we can build a little more security for our family.
If you’ve ever had to trade one dream for another, or if you’ve ever made a hard decision about who stays home so someone else can be cared for, you understand. We’re not looking for a handout. We’re trying to keep going for the people who need us.
If you’re able and willing to support us, I’d be deeply grateful.

Venmo: @Carlos_Trujillo_Guitar
Thank you for reading. It means more than I can say.

quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!
