text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

我刚把钱从交易所提出来，放进台湾的银行，没想到才几天，就看到这么永丰银行疑似被骇这么诡异的新闻😂

说被骇应该不准确，准确来说是永丰银行这次的集体异常转账事件：涉及 419 名客户、4000 多万新台币，每笔 10 万，全部同时转进台北富邦银行同一个账户。最离谱的是，受害人都反映说自己根本没打开 App，也没做人脸识别，系统却显示验证成功，钱就这么转出去了。

问了几个朋友，台湾银行业内部初步判断，应该不是传统意义上的黑客盗窃，更像是银行内控出了问题。永丰自己的说法，也是「新网银交易系统程序异常」。

一种可能是：永丰 12 天前才向金管会提交完整技术报告，新系统的交易功能可能还在开发、测试。为了让系统能正常读取台湾身份证字号，内部工程师可能写了一段测试程序，写死了程序，绕过去做批次测试，结果误把真实客户当成测试对象，直接执行了转账。

另一种可能是：内控系统刚好在跑云林地区某个批次的资料核对，程序出错，原本只是测试的交易变成了真实扣款。

但令人不安的是，如果银行后台程序真的可以绕过前端手机验证，在客户完全不知情、没有密码和 OTP 的情况下直接把钱转走，事后还给这些交易打上「刷脸成功」的标签，那问题就不只是一次出错了。

当然，这些都只是技术层面的猜测，具体原因还得等金管会调查。

目前客户的钱虽然退回来了，但这个漏洞如果真的存在，想想还是挺吓人的。毕竟我们把真金白银存在银行，谁能想到，最大的风险可能就藏在银行自己的系统里？？？

US federal debt hit a record $𝟰𝟬.𝟲𝗧 in October after adding $422B to the balance sheet, with the Treasury auctioning a record $𝟴𝟯𝟵𝗕 in bills and notes last week. Debt-to-GDP climbed to 123%, matching the 2020 pandemic peak.

𝗛𝘂𝗽𝘇𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲: Record issuance at this pace puts sustained upward pressure on long-end Treasury yields, raising the discount rate applied to non-yielding risk assets like BTC. With daily borrowing near $10B and issuance increasingly rolling forward rather than funding new spending, the fiscal trajectory reinforces the rate channel that has weighed on risk-asset valuations.

For BTC, watch the 10-year yield response to the auction calendar — persistent elevated real yields cap upside even if risk sentiment improves.

text:
Ethereum is accelerating its post-quantum roadmap, now targeting a full transition by the end of 2028. This is a significant change from the previous timeline.

The technical direction:

1. Execution layer: Replace ECDSA with hash-based signatures, leanSPHINCS.
2. Consensus layer: Replace BLS signatures with hash-based leanXMSS.
3. Data layer: Replace KZG commitments with a post-quantum alternative, leanDA.

The common theme is hash-based cryptography, with SHA-3 as the current default hash function. It’s a conservative choice with well-understood security assumptions and good security margins, but comes with significantly larger signatures and proofs. leanVM is intended to make this practical through proof aggregation.

There's also the question of existing ETH.

Our analysis at Project Eleven found that roughly 72% of the ETH supply is associated with accounts that have already exposed their public keys. These funds would be vulnerable to a sufficiently powerful quantum computer capable of recovering private keys.

You can explore the exposure here: https://t.co/CRPJi34HgT

Moving ETH to a fresh address whose public key hasn't been exposed provides some protection, but it's not a long-term solution. Once that account broadcasts a transaction, its public key is exposed again. With estimates of quantum attacks potentially taking seconds or less, relying on a short mempool window is increasingly difficult to justify.

Ultimately, all ETH needs a path to quantum-resistant authorization, not just the 72% already exposed. This doesn't necessarily require waiting until 2028. Hash-based signature verifiers can already be deployed on-chain, albeit with significantly higher costs than native protocol support.

The cryptography is only part of the problem. Ethereum needs to ship the protocol changes, get wallets and infrastructure to support them, and make migration practical for everyone.

2028 is an ambitious target, but it's great to see the urgency.

text:
@ everyone who works at a company looking for answers to "what should we do about security", here's an excellent answer. I'd say this is the 80/20. 

Most people trying to secure their systems don't understand the threat model -- who and what are you defending against? Most exploit chains in practice are just variations of phishing/supply chain attack and use local employee devices as the break-in point. It's hard to categorically eliminate malware on local devices, but it's easy to limit the blast radius and ensure that a single compromised device doesn't end your entire company.

If you could pick 1 thing to do: Require phishing-resistant MFA (like a yubikey) before employees can access any data in production. 2FA is simple but unreasonably effective, and extremely underutilized. Passkeys, TouchId/FaceID, and AI tools like Devin make it really easy to implement it too.

text:
J'ai passé 24h avec 2 Chinois.

Et j'en conclus qu'il va falloir arrêter de vous plaindre et aller bosser un peu.

Le premier sujet qu'ils ont mis sur la table, c'est les émeutes en France. Ils avaient vu les vidéos. Ils m'ont dit qu'ils avaient honte pour nous.

Ça m'a mis un petit coup. Alors j'ai voulu comprendre comment ils vivent, eux.

On a commencé par les vacances.

Eux ont 5 jours de congés payés par an. Nous c'est 5 semaines minimum, et avec les RTT certains montent à 7, 8 et plus.

Du coup ils voyagent très peu. La plupart ne connaissent que leur pays.

Et côté boulot c'est le même écart. On bosse 35 heures par semaine, eux en font 50. Et 50h en présentiel, pas en télétravail avec 3 pauses café.

Même à la fac il y a un écart. Ils ont 2 mois de vacances dans l'année. Nous rien que l'été c'est souvent 3 mois.

Ensuite on a parlé des aides. Chez eux quasiment rien. Ils ne comprenaient pas tout ce qu'on peut toucher en France.

Puis de l'immobilier. Chez eux acheter un appart c'est souvent un crédit sur 30 ans. Et ils achètent là où ils sont nés, près de leurs parents, pour y rester toute leur vie.

Le plus marquant, c'est que toute cette vie-là est vécue comme la normalité. Pas comme un sacrifice.

Et pour revenir aux émeutes, en Chine si tu passes ta vie à te plaindre sur les réseaux, ton contenu disparaît.

Nous on a la liberté de nous exprimer. Et vous vous en servez pour dire des conneries.

On a un des systèmes les plus confortables du monde et on passe notre temps à en vouloir plus.

Pendant ce temps, leurs rues sont propres, les filles sont en sécurité dehors, et ils sont super fiers de leur pays.

Vous êtes des enfants pourris gâtés.

text:
昨天很荣幸参加了两场 @yzilabs YZi 相关的活动，见到了不少老朋友和新朋友，也对 Crypto 和 Cybersecurity 行业有了一些新的感悟。

首先感谢 @Web3SisterA A姐和 @Plus_Ultra_715 Winchman 组织的 YZi Alumni Happy Hour，让我有机会和横跨四届的校友们交流，探讨合作机会。

我和 Shawn 聊了不少关于持续渗透测试、软件版本迭代中的安全更新等话题；向 Calix 哥请教了 To B 业务，特别是大企业客户的获客策略；也和 Edward 探讨了 Agent Trading 究竟在卖什么：是 Alpha Strategies，还是能够持续产出 Alpha 的 Quant System？

当然，最惊喜的是孙哥 @sunyuchentron 也作为 S3 的师兄来到了现场。我也抓住机会，和孙哥交流了十几分钟。

我们都认为，B 端 AI 正迎来巨大的代际机会，尤其是在医疗、法律、军事、网络安全等关键领域。AI 能够为企业带来的效率提升、利润增长和成本节约是巨大的，这也让这些垂直领域的企业具有非常强的付费意愿。

另外，我们也分享了自己在技术路线上的一些选择：更多地采用开源模型，计划通过后训练打造自己的小模型，并结合合成数据、模型融合等策略，真正做到 Own Our Intelligence。

专有数据、低至主流模型几十分之一甚至上百分之一的调用成本，以及更快的响应速度，都将成为我们的护城河。相信孙哥布局 BAI，也有这方面的考量。

快八点的时候，我们来到了 YZi 的 Private Dinner。感谢 Yuna @yunna025、Ella 姐 @ellazhang516、半仙 Jane @JaneSparking 的组织！

席间我们了解到，香港特区政府也非常重视网络安全，正在金融、医疗等领域投入更多资源加强攻防能力，同时也希望有更多安全企业参与其中。

回想去年，我刚辞职准备创业的时候，业界还很少有人相信 AI 能够自主发现漏洞，甚至完成端到端的攻击。彼时，我们就开始用 AI 做各种 PoC，试图让更多人相信，AI Cybersecurity 将会彻底改变这个行业。

而在过去一年里，AI-driven Attacks 层出不穷。从 Zcash、Hugging Face，到 Linux、macOS，以及 PHP2Shell 等零日漏洞相关案例，AI 网络安全已经成为最受关注的赛道之一，行业也迫切需要新的安全解决方案。

而我们也早已跨越了单纯调用模型的阶段，在上下文管理、多智能体框架、模型路由等方面进行了更深入的工程探索。同时，我们也更加坚信 Human-in-the-Loop 的价值。

我们判断，未来一年，整个cybersecurity行业都将经历属于自己的 Napster Moment，在阵痛中迎来新一轮范式转变，而新的解决方案也将逐步站稳脚跟。

也许是经过后训练的专用模型，也许是 AI SOC，也许是我们押注的 AI Offensive Security。当然，也可能是多种方案并存，共同构成下一代安全基础设施。

Security is a never-ending problem. It can never be fully solved, only continuously rebalanced between attackers and defenders.

在 AI 时代，网络安全可能会越来越像一种 Proof of Work。

谁投入了更多有效的安全工作、消耗了更多 Tokens 去发现和修复潜在漏洞，谁就有机会建立更强的安全优势。

当防御方持续投入的计算资源和安全工作量超过攻击者愿意付出的经济成本时，攻击就可能变得不再划算。

这有点像区块链的 51% Attack：理论上攻击始终可能发生，但当攻击成本足够高、预期收益足够低时，系统就能建立起一种基于经济激励的安全性。

我们当然希望自己能够站在这场 Paradigm Shift 的支点上，但更重要的是，能够为解决这个时代最重要的问题之一贡献自己的力量。

To make the world a safer place, one hack at a time.

incredible how they've almost single-handedly kept eating market share from CEXs, now sitting at more than 31% of Binance's spot volume.

that makes Uniswap the #2 crypto exchange in the world, including all CEXs and DEXs.

let that sink in.

and it means even more when you consider how unfair the game actually is. CEXs are in a completely different position to exploit their advantages, and they do. shady backdoor deals and extractive market making give them nearly endless capital and capacity to compete.

DEXs have none of that. just a protocol living onchain, fully transparent, truly sticking to the crypto ethos. but they have the better product, and slowly but surely that's winning out.

we don't get a ton of success stories like this in crypto. but it's exactly these rare cases of real innovation that keep me going, regardless of bull or bear market.

incredible what we can build as an industry despite all the obstacles in our way. and long term, it's always good to be reminded that the good ones win.

love to see it, true inspiration for all builders out there that genuinely care about building something long lasting. the better product will always win, regardless how intimidating your competition and incumbents may look like.

first of all, can a prediction market be wrong? yes. a PM can be mispriced relative to the "true" probability. 

was the 80c price for Bolso ahead of the election "wrong"? yes. the polls showed a dead heat. the market on the PM was showing tons of conviction the wrong way around. 80 cents was wrong. 

saying "20c odds happen one in five times so 20c was not wrong" is unfalsifiable. a PM can never be mispriced according to that logic. 

second, electoral PMs are not the same as dice rolls or other sources of "genuine" randomness. 

elections are uncertain in the epistemic sense - it's hard to gather all the data beforehand and price them. this is not the same kind of uncertainty you get from rolling a fair die. unlike the die, there is always some kind of inherent underlying political reality to be discovered. 

the "true probability" of an election given perfect knowledge is going to be 100/0 one way. of course, no one has perfect knowledge, which is in theory the value prop of PMs; giving sharps the financial incentive to go out there and discover that knowledge and furnish it in the form of prices. 

it's not reasonable to say "underdogs sometimes win, so a 20c probability that happens is automatically valid". you could use that to justify any nonzero probability even down to 0.1c. 

elections are not card draws or dice rolls. they are events that condense political realities into a single number. PMs are meant to pay people to discover that number. the PM in the case of Brazil (and maybe the midterms – who knows) failed to do this. so the PM was "wrong", in the sense that it wasn't useful. in fact, it was was actively worse than what the polls were suggesting. that makes it wrong.

author: transmissions11
quoted_text:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

author: FLS_OTC
quoted_text:
Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

text:
@Sandy_Carter came over.

She used to run enterprise AI at Amazon. Before that Watson at IBM. Now she is CEO of EQUS and they just kicked off their first beta of EQUS X, a personal assistant.

We spent a long time on something most AI pitches skip.

These agents are not just learning that you like pepperoni. They are learning how you think. How you negotiate. How you solve a problem. Who you trust in a deal. Sandy has two daughters and she was trying to get them to see it the way she once taught them about posting on social media. Careful what you put out there. Except now the machine can learn your judgment, not just your photos.

That is useful. That is also terrifying.

She told me about a friend with cancer who went to the Mayo Clinic and came home with a huge stack of medical reports. He put them into an assistant so he could actually use the information. Great for him. Also the exact kind of data you do not want training someone else's model or getting used to target you later.

EQUS X still learns you.
https://t.co/MrCJUOUWGo

The difference is the data stays yours. You pick who it shares with. You can pull it back out. Same convenience people already want from agents that book trips and return Amazon packages, without turning your life into training fuel.

We got into agent reputation too, which almost nobody has figured out. If your agent buys five hundred boxes of Kleenex and stiffs Amazon, is that on you or on the agent? If it escapes a sandbox and does something you never asked for, whose reputation takes the hit? Sandy says they have patents around that.

Someone at Cloudflare told her reputation is one of the hardest problems in this whole stack.

She agrees.

She is writing a paper on the ROI of data ownership and privacy. Her real obsession is privacy that does not make the product suck. She has been studying how Stripe grew by living with a small set of power users instead of shipping something half baked to everyone.

Long conversation is in the video.

Demo is separate in the first comment if you just want to see the product.

BINANCE PUBLISHED MORE DETAILS ON HOW THE $6.34 BILLION HACK HAPPENED:

>june: engineer A searches for a “popular ai coding tool”
>downloads a malicious homebrew installer 
>binance security finds out
>replaces the device
>but engineers working on wallet infrastructure have been identified
>september: engineer B gets contacted by a recruiter from a legitimate job platform
>goes on a call with HR and later, CEO of a fake company 
>gets a coding assignment 
>downloads a malicious code repo on his WORK computer 
>malware runs, replaces a legit dev tool and goes undetected by security 
>october 20: hackers use engineer B’s computer and Binance’s internal ai tool to get access to engineer A and C’s computers 
>discover a token for wallet deployment on engineer A computer 
>october 29:log into engineer C computer 
>use engineer A’s stolen credentials 
>gain access to Binance’s wallet signing service

so the hack wasn’t a spontaneous single security breach, but a sophisticated campaign over a few months, which also included social engineering.

there’s particularly 3 main human mistakes throughout this process:
1. engineer A downloading a tampered installer from a search result rather than an official source
2. engineer B trusted a fake recruitment process
3. engineer B downloaded and ran an untrusted repo into his WORK laptop, which is honestly the most strange of them.

text:
Ethereum is accelerating its post-quantum roadmap, now targeting a full transition by the end of 2028. This is a significant change from the previous timeline.

The technical direction:

1. Execution layer: Replace ECDSA with hash-based signatures, leanSPHINCS.
2. Consensus layer: Replace BLS signatures with hash-based leanXMSS.
3. Data layer: Replace KZG commitments with a post-quantum alternative, leanDA.

The common theme is hash-based cryptography, with SHA-3 as the current default hash function. It’s a conservative choice with well-understood security assumptions and good security margins, but comes with significantly larger signatures and proofs. leanVM is intended to make this practical through proof aggregation.

There's also the question of existing ETH.

Our analysis at Project Eleven found that roughly 72% of the ETH supply is associated with accounts that have already exposed their public keys. These funds would be vulnerable to a sufficiently powerful quantum computer capable of recovering private keys.

You can explore the exposure here: https://t.co/CRPJi34HgT

Moving ETH to a fresh address whose public key hasn't been exposed provides some protection, but it's not a long-term solution. Once that account broadcasts a transaction, its public key is exposed again. With estimates of quantum attacks potentially taking seconds or less, relying on a short mempool window is increasingly difficult to justify.

Ultimately, all ETH needs a path to quantum-resistant authorization, not just the 72% already exposed. This doesn't necessarily require waiting until 2028. Hash-based signature verifiers can already be deployed on-chain, albeit with significantly higher costs than native protocol support.

The cryptography is only part of the problem. Ethereum needs to ship the protocol changes, get wallets and infrastructure to support them, and make migration practical for everyone.

2028 is an ambitious target, but it's great to see the urgency.

author: stanleylee21
quoted_text:
Lending on Compute

Liquid Compute and K8 Capital are pleased to host Lending on Compute, an evening of conversation and connection in New York City on November 11, focused on GPU financing, compute markets and the credit behind them.

AI companies and infrastructure providers are committing unprecedented amounts of capital to compute, and how that capital gets financed is becoming one of the defining questions in credit. GPUs are emerging as a new asset class, with their own questions around valuation, depreciation, re-marketability and counterparty risk.

The market is also shifting quickly. Rental rates on older GPU generations have risen this year rather than falling as new chips arrive, challenging common assumptions about depreciation. At the same time, tighter capital markets are making long-term financing slower and harder to secure, leaving many neoclouds to fund large hardware deposits and bridge the gap to permanent financing. Lenders are rethinking how they underwrite the asset, and new pools of capital are looking for a way in.

Join @stanleylee21 , Chief Product Officer of Liquid Compute, and Chris Frissora of K8 Capital for a broad discussion of where compute financing stands today and where it is headed. Topics will include what recent pricing trends mean for GPU collateral, how lenders are underwriting GPU-backed loans, how tenor and pricing in the compute market shape credit risk, and the role of offtake contracts and prepayments. Stanley and Chris will also share some of the new structures Liquid Compute and K8 Capital have been developing together, from bridge financing to compute prepayments.

Join us to exchange ideas, meet potential lending partners, and connect with the people building the financial foundations of the compute economy.

Sign up: https://t.co/37MWKJrFIS

author: crypto_banter

text:
$NEAR is making a change to its token economics that I think deserves more attention.

HSP-029 has passed, with a proposal to reduce maximum annual issuance from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months.

On the surface, that’s a reduction in inflation.

But looking at it from an investor’s perspective, there’s a bigger question: can NEAR gradually move from relying on token emissions to an economy supported by actual network activity?

Here’s how I see it.

1. The supply side is changing

The proposal estimates 11.8M fewer NEAR issued over two years and 66.1M fewer over six years compared with keeping the current issuance schedule.

That’s a meaningful difference.

It isn’t a burn, and it doesn’t remove existing tokens from circulation. It means fewer new tokens enter the supply over time.

This matters particularly to holders who don’t stake. They receive no staking rewards, but still experience the dilution caused by new issuance.

2. There is a cost to reducing emissions

Staking rewards are also coming down.

Using the proposal’s September network snapshot, with 42.71% of supply staked, the model puts gross staking yield at approximately 5.27% under the current rate and 3.37% at the proposed target.

The validator side deserves equal attention. The model estimates that 24 of the 405 validator pools assessed could lose economic self-sufficiency at its $4.30 reference price.

That is a real trade-off.

Reducing inflation is good for the supply equation, but not if the network weakens the economics that support its security and decentralisation.

3. The demand side is where the wider ecosystem comes in

A lower issuance rate can slow dilution. It cannot create demand for NEAR by itself.

That demand has to come from people and businesses actually using the network.

This is why I look at NEAR Intents differently from a typical ecosystem announcement. Cross-chain transactions create activity and fees. Existing revenue mechanisms, including the fee-switch buybacks, connect some of that activity to NEAR’s token economics.

Then consider what Confidential Intents, NEAR Business and the agent economy could add.

Private financial operations, cross-chain treasury management and autonomous agents that need to transact are all potential sources of further activity.

None of this guarantees token appreciation. But it gives NEAR a route to building demand that is not solely dependent on speculation.

4. The bigger investment question

I don’t think the argument should be that reducing issuance automatically makes NEAR bullish.

The stronger argument is the combination:

Less new supply entering the market.

An ecosystem generating transaction fees and protocol revenue.

Existing buyback mechanisms continuing to operate.

More potential use cases across cross-chain finance, privacy and AI agents.

And a governance process willing to reconsider the network’s monetary policy as it matures.

The next challenge is proving that ecosystem growth can compensate for the reduction in staking incentives while keeping validators economically healthy.

My take

I’m more interested in the direction of NEAR’s economics than the headline percentage.

For years, crypto networks have competed for attention by issuing tokens and subsidising activity. The more difficult task is building products people continue to use when incentives are reduced.

That’s the test now facing $NEAR.

If Intents, privacy infrastructure, business finance and the agent economy translate into sustained usage and revenue, while validator participation remains healthy, then the lower issuance schedule could become an important part of a much stronger token model.

The vote is a meaningful step. Execution and actual demand will determine whether it becomes a meaningful investment catalyst.

That’s the part I’m watching and I won’t be sidelined for what’s to come

text:
How can we make lovable cities? If you had asked a European architect this question in 1900, they would probably have referred you to a slender, lively book by the Austrian writer Camillo Sitte, translated as ‘The Art of Building Cities’. Published in 1889, ‘The Art of Building Cities’ swiftly came to be revered around the world.

https://t.co/qwVmTrPTGV

Sitte was repudiated by the modernists and fell into obscurity, but his ideas are beginning to be revived. My cousin @PMArslanagic and I have distilled nineteenth century's finest work on urbanism into five principles:

- Create enclosed spaces
- Keep squares small
- Symmetry is overrated
- Move monuments to the edges of spaces
- Nestle monuments in vernacular fabric

Today we joined @Figure, @Securitize, Equiniti, and @centrifuge in a joint comment letter on the SEC’s transfer agent (TA) modernization proposal.  We support the long-overdue update and recognition of blockchain recordkeeping for tokenized securities, but urge a fully principles-based approach to securityholder identification and communication.

Mandating KYC, i.e. name + physical mailing address, as a baseline is an outdated method for investor protection.  Digital wallet addresses, emails, and other electronic identifiers can uniquely identify holders and enable reliable communication (often more effectively) especially for directly held tokenized holdings.  

We also recommended multi-channel contact for lost holders (not mandatory physical-address database searches) and that AML/BSA goals stay with FinCEN, not this @SECGov rulemaking.

This is why we call it the “Pilot In Command”

This happened in the same vicinity where the ill-fated Lear Jet hit the storm cell.

JetBlue pilot en route from Fort Lauderdale to Austin says to ATC:

“So you're gonna make us go through a, uh, severe thunderstorm?”

The captain then commanded the situation and overrode the ATC:

“So we declare an emergency, making a left turn heading 260 for severe weather avoidance.”

Sometimes piloting demands a specific set of traits - decisiveness, independent judgment, and the backbone to reject an instruction when it doesn’t feel right.

text:
Polymarket's resolution system is fundamentally flawed.

Two NBA markets were rugged by a malicious proposal that went unnoticed, causing >$306,379k of potential losses.

"Zach LaVin next team : Sacramento Kings" -> NO
"Fred VanVleet Next Team: Houston Rockets" -> NO

Despite both player signing for the mentioned teams.

> User Chims, holding 306k shares correctly proposes YES 
> Chims goes to sleep
> user ClarenceThomas, waiting for the last minute of the dispute window, proposes NO
> Chims isn't there to counter the dispute in time
> both markets resolve to NO automatically

This exposes a grave flaw in UMA's protocol.

UMA incentivizes user to dispute proposals with a $250 reward, but the bond is $750.

So in practice the only users taking the risk are whales with a lot of shares in the market.

If they are AFK for a few hours (happens often on small markets), blatantly wrong resolution can pass through without even going to a vote.

wouldn't it be better to just use centralized resolution at this point ?

quoted_text:
Long post worth the read. I have a close friend who flies private jets. He flew Lear 60 for over 15 years and now flies a Gulfstream. This is a copy and paste of his response to me asking him if I thought Ice was the issue. 

“We always fly in ridiculous cold temperatures.” 

“Usually you get the bad ice when the temperatures are like 0 to negative 20.  Believe it or not,  there's a point where it gets too cold for ice.   At negative 40, you pretty much can't get ice.   Besides that,  the airplane is equipped with hot wings and hot tail.”

“I flew the Lear 60 for like 15 years.   It's a no joke airplane and probably the most dangerous airplane I've ever flown.   It has a super critical wing.   The airflow has to be perfect.   When it gets into rough air and turbulence,  it will easily stall.   It has stalled on me at 41,000 feet just because we got into some turbulence.   (On the way to Palm Beach as a matter of fact. ) we recovered and got her flying again around 30,000 ft.   Scary

But here's the problem.   This airplane has a terrible coffin corner.   (At high altitudes)  what that means is,  you fly in a really narrow window where if you lose 20 knots,  it stalls.   And if you gain 20 knots,  it goes into overspeed.   The air goes supersonic over the wing and it goes into a high speed stall,  or worse,  a Mach tuck.   

So if you stall,  the normal recovery is to push the yoke forward to lower the nose and gain air speed again.   At low altitude,  you can push really hard and recover quickly.   But in the 60... if you push hard,  it will gain air speed and go into a high speed stall,  it doesn't take much.   It's very sensitive.  The 60 has super short wings that don't make much lift.   So then you high speed stall,  and the computer is yelling at you... OVERSPEED!   So then you pull back and enter a low speed stall.   And you go back and forth trying to keep it in the air speed window.   

This whole thing is pretty scary.   And you should recover basically by using your finger tips using super small corrections.   You can't over do it.   If you try to muscle the recovery, she gets mad and will become unrecoverable.  If she enters a mach tuck.  You're done.”

“I taught the Lear 60 to other pilots and mentored them.   I told them... this airplane has a soul and it's trying to kill you.   Do not ever try to top the weather.   Don't go over a thunderstorm.   Go around it.   If it means a half hour longer,  then do it.   Going over the thunderstorm will go into turbulence that you might not recover from.   

These pilots went right over a thunderstorm.   I think it stalled which caused them to drop down into the thunderstorm and ended up in mach tuck.   They picked up so much speed that it ripped off the horizontal stabilizer.   At that point... chuck Yeager can't fix it.   

These same pilots did something similar a couple months ago.   ATC got mad at them.   They poked the bear one too many times.   

This is not a beginner airplane.   The Gulfstream would never do this.   It has HUGE margins of error and won't stall like that.   But then again... it's got HUGE wings.   It's a pussy cat.  

The Gulfstream is like driving a 4 wheeler.   The Lear 60 is like riding a uni cycle.”

text:
Great convo with @luke10ferrari on his home turf in italy about irrational investor preference for growth over cash, invention vs. optimization, where durability lives after the saaspocalypse, and what happens to the org chart when AI writes 94% of your code.

Some takeaways:
- Investors seem to oddly dislike profit and greatly prefer growth - optimize for compounding free cash flow knowing that this is just a moment in time distortion.
- Invention vs. optimization: pick a camp. Invention has higher peaks but an awful median case. Google is still ~80% search 30 years later.
- Ambition in product, paranoia with debt. Rule #1 of becoming a huge success is not dying in the meantime & credit is a high wire act.
- Software has been cheap to build for a long time. Durability lives in habits, network effects, proprietary data and scale.
- SaaSpocalypse wasn't really about AI. In many cases these were poorly run companies and this cycle gave them an opportunity to improve.
- Bending Spoons went from 0% to 94% of code written by AI in two years. Support managers now look like PMs, data scientists build tooling instead of cleaning CSVs - everyone is both oddly more direct + giving more direction.
- If you're not winning when do you quit? No idea - bureaucracy created Bending Spoons b/c a Danish tax refund that never came killed Luca's first startup and catalyzed Spoons.

Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

text:
Anthropic has a 15-person chip design team and has told investors they are using Claude to design chips faster than Nvidia or AMD

Earlier this year at GTC, Nvidia’s Chief Scienst Bill Dally told Jeff Dean how Nvidia uses AI to speed up the chip design process:

▫️trained an LLM on all proprietary internal Nvidia docs over past 30+ years (junior employees query it instead of interrupting senior designers)

▫️one AI tool ports Nvidia’s cell library to a new semiconductor process and does it in only one night (used to take 10 employees up to 8 months, or 80 total person-months)

▫️since the 1950s, there’s been a classic chip design problem of where to place look ahead stages in a chain (AI is coming up with solutions using “bizarre designs thay no human” would think of)

▫️agentic AI systems are doing a ton of exploration…testing parameters spaces…suggesting new approaches…running architecture experiments 

▫️verification process is laborious but AI able to do it at fraction of time (compresses time from design to tape-out, with TSMC making chip)

Dally says it’s still a long way from end-to-end chip design but imagines a world where one master AI agents manages multiple sub-agents (similar to the current human-led process).

Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Thank you to our users for embracing a new way of working. Your constant feedback shaped so much of what we shipped and your stories made the work so meaningful.

Excited to see what you all make next!

刚刚，Binance 官方正式发布了关于 10 月 29 日 63 亿美元被盗事件的初步调查报告。

结论显示，这并非一次简单的“私钥泄露”，而是朝鲜黑客（FBI 调查认为吻合）潜伏数月、策划的一场有预谋的攻击。

报告透露了几个实战关键细节：

1.极致的社工骗局，连“HR”的社交日常都是伪造的
黑客在 9 月通过正规招聘平台盯上了币安的软件工程师。为了诱敌深入，黑客不仅安排了“项目总监”和“CEO”的多轮视频面试，甚至在面试中主动分享虚假的社交媒体照片和视频来建立信任。
最终，他们成功诱导该工程师在面试后，给自己的工作电脑上下载了伪装成“面试作业”的 0-day 恶意软件。

2. 内部 AI 工具沦为黑客的“内网跳板”

黑客在控制了首个工程师的电脑后，竟然直接利用币安的“内部 AI 工具”作为横向移动的跳板，顺藤摸瓜控制了另一位拥有核心权限的钱包 DevOps 工程师的设备，最终拿到了容器部署权限。

3. EIP-7702 与 MPC 机制，被坏人利用

在 10 月 29 日的最终收网阶段，黑客极其狡猾地利用了以太坊的 EIP-7702 机制（允许账户将执行权委托给智能合约，而无需暴露私钥）。

更让人感到无奈的是，币安热钱包所采用的 MPC（多方安全计算）机制，原本是为了消除单点故障、提升安全性，却在黑客发难的紧急时刻成了限制因素；
因为“没有单一私钥”，安全团队无法一键撤销黑客的恶意授权，反而拉长了阻断攻击的时间。

看完这个官方的报告，小编的感觉只有用防不胜防来形容了。

视频面试做局、大厂AI工具当跳板、反向利用 MCP 机制来拖延时间，原有的每一个环节都以意想不到的方式被巧妙的利用起来。

整个行业的安全假设确实需要重新审视了。

text:
THE DIESEL REPORT: UNDER THE HOOD 🔧🐻
Bears 34, Seahawks 17

Couple things I noticed Monday night that go deeper than the scoreboard.

1. Simmons is making everybody else’s job easier.

Interior pressure is worth its weight in gold. When a QB can’t step up, the edge rushers don’t have to win clean every snap. Simmons is forcing protection decisions before the ball’s even snapped. That’s how one big bastard changes an entire front seven.

2. Caleb’s best plays weren’t necessarily his biggest.

24/34, 247 yards. What I liked was the willingness to take the boring completion. There’s a time to play backyard ball, but against good defenses, you gotta learn to make your money on schedule.

3. Ben Johnson is making defenses defend every blade of grass.

Burden, Odunze, Loveland. Different skill sets, different ways to stress coverage. You can’t double everybody. Somebody’s getting a favorable matchup, and Caleb’s getting better at finding it.

4. The run game needs a wrench taken to it.

Swift’s three touchdowns look beautiful on paper. But 27 carries for 69 yards is 2.6 a pop. That’s not sustainable efficiency. Gotta find out whether the issue is blocking, defensive numbers in the box, or play design before January rolls around.

5. Third downs are where the defense earned its paycheck.

Seattle went 1/11. That’s not just good tackling. That’s winning early downs, putting the offense in predictable situations, and getting off the damn field.

DIESEL’S VERDICT:

The encouraging part isn’t that Chicago won by 17. It’s that there’s still plenty to fix and they handled business anyway.

That’s what good teams do.

KEEP THE TURBO SPOOLING. BEAR DOWN. 🐻⬇️

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

Polymarket's resolution system is fundamentally flawed.

Two NBA markets were rugged by a malicious proposal that went unnoticed, causing >$306,379k of potential losses.

"Zach LaVin next team : Sacramento Kings" -> NO
"Fred VanVleet Next Team: Houston Rockets" -> NO

Despite both player signing for the mentioned teams.

> User Chims, holding 306k shares correctly proposes YES 
> Chims goes to sleep
> user ClarenceThomas, waiting for the last minute of the dispute window, proposes NO
> Chims isn't there to counter the dispute in time
> both markets resolve to NO automatically

This exposes a grave flaw in UMA's protocol.

UMA incentivizes user to dispute proposals with a $250 reward, but the bond is $750.

So in practice the only users taking the risk are whales with a lot of shares in the market.

If they are AFK for a few hours (happens often on small markets), blatantly wrong resolution can pass through without even going to a vote.

wouldn't it be better to just use centralized resolution at this point ?

text:
As models automate more and more of the tasks involved in AI research, many people (myself included) worry this could dramatically accelerate progress and leave humanity with less control over the process.

When people say “recursive self-improvement” (RSI), it’s often unclear to me whether they mean just the automation piece or that whole scenario. I think the whole scenario is a plausible default. But importantly, these things can come apart.

For one thing, good old-fashioned human research could uncover a new architecture or a new way to scale that dramatically speeds up progress, without models doing any more of the work. On the flip side, it's possible you could fully automate AI research and find that progress hardly speeds up because the bottleneck is still waiting for experiments. And all else equal, at a given pace of progress, I think more automation is probably net good because it should leave people more time to understand the safety and alignment properties of the models, for operational excellence, etc.

Even if models are doing essentially all the research and progress is speeding up, I can imagine pretty different worlds. Say a country of geniuses in a datacenter thinks for a month and writes a four-page paper describing a much more efficient architecture. Humans pore over it, understand every detail, and decide to try it. The models train the successor and make a safety argument for using it that humans can actually understand and check. Alternatively, say the models are asked to produce their successor directly. They deliver one just as good, just as quickly, along with a spaghetti mess of code and an extremely convoluted safety argument that nobody can really follow. I think humans clearly have a lot more control over the process in the first world.

So I think we should be clear about what we mean when we talk about RSI and how we might put limits on it:
• How much of the research are models doing?
• How fast is AI improving?
• How much do humans understand about what’s happening, and how much control do we have over it?

When people talk about controlling RSI, I think they often jump to limiting how much models can help with research. But my guess is they’re often actually more concerned about the pace of progress and whether humanity can still understand and steer the research. I think there are legitimate reasons that controlling inputs may be easier than directly controlling outputs, but I think we should at least try to be clear about our goals and what we potentially gain (or lose) by optimizing a proxy.

text:
Polymarket's resolution system is fundamentally flawed.

Two NBA markets were rugged by a malicious proposal that went unnoticed, causing >$306,379k of potential losses.

"Zach LaVin next team : Sacramento Kings" -> NO
"Fred VanVleet Next Team: Houston Rockets" -> NO

Despite both player signing for the mentioned teams.

> User Chims, holding 306k shares correctly proposes YES 
> Chims goes to sleep
> user ClarenceThomas, waiting for the last minute of the dispute window, proposes NO
> Chims isn't there to counter the dispute in time
> both markets resolve to NO automatically

This exposes a grave flaw in UMA's protocol.

UMA incentivizes user to dispute proposals with a $250 reward, but the bond is $750.

So in practice the only users taking the risk are whales with a lot of shares in the market.

If they are AFK for a few hours (happens often on small markets), blatantly wrong resolution can pass through without even going to a vote.

wouldn't it be better to just use centralized resolution at this point ?

Bybit CEO: Exchanges Must Prepare for Hacks to Happen(ARCHIVE FOOTAGE)

On April 21, 2026, Bybit Co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou @benbybit reflected on the exchange's hack in an interview with The Block @TheBlockCo. He said one of the biggest shifts in thinking was moving from preventing attacks to assuming an attack will happen, minimizing the damage, and ensuring the company survives. 

He also discussed Bybit's previous reliance on a third party for its cold wallet. The exchange has since built a banking-grade hardware wallet system requiring staff to be physically present to unlock the HSM. However, such systems are costly and time-consuming to build, so most projects still need to rely on third parties. He said companies should address social engineering alongside technical security and build multiple layers of protection on the assumption that an attack will occur.

quoted_text:
Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

quoted_text:
Q&A: @audreyt & @VitalikButerin 

Ethereum’s priorities for the next decade
– first priority is surviving. institutions appreciate Ethereum not for speed, but for the fact the chain has never gone down. if Ethereum is not secure, it can’t make anyone else secure. if it’s not private, it can’t help anyone else be private. if it’s not open source, nothing built on top is open source
– stop doing: chasing 5% improvements when AI is turning everything over every year. chase the 5x instead. “helping people get 4.8% APY instead of 4.2% APY is fundamentally not interesting”. the applications that matter reduce the chance of a negative 100% APY. make simple and basic things good rather than hyper-optimising everything

fragmentation
– core R&D participation still has elements of being a social game. AI competitions may help: everyone who contributes is technically a core dev. anything that can be measured gets accelerated through AI; the things that can’t become the hard problem, but at least a smaller one
– privacy is the clearest example of taste-level fragmentation: data confidentiality, anonymity, metadata privacy, short-term privacy (front-running resistance), payment privacy, DeFi privacy... all different trade-offs with provable upper limits. sometimes different positions on the impossibility triangle are legitimate; sometimes a bigger solution turns the tribal warfare into a slider (even presenting the slider as common knowledge is progress, right now it feels zero-sum)

AI agents managing community treasuries
–a special case of the alignment problem, or “the ultimate problem facing humanity”. expects not one answer but a hundred answers each solving 1% of the problem
– any agent governing community assets sits in a sandbox, even when it has the keys: who picks the AI, who controls training, who decides on upgrades, who defines what counts as a big decision, what’s the process for feedback. those sandbox rules still have to be decided by people
– alignment by process: agentic systems earn trust by trusting the community more, not by a single designer setting rules from above

privacy vs transparency
– it’s about power asymmetry. concentrated power owes more transparency; lesser power is owed more privacy. the North Star is de-totalisation
– in practice, lines don’t get drawn by philosophers, they get drawn when two factions fight long enough, get tired, and need a peace settlement they can live with. that’s how the Magna Carta and the Peace of Westphalia happened
– influence it by building practical solutions that give more of the good kind of transparency and more of the good kind of privacy at the same time
– “be the agent you want to see in the world”

agents onchain
– audience question: if everyone can see how my agent works, scammers can too - does openness actually make it safer? answer: “I don’t think we want to put our agents on-chain”

P(doom)
– Audrey: “my P(doom) is NaN” - current model interpretability can’t read the neurons of very large models. visibility is zero; zero divided by zero is Not a Number
– on cyber apocalypse: it’s already happening. “assume breach” used to be a slogan; now anything you collect is probably already breached. the real apocalypse is the day all that leaked PII comes back to bite everyone

AI meets Ethereum (Vitalik)
– most excited: speed-running cryptography. the zero-knowledge proof singularity - a single ZKP verifying everything. indistinguishability obfuscation was always “30 years away”; AI is accelerating things he thought wouldn’t arrive for a quarter century
– most worried: “it’s like the dog-in-a-fire meme. we are the dog. the fire is creating diamonds that could go into chips and make everything awesome, but it’s also burning the house, and we have to take care of the house”

text:
蘇媽來救場啦！

AMD Q3 營收年增 45% 達 134 億美元，EPS 年增 74% 至 2.09 美元，都超越市場預期。

AMD 執行長 Lisa Su 在財報電話會議上表示：「Q3是我們歷史上規模最大、獲利最高的一季。在創紀錄的 Epic 和 Instinct 銷售以及強勁的嵌入式業務成長帶動下，EPS 成長速度甚至更快，提升了 74% 達到 2.09 美元。」

#2027年營收預估成長逾八成，化解基礎架構擴建疑慮
展望Q4， $AMD 預估營收將達 170 億美元左右（年增約 65%），高於市場平均預期的 162 億至 163 億美元。財務長 Jean Hu 指出，第四季資料中心業務季增預計達 50%，資料中心 AI 營收將首度超越伺服器業務。

對於 2027 年的全年展望，Lisa Su 給出遠超市場預期的指引：「根據我們目前的能見度，我們現在預期 2027 年營收將成長超過 80%，這是我們在去年 11 月財務分析師日所提出的長期財務模型的兩倍多。資料中心將成為最大的貢獻來源，營收占比預計將超過 80%。」

面對分析師針對電力、土地與晶片供應瓶頸的提問，Lisa Su 強調：「確實需求高於供給。我們持續與供應鏈夥伴合作擴充產能，以我們在整個生態系統中建立的深厚關係，我相信我們有絕佳的機會達成目標。我們手握史上最強大的產品組合，對於維持多年的高速成長與獲利擴張具備高度信心。」

#資料中心營收近翻倍，agent 浪潮推動 CPU 強勁需求
資料中心部門已占 AMD 總營收的 64%，該部門第三季營收年增 97% 達到 85 億美元。在伺服器端，雲端與企業端銷售額皆較去年同期翻倍，其中 agent 工作負載帶來了顯著動能。

Lisa Su 指出：「雲端供應商在這一季增加了大量的 Epic 產能來運行個人和企業 agent，這正迅速成為雲端 CPU 的下一個殺手級應用。Meta 的 Muse 和 OpenAI 的 Dots 展現了個人 agent 的快速普及，企業端也迅速將 agent 導入軟體開發、供應鏈與 IT 營運。」

她補充說：「導入才剛開始，隨著 agent 更廣泛部署並承接更複雜的工作，我們預期需求將大幅成長。」

除了 OpenAI 選擇 Turin Epic 作為其首款自研加速器的主機 CPU，AMD 也開始出貨 Epic Venice 處理器，並推出專為 agent 基礎架構設計的 Helion 參考架構。在全 CPU 配置下，單一 Helion 機櫃可容納多達 144 顆 Venice 處理器與近 7 萬 4000 個執行緒，具備極高的運算密度。

#Helios機櫃全面放量，收購 World Labs 拓展超級智慧
在資料中心 AI 加速器方面，AMD 開始放量出貨 MI455X，包含 Anthropic、Meta、Microsoft、OpenAI 及 Oracle 等客戶已迅速將首批 Helios 機櫃上線運行。Meta 的 Helios 機櫃已正式運作，AMD 也參與 Meta 10 億美元的增資，並承諾向即將進行 IPO 的 Anthropic 投資最高達 50 億美元。

在技術生態上，AMD 推出具備 agent 效能調校功能的 ROCm10 軟體，大幅縮短最佳化時間。同時，AMD 宣布收購低延遲推論晶片商 Talus，並以 82 億美元全股票收購由 AI 先驅 Fei-Fei Li 共同創立的 World Labs。Fei-Fei Li 將加入 AMD 擔任首席科學家，領導模型研究並協助規劃硬體、軟體與系統藍圖。

#零組件成本壓抑PC需求，產能彈性支援資料中心
PC 與遊戲部門第三季營收年減 8% 至 37 億美元。其中終端處理器營收年增 7% 至 29 億美元，但遊戲營收年減 40% 至 7 億 7300 萬美元。

高漲的記憶體與零組件成本正在壓抑 PC 市場買氣。Lisa Su 表示：「我們對 2027 年的規劃假設是整個 PC 市場出貨量將呈現雙位數百分比的衰退。但好處是我們的供應鏈在 PC 與資料中心業務之間具備相當好的彈性，這讓我們能夠根據市場訊號靈活調配產能。」

Exciting to see ZK finding its way into more real-world applications!

One question I’m particularly curious about: will this remain a research project, or could Anthropic eventually deploy it in production? @GiacomoFenzi @gwberg95 @miranda__christ @transmissions11 @RoyRinberg

How important is verifiable inference to model providers? Even with major performance improvements, proving will always come with some computational overhead. Perhaps a practical middle ground is periodic proofs, on-demand verification for paying customers, or even interactive proof systems.

More broadly, I believe we need a world where more things can be verified rather than simply trusted, from model execution to agent behavior and beyond.

The real question is where verifiability becomes valuable enough to justify its cost.

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

BREAKING: Elon Musk’s Starlink could dominate the global mobile and internet industry within three years, predicts Morris Group CEO Joseph Grinkorn.

THE PREDICTION

• Investment expert Joseph Grinkorn believes Starlink could change how billions of people access the internet and mobile services.

• He sees the next three years as a major opportunity for Musk to challenge traditional telecom companies.

WHY HE BELIEVES STARLINK COULD LEAD

• Global reach: Satellite internet can connect remote communities where reliable broadband is difficult to get.

• Direct to phone: Satellite connections through partner mobile networks can extend coverage beyond traditional cell towers.

• A huge customer base: The opportunity includes homes, businesses, governments, airlines, ships and remote industries.

• Stronger competition: As satellite services improve, traditional providers could face growing pressure to offer better connectivity.

• Musk’s track record: Grinkorn points to Tesla and SpaceX as reasons to take Starlink’s potential seriously.

THE NETWORK IS ALREADY HUGE

• Starlink reports more than 12 million people using its service across over 160 countries, territories and markets.

• SpaceX reported more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in orbit in October. That gives Musk an enormous network to keep building on. 

THE BIG PUSH INTO MOBILE

• Starlink has already launched more than 650 Direct to Cell satellites, bringing satellite connectivity to ordinary compatible mobile phones.

• SpaceX agreed to buy wireless frequencies from EchoStar in a deal originally worth $17 billion and later expanded to roughly $20 billion. These frequencies will support its next generation of satellite mobile services.

• The partnership also provides for EchoStar’s Boost Mobile customers to access Starlink’s next-generation Direct to Cell service.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT

• Growth in customers.
• More partnerships with mobile carriers.
• More satellite launches and improved capacity.

Grinkorn believes these developments could make Starlink one of Musk’s biggest achievements.

Whenever I point out how cheap something is in Japan compared to America everyone goes “yeah but their wages are much lower!”

Sure, but in Japan everyone can afford to go out to eat every night because it’s so cheap, people go out drinking multiple nights a week because it’s so cheap, airport beers are the equivalent of $1.50 and they consider that a scam.

Meanwhile in America no one goes out to eat anymore, no one goes out to bars anymore, and an airport beer is equivalent to minimum wage (plus tip!)

Sure we have more buying power *IF* we leave America, but comparing cost of living and wages in America vs Japan if you only spend inside your own country? Japan has us so beat it’s not even funny.

text:
卧槽！币安 63 亿美元被盗，竟然从一个员工跳槽开始，黑客前后布局近 4 个月！

币安最新公布的完整初步复盘，黑客盯上交易所员工，利用求职面试、恶意软件、内部 AI 工具，一步步从员工电脑渗透到核心钱包签名服务。

6 月开始铺线，10 月 29 日正式动手。

1️⃣ 黑客是怎么混进来的？

6 月，钱包运维工程师 A 搜索 AI 编程工具，下载了被篡改的 Homebrew 安装包。币安虽然发现异常、更换设备并轮换凭证，但攻击者已经掌握了钱包团队的岗位关系。

9 月，工程师 B 在正规招聘平台遇到假项目总监，先后经历 HR 视频面试、假 CEO 面试，对方甚至用社交账号和生活照片建立信任。最后以面试作业为由，让他把恶意代码仓库下载到工作电脑。

PS：这一个步骤就能暴露出很多问题，首先是员工非常不专业，这么敏感的岗位，私自下载未经审查的代码，显得很low。其次是交易所，对员工的电脑开发环境监控不够谨慎，尤其是掌控钱包领域的关键岗位，别说下载代码，点一个链接都必须要谨慎。

这个 0day 木马替换了合法开发工具组件，绕过了当时的终端安全防护，员工自己甚至没有察觉。

10 月 20 日，黑客利用 B 被控制的电脑和币安内部 AI 工具，横向渗透到 A 和工程师 C 的电脑，发现 A 电脑里有容器部署权限令牌。

10 月 29 日，黑客利用窃取的凭证登录 C 的电脑，部署容器、执行恶意脚本，最终摸进币安内部钱包签名服务。

2️⃣ 4 分钟搬走多少钱？

5 个热钱包在 4 分钟内转出 2.3346 亿枚 $XRP。

随后又转出约 97.05 万枚 $SOL、4420 万枚 $OP、18,270 枚 $BTC。

最后一笔 2961.9 枚 $ETH，直到近 4 小时后才最终上链。

整个事件涉及约 63.4 亿美元资产，其中约 28.5 亿美元被冻结或拦截。

3️⃣ 为什么币安暂停提现，黑客还能继续转账？

这里才是技术上最有意思的地方。

攻击者通过钱包签名服务提交了 50 笔签名交易，操纵账户 Nonce，利用以太坊 EIP-7702 机制，让自己控制的智能合约获得币安热钱包的部分执行权限。

问题来了：这些授权已经写入区块链，独立于币安正常提现系统。

暂停提现，只能关闭正常提现通道，无法自动撤销已经生效的链上授权。

4️⃣ 最尴尬的地方：币安热钱包本来就用了 MPC！

很多人以为用了 MPC（多方计算），就能防止私钥被盗。

但这次恰恰暴露了另一个问题：黑客没有必要直接拿到私钥，只要控制了能够调用签名服务的内部权限，就可能绕过正常的安全边界。

而且 MPC 没有单一私钥，币安无法直接用一把私钥撤销恶意授权，只能专门设计撤权流程。

最后一笔 ETH 转账在 23:56 UTC 才完成，30 日 00:10 UTC 才清除了 EIP-7702 委托。

MPC 能保护私钥，却不能替你保护已经失陷的员工终端和签名服务。

5️⃣ 币安现在怎么兜底？

币安承诺全部损失由平台承担，并且已经准备超过 100% 的覆盖资金。

截至 10 月 31 日，98% 受影响的代币资产已经补充，可以通过储备证明验证，剩余流动性较差的资产仍在购买。

截至 11 月 3 日，币安已经重建钱包系统和内部 AI 工具、更换受影响设备、废除相关凭证，并完成全员设备增强扫描。

FBI 最新信息将此次事件归因于朝鲜。今年币安安全团队已经检测并阻止了 57 起疑似朝鲜关联网络威胁。

6️⃣ 这次事故会给整个交易所行业带来什么？

我觉得接下来有几件事几乎是必然的：

① 交易所员工的设备权限会进一步收紧，尤其是钱包、运维和基础设施团队。

② 员工电脑的终端防护、异常行为监控、软件安装审计会全面升级，陌生代码仓库和开发工具将受到更严格管控。

③ 内部 AI 工具必须重新审视权限隔离。AI 工具一旦成为横向渗透的跳板，就可能把原本隔离的系统串联起来。

④ MPC、热钱包和签名服务需要重新设计应急撤权机制，不能只考虑如何防止私钥泄露，还要考虑授权被滥用后如何快速止损。

这次最让人后怕的，是攻击者甚至不需要直接攻破币安的核心钱包系统，只需要从一个员工的电脑开始，一层层拿到权限。

一个假招聘、一个恶意安装包，最后让整个行业为 63 亿美元的安全事故买单。

这名工程师恐怕也要承受巨大的心理压力。但真正该反思的，是为什么一个员工终端被攻破，最终能够一路触达几十亿美元级别的核心签名系统。

交易所的安全防线，不能建立在每个员工永远不犯错的假设上。

New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.

Here, we introduce FlashProve. Building on established cryptographic techniques, FlashProve allows developers to verify whether a given response came from a given AI model. It’s substantially more efficient than prior open-source methods for doing so. 

These proofs have a range of applications. They can, for instance, make it harder for attackers to hijack a chat, or enable safety evaluators to verify that the model they’re testing is the same one being served to customers.

For our full write-up, see here: https://t.co/OIZWPb6QZa

Further progress in provable inference will likely be an important part of improving trust in AI deployment. To that end, we're open-sourcing FlashProve’s code, here: https://t.co/7ky3Ir8V06

We’re grateful to our collaborators: Alessandro Chiesa, @GiacomoFenzi, @gwberg95, @miranda__christ, Rahul Dalal (https://t.co/pjWKLHWXyz) and Ben Mayer (@transmissions11).

quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

The best question I ask every single person on 20VC is:

“What do you know now that you wish you had known 12 months ago?”

My answer: the demand for inference is infinite. It is truly so much larger than any of us comprehend.

It will be very hard for neo-cloud providers to move into this market effectively.

We will have 3-4 specialised inference providers worth $300-$500BN in this market.

@modal is one of them. $1BN in ARR. $300M in sandbox revenue alone. WTF.

Erik @bernhardsson is also one of the coolest, most authentic people I have had the fortune of having on the show. Money on cos he is European! 😉

We sat down to shoot the s*** and my notes below.

1. Why I Hate the Description of Entrepreneurship as Pain and Eating Glass. That Is BS

Erik rejects the idea that building a company means suffering pain for a big reward at the end. He enjoys work every day, even the hard conversations, and hopes to work on Modal for 20 to 50 years. He has no wish to sell, saying he "would just go and start Modal 2."

2. Why the Days of 90% Software Margins Are Totally Gone

Almost no company today has the 90%-plus software margins common in Silicon Valley a decade ago. A dollar paid at the top of the stack flows through applications, models, infrastructure, cloud and NVIDIA, with each layer taking 20% to 30% gross margins. Erik sees Modal reaching 40% to 60% margins long term, but never software margins.

Are the days of 90% margins over or is this just the buildout phase of the new cycle meaning margin reduction @venkyganesan @AnjneyMidha

3. Why Inference Alone Will Become Commoditized, and You Have to Have a Suite of Products Around It

Selling inference alone is a commodity business with no switching costs and a race to the bottom. Erik argues it must come with post-training, sandboxes, agentic tooling, reinforcement learning, and low-latency and batch inference. Modal has spent five years building that infrastructure, which he calls very hard to copy.

Do you agree, inference will be commoditised and product breadth is the secret to retention @evishria @sarahcat21

4. Why We Will Have More Not Fewer Engineers in the Future

Every time programmers become more efficient, demand for software rises. Erik says the job was never translating English into code but understanding human requirements, and that work keeps moving up the stack, from assembly and punch cards to Python and now agents. He expects software engineers to be fine for the next 10 to 20 years.

What does no one see that everyone should see about the future of software engineering @matansf @pmarca @rabois

5. The Wildest Prediction on the Future of the Inference Market

The inference market has grown 10x to 100x bigger than Erik expected, and he predicts it will split into many specialized segments. He sees room for low-latency, high-latency, fine-tuning and post-training offerings, plus new hardware and technologies that need far fewer resources.

What is your wildest prediction on the future of the inference market @gavinsbaker @eladgil @romanchernin

6. The $15.75 Billion Company That Has Never Made a Pitch Deck

Modal has never made a pitch deck for any of its rounds. Erik gets to know investors well before raising and had spoken with Rich and Gonzalo at Accel for at least a year before the D round, so the deal came together very quickly.
