text:
Last night, my lawyers moved to sanction World Liberty Financial @worldlibertyfi for failing to disclose, until months into my litigation against the company, that it is a citizen of the UAE 🇦🇪 . #WLFI #USD1 

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

For banks, moving onchain has always meant choosing between public and private networks. They'd have to give up control on one or sacrifice liquidity and interoperability on another.

Tempo Zones ends that trade-off. Institutions can issue deposits on a private ledger they control that sits on top of Tempo’s mainnet liquidity.

Within its Zone, a bank operates a performant, enterprise-grade chain running Tempo’s software. Beyond its Zone, the bank maintains low-latency access to the public liquidity and interbank workflows that live on Tempo mainnet.

Anthropic 刚刚开源 FlashProve：以后 AI 有没有偷偷换模型，竟然可以用密码学验证了！ 🔥

你有没有想过：调用一个昂贵的 AI 模型，服务商是否可能在后台偷偷替换成便宜的小模型？

以前我们只能选择相信，现在 Anthropic 给出了新的解决方案！

FlashProve 是一个基于零知识证明（zkSNARK）的开源项目，核心能力非常惊艳：

✅ 模型身份验证：通过密码学证明 AI 的回答确实来自指定模型，而不是被偷偷替换。

✅ 保护模型权重：验证过程无需公开模型参数，兼顾商业机密与透明度。

✅ 普通 CPU 验证：用户无需运行原始大模型，就能独立核验推理结果。

✅ 形式化安全证明：使用 Lean 4 验证协议的核心安全性质，Claude 也参与了系统优化。

性能方面同样值得关注！

在 4000 亿参数的 Llama 4 Maverick 上，单张 H100 GPU 的证明生成速度约为 110 tokens/s，每 1024 token 的证明约 19 MB。

不过，目前仍是研究原型，证明过程需要普通推理约 70–95 倍的 GPU 时间，距离大规模商用还有距离。

这项技术的真正价值，是让 AI 服务从“相信厂商”迈向“密码学可验证”！

text:
Republicans are going to have a terrible night, and the simple reason why is that Trump has put up perhaps the worst *performance* this term of any president in a century or more.

Remember that he entered with an actual mandate: the House and Senate, a popular vote victory and a swing-state sweep, and 6-3 Supreme Court. Democrats were afraid enough to vote for mild but real immigration restrictionist legislation in the Laken Riley Act. Everyone wondered how far the "Vibe Shift" would go.

Trump managed to turn that into essentially zero durable wins whatsoever. He personally *hates* the very idea of legislation, the notion that he would have to spend time going back and forth with Congress, learning details and making compromises. So he simply didn't do it! He didn't make a compelling case for abolishing the filibuster. He didn't try communicating clearly to the public in support of popular bills to get to 60 votes. He just decided not to do it at all.

So they passed an unpopular tax cut, some funding for ICE, and a sop to the crypto industry, and that was basically it. Least productive Congress in decades, due to the tastes of one man.

Trump adopted one of the worst macro policies we've ever had: high deficits, high tariffs, and attacks on central bank independence. We managed to pay higher interest rates while still having high trade deficits AND weakening the dollar. Just a total failure.

On immigration, perhaps THE signature issue, Trump essentially min-maxxed effectiveness and backlash. Instead of trying to leverage the political moment for new laws and a self-deportation agenda (that is, walling off the economy to remove the benefit of irregular presence in the US), he opted for a maximally aggressive approach. The administration spent attention, funds, legal manpower on stunts like deporting random people to Salvadoran prisons with essentially no due process. ICE and Border Patrol were encouraged to be aggressive and confrontational, which helped contribute to the shooting deaths of American protestors. It turns out, that's extremely unpopular!

What about the approach of going after employers? The obvious vector? Trump hated that idea! He repeatedly has said he doesn't want to target businesses (especially farms) that use large amounts of illegal labor. This is just an incomprehensible position. Instead of charging a few dozen businessmen and removing the incentive for millions of illegal workers to be here, you arrest people off the street one by one at the cost of thousands of dollars in manpower per each, while their crying wives and kids post TikToks about it.

Upshot on immigration: electoral strength turned into a crippling electoral weakness in exchange for deporting maybe 6% of the illegally present population.

The tariffs were a total shitshow. Embarrassing rollout, no underlying theory of action at all. No targeted focus on key industries. Our country tariffed products we can't grow. We tariffed *inputs* of our own valuable exports. The schemes and amounts changed constantly, sending the stock market reeling and presenting scenes of chaos to the world.

Trump's messaging throughout has been generationally bad. While facing nearly 2:1 unpopularity, he spends his days posting AI slop, saying he'll rename New Mexico or invade allies, among other bizarre remarks. He brags about a ballroom and a pool repainting while gas hits records. At no point has he ever attempted any kind of message discipline.

Then there are the deeply unpopular attacks on rule of law, his "game-recognize-game" pardons for all manner of scammers and criminals, the crypto schemes that he and his family engage in, the evilly conceived and embarrassingly executed legal attacks on Comey, Jerome Powell, and others. With his monthslong stand on NOT releasing the Epstein files, he became maybe the first president ever to stake out a 99-1 issue on the 1% side.

text:
Alibaba's sales agent lifted conversion 15.8% in a live A/B test across 200,000+ merchants, without touching the model's weights.

It does outreach on 1688, Alibaba's B2B wholesale marketplace, where a deal usually takes several conversations. Most sales agents start every call from scratch.

SPAR treats each selling strategy as a hypothesis. It starts at 50/50 and its score moves toward its real success rate as results come in, so two lucky wins don't make it a favourite. If a merchant walks away because their budget got cut, an LLM marks that as external and it doesn't count against the pitch.

ExpeL, an earlier method that saves lessons as free-text notes, got +1.1% in the same test.

It's very similar to what we launched with Scout in June. You tell it the KPI you care about, it learns from every conversation, tests each change and keeps improving that number.

Optimising on business KPIs is the future for agents.

text:
A useful example of how DeFi lending markets respond to liquidity shocks.

What happened in 3F's wFalconX/USDC market on Morpho last week:

Oct 29, 20:05 UTC: Binance hot wallet compromise reported.

Oct 29, 22:00 UTC: Lenders withdrew liquidity. Utilization reached 100%, pushing borrow rates from 5.5% to 26%.

Oct 30: Collateral market reopened following confirmation of no impact.

Oct 31, ~02:00 UTC: Higher rates attracted liquidity back, with supply exceeding pre-incident levels.

Nov 2: A second, smaller rate spike to ~12% normalized within six hours.

Today: Borrow rates normalized with utilization at 87%.

The liquidity shock temporarily increased financing costs for leveraged positions, but higher rates incentivized lenders to return, restoring market liquidity.

Carry went negative for about a day, but doesn’t show up in the month’s results: the 6.5x vault is up about 1.15% vs about 0.58% for the unlevered NAV.

text:
终于知道外国人在opus5.5这么优秀情况下，还有这么多人订阅Codex了

说真的，Opus 5.5 确实很强。

尤其是在 Claude Code 里跑任务，执行果断、少废话，整个过程相当丝滑。

有段时间，我甚至觉得 Codex 可以退订了。

但真正把复杂业务、后端逻辑和大型项目交给它之后，我发现自己还是高兴得太早了。

Opus 5.5 赢在执行体验，GPT-6 Sol 和 Astra 则在我的复杂业务项目中更让我放心。

原因主要有两个：

1. 复杂业务逻辑，GPT 的全局理解能力更符合我的需求。

Opus 5.5 处理日常开发任务是真的舒服，执行效率高，也不用我反复催促。

但在我处理的一些复杂后端项目中，一旦涉及多模块联动、业务约束和超长上下文，它就容易开始顾此失彼。

让它改 A，结果影响了 B；让它修 B，又忘了 C 的约束。

看起来每一步都完成了，最后整个系统却没改对。

最折磨人的不是它不会写代码，而是它经常解决了眼前的问题，却没处理好整个业务系统的关联。

反复折腾半天，最后还得请 GPT 出山。

GPT-6 Sol 更适合我处理明确的业务需求和常规复杂开发，而遇到特别棘手、需要深入推理的问题，我会进一步交给 Astra。

当然，Sol 和 Astra 也不是完美的，有时候理解错需求，同样能把我气得够呛。

但只要把业务背景、约束条件和修改目标交代清楚，它们往往更能顺着整个系统的逻辑去分析问题，把反复折腾的任务真正收敛掉。

复杂开发最怕的不是模型慢，而是看起来一直在干活，实际上一直在返工。

2. ChatGPT 的深度研究能力，我是真的离不开。

这个功能甚至比写代码更让我舍不得退订 GPT。

比如我要研究一个陌生行业、一套技术架构，或者某个复杂产品的商业模式。

只需要在 ChatGPT 网页端描述清楚研究方向，启动深度研究，让它自己去跑。

过一阵子回来，它就能整理出大量参考资料、不同观点、技术路线和相对完整的分析框架。

当然，重要结论仍然需要核实。

但最让我惊喜的不是它能搜到多少资料，而是它经常能提出一些我自己根本没想到、但又非常值得研究的问题。

好的 AI 不只是回答你提出的问题，更重要的是帮你发现自己还没想到的问题。

我现在的结论越来越明确：

Opus 5.5： 日常高频开发、长时间连续执行，体验最舒服。
GPT-6 Sol： 业务逻辑明确、需要兼顾多个模块的开发任务，是我常用的攻坚选择。
GPT-6 Astra： 遇到特别复杂、反复修改仍无法解决的问题，作为最后的攻坚手段。
ChatGPT 深度研究： 资料搜集、技术调研和复杂问题分析，我依然离不开。

这不是标准化跑分，而是我连续一个月把它们放进实际工作流后的主观体验。

Claude 更像一个执行力极强的程序员，GPT 更像一个能啃硬骨头的技术合伙人。

最尴尬的是：

原本以为 Opus 5.5 能帮我省下一份订阅费，结果用得越深，越发现两个都舍不得退。

你们长期同时用 Opus 5.5、Sol 和 Astra 的，最后谁才是真正的主力？

text:
Chinese app design looks ugly on purpose.

If you open a Chinese app for the first time, you’ll probably think it’s badly designed.

Too many icons and features. Everything crammed onto one screen.

If you grew up on Western apps, your instinct is immediate: this is cluttered.

But it works.

In the U.S., we’ve been trained to associate good UX with minimalism. In China, density often signals value.

Open WeChat or Alipay, it feels overwhelming at first. Information-heavy, feature-packed.

But to local users, that density means capability. It says: everything you might need is already here in front of you.

If you enter a new market assuming your design taste equals good UX, you’ll misread the signal.

Good design is contextual.

text:
别再沉迷让 Sub-agent 互相 Review 代码了——你以为是“左脚踩右脚上天”，其实是“左手掏右手钱包”。🔥🤖

太赞同 poteto 小姐姐今天的说法了！！

她直言对抗式代码审查（Adversarial Review）大多是在纯烧 Token，不仅大幅砍掉了 pstack 里的 interrogate 技能，还打算把省下的算力全砸向“实测 + 形式化验证”。

跑过自动化 Agent 工作流的人都懂，静态的 AI 代码互审有三个近乎无解的死穴：

▸ 没苦硬吃：Reviewer 为了证明自己“干活了”，没 Bug 也要硬挑一堆可有可无的代码风格问题（Nitpicking）。
▸ 过度设计（YAGNI）：为了应付 Reviewer 脑补出来的“极端假设”，主 Agent 会疯狂往代码里塞毫无必要的抽象层和防御逻辑，越改越臃肿，上下文越滚越脏。
▸ 算力错配：用最贵的推理 Token 去“猜”代码会不会报错，却不用免费的编译器和 Linter 去直接跑一下。

一边是 xAI 工程师砍掉模型互撕、回归硬核验证；另一边是今天 OpenAI 和 Muse 狂提赏金、直接花钱买外部黑客打系统找 Bug。

顶级团队都在用行动投票：两个大模型在终端里吵一万句，不如测试框架红一次，更不如真实红队来一拳。

你的工作流里，AI 审查员到底是在帮你抓真漏洞，还是在帮你刷 API 账单？

For those who are new to this dispute, I was one of World Liberty’s earliest and largest investors.  In November 2024, I agreed to buy $30 million of $WLFI tokens under a Token Purchase Agreement with World Liberty, and I later increased my total investment to $45 million. 

In April, I sued World Liberty, alleging that the company induced my investment through fraud and then unlawfully froze my tokens.

My Token Purchase Agreement gives me the right to bring my claims in either California federal or state court.  

I chose federal court.

Federal courts can hear a case like mine only when the two sides come from different places.  Foreign plaintiffs like me can sue an American defendant in federal court, but foreign plaintiffs generally cannot sue a foreign defendant there.  For these purposes, a company like World Liberty takes on the citizenship of each of its owners, so a single foreign owner makes the company foreign.  

In other words, so long as World Liberty and all of its owners were American, my case could be heard in federal court.

The federal court’s rules required World Liberty to file a disclosure at the start of the case identifying every one of its owners and where each is a citizen.  World Liberty’s disclosure identified only one entity—World Liberty itself—and listed Florida as its sole citizenship.  Its lawyers certified that they were unaware of anyone else who needed to be disclosed.

World Liberty then moved to compel arbitration, seeking to pull my case out of open court and into secret arbitration proceedings. 

I opposed that motion, and my lawyers spent months and hundreds of thousands of dollars fighting it.  At a hearing in August, the Court signaled that it was not persuaded that my claims belonged in arbitration.  Instead, the Court ruled that certain of my claims should stay in open court, and certain claims should be sent to arbitration, and ordered the parties to meet and confer to come up with a proposed agreement on which claims stay in open court and which ones go to arbitration.

Less than a week later, World Liberty suddenly “corrected” its disclosure.  Where it had previously listed only one member in its ownership chain, it now listed 22, and claimed citizenship in Florida, Delaware, Puerto Rico, and the UAE.  

World Liberty now says that the federal court has no jurisdiction over my case, since its UAE citizenship means there are foreign parties on both sides of the case.

The irony is hard to miss.  World Liberty’s gold paper declares that “[b]y design, World Liberty Financial is not organized offshore,” and that it is “an American, tax-paying, corporation that aims to bring DeFi to its rightful home—America.”  It promises a “US-based decentralized platform” built on “American ideals of liberty, privacy, and freedom to transact,” calls private, intermediary-free transactions “a core American value,” and boasts that “[r]ather than shying away from the United States, World Liberty Financial embraces the United States as the future CRYPTO CAPITAL OF THE PLANET.”

World Liberty was proudly American 🇺🇸 when it was selling tokens.  It discovered its UAE 🇦🇪 roots only when it needed a way out of an American federal courtroom.

World Liberty presumably always knew who its owners were.  Its lawyers claim that they learned about the company’s UAE citizenship only after they filed the original disclosure.  

As my motion explains, if that is true, then either World Liberty’s lawyers failed to conduct appropriate diligence, or World Liberty did not give its lawyers a straight answer.  When we asked how this happened, World Liberty refused to tell us.

Token holders deserve to know whether the projects they invest in are telling the truth, both to the public and to courts.  I am filing this motion to hold World Liberty and its lawyers accountable for what I believe was a misleading disclosure to the Court, and to make sure that the cost of World Liberty’s gamesmanship falls on them, not on me.  

And after my sanctions motion is resolved in federal court, I will re-file my lawsuit against World Liberty in California state court.

I will keep fighting for the transparency this community deserves.

Astra 好强！

只改万分之一点六的参数，小模型数学分直接翻好几倍。

MIT CSAIL 11月2日发文《Weight-Space Programming》：让 GPT-6 Astra 不靠梯度、不训练，直接读写神经网络权重。对 Qwen3.5-0.8B，Astra 只改约 0.016% 权重（131,072 个），修掉推理循环。同样采样设置下，MATH-500 从 7.9% 升到 48.1%，GSM8K 13.8%→67.1%，指令跟随 IFEval 21.0%→62.3%；撞 token 上限比例从约 93% 降到约 33%。Ethan Mollick 转评称「等复现，但分量很大」。

这对中国年轻人意味着什么：以后调模型不一定非得会训、会堆卡，能读懂权重行为、会下精确改动指令的人，也可能切入模型优化这条路。小模型端侧部署也会更香——修好一个卡点，就能把现成能力释放出来。

你觉得「直接改权重」会先成批量工具，还是长期只停在实验室演示？

海外 StarSkirmish 星际争霸 AI 挑战赛落幕，OpenAI 的 GPT-6 Astra 智能体发挥拉胯，直接暴露出通用大模型在博弈对战上的短板。

比赛里 GPT-6 Astra 没有靠自己算力去推导对战策略，反而直接调用人类写好的顶尖对战机器人 Stardust 上场，最后还是输给专门做对战的专业 AI。

这个结果打破了很多人的固有印象：不是通用大模型就能碾压所有专项 AI。通用大模型擅长写文字、回答问题，但是面对这种实时对抗、局势随时变化、变量极多的博弈场景，很容易出现决策漏洞。

业内分析，后续大模型想要突破，必须加强实时场景推演、自主调整策略的能力，才有机会用到工业、复杂决策这类高要求场景。

text:
I’ve been talking about Bitcoin since 2017. I was early, especially for my age group.

A lot of things attracted me to it. Part of it was the digital gold thesis. I thought that made sense, and in many ways, it still does.

But one of the things that makes Bitcoin unique is that there’s no CEO, no bank, no third party. And that’s also what makes it risky.

With a bank, there’s FDIC insurance, fraud investigations, sometimes reversals. With Bitcoin, that’s gone by design.

And for years I bought into “not your keys, not your coins.”

But here’s what I’ve learned the hardest possible way.

I was hacked, and everything in my cold wallet is gone.

I don’t know exactly how it happened, and I can’t go into detail because I’ve reported it to the FBI. Even after almost two months, I haven’t heard back.

Over half my net worth disappeared.

I’m embarrassed because I considered myself savvy. I watched phishing attempts, scams, and reports of wallet security failures, and I still thought I was careful enough.

I wasn’t.

If you’re someone who followed me early and you’re sitting on life-changing gains, don’t assume a single wallet will save you.

I now believe having millions in a wallet you alone control is too risky.

If I could do it over, I probably would have diversified custody, maybe even accepted some third-party risk with a regulated custodian.

That’s why today’s conversation matters.

We’re talking about Bitcoin security with Jameson Lopp @lopp, co-founder and Chief Security Officer of Casa, because if self-custody is still part of your plan, you need to understand the trade-offs.

We’ll also discuss the emerging quantum-computing threat and what Bitcoin holders should understand about preparing for it.

Because losing money on a bad investment is one thing. Losing money on an investment you got right, simply because you failed to protect it, is something else entirely.

With that, here’s my conversation with Jameson Lopp.

quoted_text:
Republicans are going to have a terrible night, and the simple reason why is that Trump has put up perhaps the worst *performance* this term of any president in a century or more.

Remember that he entered with an actual mandate: the House and Senate, a popular vote victory and a swing-state sweep, and 6-3 Supreme Court. Democrats were afraid enough to vote for mild but real immigration restrictionist legislation in the Laken Riley Act. Everyone wondered how far the "Vibe Shift" would go.

Trump managed to turn that into essentially zero durable wins whatsoever. He personally *hates* the very idea of legislation, the notion that he would have to spend time going back and forth with Congress, learning details and making compromises. So he simply didn't do it! He didn't make a compelling case for abolishing the filibuster. He didn't try communicating clearly to the public in support of popular bills to get to 60 votes. He just decided not to do it at all.

So they passed an unpopular tax cut, some funding for ICE, and a sop to the crypto industry, and that was basically it. Least productive Congress in decades, due to the tastes of one man.

Trump adopted one of the worst macro policies we've ever had: high deficits, high tariffs, and attacks on central bank independence. We managed to pay higher interest rates while still having high trade deficits AND weakening the dollar. Just a total failure.

On immigration, perhaps THE signature issue, Trump essentially min-maxxed effectiveness and backlash. Instead of trying to leverage the political moment for new laws and a self-deportation agenda (that is, walling off the economy to remove the benefit of irregular presence in the US), he opted for a maximally aggressive approach. The administration spent attention, funds, legal manpower on stunts like deporting random people to Salvadoran prisons with essentially no due process. ICE and Border Patrol were encouraged to be aggressive and confrontational, which helped contribute to the shooting deaths of American protestors. It turns out, that's extremely unpopular!

What about the approach of going after employers? The obvious vector? Trump hated that idea! He repeatedly has said he doesn't want to target businesses (especially farms) that use large amounts of illegal labor. This is just an incomprehensible position. Instead of charging a few dozen businessmen and removing the incentive for millions of illegal workers to be here, you arrest people off the street one by one at the cost of thousands of dollars in manpower per each, while their crying wives and kids post TikToks about it.

Upshot on immigration: electoral strength turned into a crippling electoral weakness in exchange for deporting maybe 6% of the illegally present population.

The tariffs were a total shitshow. Embarrassing rollout, no underlying theory of action at all. No targeted focus on key industries. Our country tariffed products we can't grow. We tariffed *inputs* of our own valuable exports. The schemes and amounts changed constantly, sending the stock market reeling and presenting scenes of chaos to the world.

Trump's messaging throughout has been generationally bad. While facing nearly 2:1 unpopularity, he spends his days posting AI slop, saying he'll rename New Mexico or invade allies, among other bizarre remarks. He brags about a ballroom and a pool repainting while gas hits records. At no point has he ever attempted any kind of message discipline.

Then there are the deeply unpopular attacks on rule of law, his "game-recognize-game" pardons for all manner of scammers and criminals, the crypto schemes that he and his family engage in, the evilly conceived and embarrassingly executed legal attacks on Comey, Jerome Powell, and others. With his monthslong stand on NOT releasing the Epstein files, he became maybe the first president ever to stake out a 99-1 issue on the 1% side.

That's not even getting into Iran, DOGE, his candidate recruitment choices, or countless other things. Simply put: Trump has managed to royally screw up virtually every single facet of his presidency. It's been undeniable, voters have noticed, and there's really no escape from it. This is what the GOP base chose in early 2024, and this is the world they're living with now. Where they handed the reins of history to a fat, vain, washed-up old man and let him drive.

.@dylan522p says a common misconception is that most AI spend in the hard sciences is going toward discovery, when in reality the vast majority is going to engineering. 

He explains why that's a good thing:

"You have to get really good at the engineering before you can discover something and bring it to market."

"It's not about inventing a new material. In semiconductors, if you improve the deposition of something, and so then your chip has less resistance, or you can shrink it a bit further, that's so much economic value that is *immediately* delivered."

"Chips sit on substrates. Substrates route the wires in and out, and power in. The substrates for CPUs — the yields there are in the range of 40 to 60%. What if those yields become 95%? The economic value that's generated is massive."

"Or take an Intel fab. Its fab yields are lower than TSMC. If its yields are all of a sudden higher than TSMC, or equivalent, the economic value that can be delivered is massive."

cz在发言中说：“如果交易所可以被黑客攻击，那么银行风险更高”
我说句粗糙的话：杀一个人的技术和能力人人都有，但一个国家的凶杀率，取决于国家政治治理能力。
技术和风险是两码事，
银行和加密货币面对犯罪时，风险结构完全不同。
真正阻止大多数人抢银行的，不是保险柜技术，而是抢完银行之后需要承担的代价。
同样是抢劫，在不同司法体系下，犯罪成本可能天差地别
决定安全的是抢完以后会有什么代价
两种货币体系更重要的区别：信用。
银行体系背后有国家法律、金融监管、存款保障条款，以及明确的责任主体。
而去中心化加密货币依赖的是共识机制。
中心化信用出了问题，你至少知道应该向谁追责。会负责到什么程度。
去中心化共识出了问题，但没有人有义务替你承担损失。币安的承担不是出于义务，而是出于生存需要。这很重要。币安也只是个交易所，他能因为经营需要承担交易所的内的损失。不代表整个虚拟货币行业有人负责。
一个劫匪拿刀架在你脖子上，让你转走100万美元加密货币，可能几分钟就完成了。但让你从银行立刻转走100万美元，恐怕没那么容易。
你如果去美国银行黑走60亿美元，美国一定要对公众有一个交代，但如果是交易所，美国需要一个交代表达自己对全世界的安全负责，也有权力干涉。
这个一定要负责，和需要权责对等是两件事。
我认为金融安全，讨论技术能不能被攻破。没有意义。
真正的安全，不是有没有人能拿走你的钱，而已是别人拿走你的钱之后，需要付出什么代价，以及谁有责任保护你。
自由是加密货币的优势，
这也是他的最大价值。
但自由不等于安全。
没有明确的责任主体，
也不代表风险就消失了。
而是风险最终全部落到了持有人身上。
如同我们回到
“物竞天择适者生存”的石器时代
每个人独立对自己生命负责
而不是集体。

（为了避免二圣看的心烦，各位自己加戏意淫我要发币，我就先把二圣拉黑了）

419名客户中招，427笔异常转账，单笔约10万新台币，总金额超过4000万新台币。

所有资金竟然全部转入了台湾台北富邦银行的同一个账户。

受害者表示，自己根本没有打开银行App，也没有进行任何转账操作，部分交易记录却显示经过了人脸扫描验证。甚至有人根本没有设置约定账户，也照样发生了资金转出。

目前永丰银行称事故源于新网银系统程序异常，已暂停相关服务并全额垫付退款。

text:
当 Agent 帮你干活，我们该思考什么？来自 Claude Code 团队的 Addy 分享的这篇虽然是拿 Coding 做例子，但这个方法可以衍生到任何 Agent 工作。模型越强，批判性思维越难，而且难的方式跟大家预想的不一样。明显错误越来越少，大多数输出都不错，而且你同时跑多个 Agent，但只有一双眼睛，在这种舒服的状态下就会放松警惕，所以批判性思维得刻意排进日程👀 首先要警惕认知滑坡：

- 卸载：把任务交给 AI，但结果仍归你负责；
- 延迟：工具输出直接成了你的下一步输入，不再是假设;
- 投降：AI 的输出悄悄变成你自己的观点，你不觉得需要检查;

人会一步步往下滑，每一步都很小、都显得合理，所以很少有人察觉。如果你连借助 agent 都解释不清这个答案，你这时就已经交出了所有权。因此，要把判断力放在任务两端：

1. 事前定义：先写自己的假设，明确目标、边界与完成标准。对于任何架构和执行性的工作，我会和 Agent 一同完成设计说明。这样我们双方都知道接下来会做什么，以及完成标准是什么？

2. 事中执行：Agent 生成与迭代，让验证进入执行循环。分步骤地让 Agent 输出中间产物，我们可以确定部分的执行结果是否正确。如果连续有效，就可以放心大胆执行；

3. 事后验证：先看证据，再看总结，审查隐藏的假设与决策。一定要校验 Agent 的执行结果，可以用另外的模型来阅读执行文档和中间产出的 log 记录，来双向校验。

交付前的最终门槛：我能解释它，也愿意为它署名负责吗？产出不应超过审查能力，持续练习不愿失去的技能！

quoted_text:
New Study: ChatGPT Ads Are Getting Crushed by Google - So Much for OpenAI Making Google the Next Yahoo

Lately, there has been a lot of talk about ChatGPT doing to Google what Google did to Yahoo. A new study suggests that's not exactly imminent. The reason: OpenAI's ads aren't delivering.

Researchers Maximilian Kaiser and Christian Schulze examined ChatGPT's advertising performance, and the numbers aren't pretty.

Google is eating ChatGPT's lunch

US visitors from ChatGPT ads generated $0.89 in revenue per visit, versus $2.45 for Google Search ads – 64% less. Conversion rates were 0.37% versus 1.17%. Among 87 advertisers using both, 73 recorded zero ChatGPT-driven purchases. The researchers estimate a ChatGPT click is worth about $0.26 if advertisers want Google's return on ad spend. One advertiser reportedly paid $1.72 per click. Oops.

Could ads be hurting ChatGPT?

The study estimates that ads reduced organic referrals from ChatGPT to shopping sites by 6 - 8%. So OpenAI may be sacrificing some organic traffic while selling ads that deliver weak returns. Awkward for a company counting on advertising to help pay its enormous AI bills.

Google shouldn't celebrate yet

Google has spent two decades perfecting the monetization of commercial intent. ChatGPT ads are barely nine months old.

Also, the two services have different audiences. Someone Googling running shoes may be ready to buy. Someone asking ChatGPT for marathon training advice may still be debating whether running is a terrible idea. Comparing the two risks confusing discovery with purchase intent.

Conversational AI could eventually capture purchase intent earlier in the customer journey. Google's push to put ads in AI Mode suggests it takes that possibility seriously, suggesting that OpenAI may be able to figure out how to deliver better performance.

Strong study, important caveats

The researchers analyzed nearly 10 billion visits across 1,898 websites over 60 weeks, comparing markets with ChatGPT ads against an ad-free European control group.

But the paid-ad analysis covers only 102 advertisers, with just one of them accounting for 66% of ChatGPT ad purchases. Also, Website sales attribution may miss later purchases and brand effects. The study remains observational and under peer review.

What advertisers should do

Test ChatGPT ads, but measure incremental sales, allow longer conversion windows and demand prices grounded in performance. Early-adopter bragging rights aren't a KPI.

@Google, @OpenAI, @Yahoo

text:
想证明自己的交易所账户开了半年以上、交易量过了某个门槛，又不想交出账号和流水，已经有项目在做，做这件事的是 Primus。

它是什么：Primus（@primus_labs）给自己的定位是「机构链上金融的机密基础设施」，核心是两样技术：

· zkTLS：你登录网站时，浏览器和网站之间走加密通道，地址栏那把小锁就是 TLS。zkTLS 在这条通道上生成一份证明，说明「这条数据确实来自这个网站」，对外只公开你要证明的结论，原始数据不外传。
· FHE（全同态加密）：数据全程加密，合约不用解密也能对它做加减、记账。

解决什么问题：公链上每个地址的余额、仓位、对手方都公开。散户无所谓，机构的调仓一旦被看见，就可能被人抢在前面。另一边，交易所记录、支付流水这些链下数据很有用，可要么交出去，要么用不上。Primus 的做法是在现有公链上补一层隐私和验证，不另起一条新链，省掉新链从零拉用户的成本。

谁在用（日期和出处在括号里）：
· ZKredit（BNB Chain 官方博客，3 月 25 日）：Primus 和 Brevis 合做，用户通过浏览器插件登录交易所，证明「账户超过 6 个月」「交易量达到门槛」，证明记到链上供借贷协议查询，原始数据不上传。
· Perena 的稳定币 USD*（Primus 官方帖，4 月 10 日）：储备金由 Primus 的 zkTLS 加 Brevis 的 zkVM 在链上持续验证，策略细节不公开。
· Confidential Vault（Primus 官方长文，8 月 26 日）：在 BNB Chain 上把稳定币 U 按 1 比 1 换成加密版 eU，转账照常上链，金额和余额不以明文显示；存进金库后，和公开金库走同一个 Unitas 收益市场。官方称上线 24 小时存入超过 100 万美元。

我的判断：Primus 藏的是数字，不藏行为。转账这件事照样上链可查，看不见的是金额和余额。这条路比完全匿名更容易让合规机构接受，它把自己定位成机构基础设施，底气也在这里。

还没想通的一点：zkTLS 的证明要由第三方节点（官方叫 attestor）参与生成，信任从「交出账号」转到了「相信这些节点如实签名」。机构和监管愿不愿意认这层节点，我还没看到公开答案。

下次遇到要你交账号或截图才能通过的验证，可以先找找有没有这种只交结论的做法。

Primus 积分任务入口：https://t.co/gTCaBnDkwm

quoted_text:
Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
First, congrats to all $AMD bulls. I got too bearish from reading daily tapes.

AMD的Client和Gaming在四季度同样被指引环比暴跌超过20%，跌幅和 Intel 一模一样，但 AMD 把可通用的晶圆和封装产能直接转给了供不应求的数据中心，让 Q4 数据中心环比暴增约50%至128亿美元。Lisa is a fucking goat and Intel is the only incompetent one.

Intel在财报里承认受制于基板（substrate）产能不足，守着需求却交不出货 。而AMD从今年二季度看到需求拐点开始，就提前锁定了晶圆、基板和后端封装产能，甚至在三季度砸了近300亿美元的采购承诺 。结果就是同一个x86服务器紧缺周期里，Intel被卡住脖子，AMD把溢出的份额全吃进了自己的报表。

PC去库存是真的，但对AMD只是皮外伤。AMD的Q3 Client收入29.5亿美元，环比跌了5%，低于预期 。这说明OEM清库存是全行业现象，AMD也没有完全躲过。但区别在于，数据中心已经占到AMD总营收的64%（Q4还会升到70%以上），且手握380亿美元级别的AI GPU增量 。Intel没有AI GPU，数据中心体量又压不住PC的窟窿，再加上代工业务烧钱，所以PC一去库存，Intel全公司指引直接崩盘。而AMD在Q4靠数据中心单季就能多干出30多亿美元的环比增量，把PC的几个亿缺口直接填平还富余一大截 。

看一下这个算术最惊人的地方：
仅仅按 Q4指引（170亿营收、55%毛利率、37.5亿 OpEx、13%税率、16.7亿股）算出来的Q4 单季Non-GAAP EPS 就高达 2.92 美元，年化已经是 11.7 美元。而到了2027年，哪怕我把毛利率压到 55%，营业利润率也会从 Q3 的 29.3% 一路扩张到 2027 年的35.3%，直接把基准 EPS 推到 17.55 美元（市场共识之前只有15.6左右）。卖方此前哪怕最激进的 Wedbush 和 Bernstein 也只敢给810–850亿美元营收和14.7–15.7美元 EPS。

So new base case 17.55 EPS implies the following valuation:
- 30x（核心安全边际区）：526 美元
- 32x（合理价值中枢）：562 美元
- 34x（合理价值上沿）：597 美元

如果建/加，500-525就是第一档区域。如果明天开盘受大盘影响回踩则更优！

🇪🇺 The EU is telling 450 million people to pack an EMERGENCY bag.

And it has put “payments” on the same list as food, water and medicine.

On November 3, Brussels unveiled new crisis guidelines. 

The rule: every household should be able to survive the first 72 hours of an emergency on its own, with a grab bag ready to go.

The 7 things the EU says you NEED to cover:

1. Food
2. Water
3. Heat and light
4. Medication
5. Hygiene
6. Information
7. Payments

Why payments?

Because card machines and banking apps NEED power and internet.

In April 2025, when Spain and Portugal lost power, card terminals went dark and people queued at cash machines that still worked.

Some countries are already going FURTHER than Brussels:

• Sweden tells people to cope on their own for a full week

• The Netherlands raised its advice from 48 hours to 72

• France published a 27-page survival guide

The EU even wants an annual Preparedness Day, starting October 23, 2027.

The guidelines are non-binding. Brussels says the goal is to avoid panic, not cause it.

But the message is clear. People are expected to have a way to pay that doesn’t depend on the grid.

If the power went out tomorrow, how would you pay for anything?

text:
Long post worth the read. I have a close friend who flies private jets. He flew Lear 60 for over 15 years and now flies a Gulfstream. This is a copy and paste of his response to me asking him if I thought Ice was the issue. 

“We always fly in ridiculous cold temperatures.” 

“Usually you get the bad ice when the temperatures are like 0 to negative 20.  Believe it or not,  there's a point where it gets too cold for ice.   At negative 40, you pretty much can't get ice.   Besides that,  the airplane is equipped with hot wings and hot tail.”

“I flew the Lear 60 for like 15 years.   It's a no joke airplane and probably the most dangerous airplane I've ever flown.   It has a super critical wing.   The airflow has to be perfect.   When it gets into rough air and turbulence,  it will easily stall.   It has stalled on me at 41,000 feet just because we got into some turbulence.   (On the way to Palm Beach as a matter of fact. ) we recovered and got her flying again around 30,000 ft.   Scary

But here's the problem.   This airplane has a terrible coffin corner.   (At high altitudes)  what that means is,  you fly in a really narrow window where if you lose 20 knots,  it stalls.   And if you gain 20 knots,  it goes into overspeed.   The air goes supersonic over the wing and it goes into a high speed stall,  or worse,  a Mach tuck.   

So if you stall,  the normal recovery is to push the yoke forward to lower the nose and gain air speed again.   At low altitude,  you can push really hard and recover quickly.   But in the 60... if you push hard,  it will gain air speed and go into a high speed stall,  it doesn't take much.   It's very sensitive.  The 60 has super short wings that don't make much lift.   So then you high speed stall,  and the computer is yelling at you... OVERSPEED!   So then you pull back and enter a low speed stall.   And you go back and forth trying to keep it in the air speed window.   

This whole thing is pretty scary.   And you should recover basically by using your finger tips using super small corrections.   You can't over do it.   If you try to muscle the recovery, she gets mad and will become unrecoverable.  If she enters a mach tuck.  You're done.”

“I taught the Lear 60 to other pilots and mentored them.   I told them... this airplane has a soul and it's trying to kill you.   Do not ever try to top the weather.   Don't go over a thunderstorm.   Go around it.   If it means a half hour longer,  then do it.   Going over the thunderstorm will go into turbulence that you might not recover from.   

These pilots went right over a thunderstorm.   I think it stalled which caused them to drop down into the thunderstorm and ended up in mach tuck.   They picked up so much speed that it ripped off the horizontal stabilizer.   At that point... chuck Yeager can't fix it.   

These same pilots did something similar a couple months ago.   ATC got mad at them.   They poked the bear one too many times.   

This is not a beginner airplane.   The Gulfstream would never do this.   It has HUGE margins of error and won't stall like that.   But then again... it's got HUGE wings.   It's a pussy cat.  

The Gulfstream is like driving a 4 wheeler.   The Lear 60 is like riding a uni cycle.”

I genuinely don’t want to criticize a competitor during their crisis. What I really want is for us to work together with them to raise security standards and better protect the entire crypto industry.

But I have to say, the interview with the “richest man in crypto,” who claims he no longer runs Binance (do you really believe that?), made me sick.

The interview was full of bullshits. It was misleading, appeared to downplay their own responsibilities, and attempted to discredit traditional banks to make excuses for their own failures.

Instead of demonstrating accountability and leadership during a crisis, the interview seemed more focused on deflecting responsibility and shifting blame. This is not the kind of leadership our industry needs.

Since the incident, the “richest man in crypto” seems unable to stop making noise:

1. He has arguably been the most vocal individual associated with Binance on social media throughout this crisis.

2. He has found time to argue with Elon Musk @elonmusk over SpaceX stock investments.

3. He keeps emphasizing that “only 2%” of funds have left Binance, as if that somehow addresses the underlying security concerns.

4. Marketing campaigns to attract new deposits have continued amid the crisis.

5. He has tried to suggest that traditional banks have weaker security. How can someone claiming to be a professional crypto industry leader make such a misleading comparison? The threat models, attack surfaces, and consequences are fundamentally different. Comparing the two without that context is irresponsible.

6. And almost every time he speaks, he appeared to leave a pregnant woman on the front line and  adds the same disclaimer: “I don’t run Binance.”

Meanwhile, the entire crypto industry is suffering the consequences:

1. Bitcoin reportedly fell from around $81,000 to $75,000 during the turmoil.

2. Billions of dollars in leveraged positions were liquidated amid the market disruption.

3. The incident has potentially damaged the credibility of the entire crypto industry in the eyes of traditional capital markets, institutional investors, and global regulators.

And after all this, their so-called “multi-layer security defense” is looking increasingly like a joke.

A friend sent me photos of Halloween costumes that they came across. I’m sharing them here. The satire speaks for itself.

Our industry needs fewer excuses, less PR spin, and more genuine collaboration to protect users and strengthen security standards.

That is what I would rather spend my time building together—even with our competitors.

Clanker: Reboot.

2 years ago (almost to the day), Clanker was born over on the original Farcaster app. The idea was simple: Make it possible for anyone to launch a token just by posting on the timeline and tagging @clanker_world. 

The timing was right, and it caught on like wildfire. Suddenly, even people who never thought they’d launch a token were trying it out in the feed. (I even clanked my first meme token on day 1 to see how it all worked. If you search hard, you can probably find it.)

Over the ensuing year, Clanker went on a genny run, expanding from Fc to the X feed and becoming the highest volume launchpad on @base by far, birthing some of the most iconic tokens & token communities of that era, including BNKR, DRB, FAIR & more. 

So many builders on Farcaster & beyond turned to Clanker to bootstrap their ideas & find their first 1,000 true fans. Legends like @0FJAKE, @AtownBrown, @david_tomu and @darkohh clanked tokens for their projects. Some, like @MLeeJr, even took it upon themselves to clank tokens for OTHER people’s projects.

And when @netnose and I decided to build a gacha app for creator discovery, we clanked our native token on day one too.

There’s just always been something fundamentally OP about clanking tokens right in the feed. Social graph integration remains undefeated in the attention economy. 

But despite all this pedigree & lore, Clanker has had… a rough time lately, to say the least. Between early founder drama, the sale to Farcaster and the eventual handoff to Neynar, Clanker’s been like a teenager who hasn’t been allowed to finish a full year at the same school. How can you even make friends like that?

Hopefully, that all changes today.

Clanker is in good hands now with @masknetwork (stewards of Firefly and Lens Protocol), and they’ve partnered with one of the best engineering teams in the space to give Clanker a much-needed Reboot. More on that soon, but in the meantime…

I’m excited to announce that I’ve accepted the role of Clanker CEO and will be taking on the challenge of guiding our beloved tokenbot back to its former glory.

Transparently, this wasn’t a decision I took lightly. I’ve been self-employed since I was 17, and always preferred to work on things I founded myself. But Clanker has held a very special place in my heart since day 1, and I feel like the little guy’s been a victim of circumstance for much of the past 18 months. He deserves a second chance at romance, and I’m honored to be the one to lead the charge. 

I’m also grateful to everyone who helped make Clanker what it is today. To Proxy and Jack for the founder energy, to Base and Farcaster for backing the ecosystem, to communities like DRB and Bankr for keeping it alive, and to @ProfWerder & @age_shulman for their stewardship too. The fact that this little tokenbot has survived all these seasons is crazy in its own right. We stand on the shoulders of giants.

Much more to come from me soon, but here are my main priorities to start:

- Reboot and refresh the Clanker brand without losing its special je ne sais quoi.

- Work with our socials guru @stanisloou to keep comms fresh and clean.

- Work with our engineering team to bring clanker features up to parity with modern launchpads (stock pairs, new chains and even day one support for _______)

- Rebuild the trust that has been lost with both builders & trenchers through all these transitions.

- Show up for OG communities who are still here building and shipping two years later.

- Bring new launch energy back to Clanker & back to the feed, where distribution is built-in by default. 

So if you’re looking to launch a funny meme, a clever stock pair, or an app coin to bootstrap your project, I want to help you succeed. 

Same goes if you’re a builder with an idea to build on top of clanker protocol; the energy here has always been collaborative and that won’t change. 

My DMs are open and we can win together. 

Let’s press REBOOT and run it back turbo. 

Clank Clank!

text:
The Race Toward Autonomous Chip Design!!

Anthropic is reportedly using Claude frontier models for chip design... +OpenAI and Broadcom got Jalapeneo from RTL to tapeout in just 9 months, using AI to speed up the process. OpenAI is also working with Synopsys on AI for EDA.

I'm curious about a few things with Anthropic's approach:

1. To what degree is Claude doing the design for Anthropic? Is it just RTL generation and verification or does it also include synthesis, place and route, timing closure etc. until finally the GDSII file is written out?

2. Who's doing the physical implementation and signoff? OpenAI worked with Broadcom on Jalapeño, so is Anthropic planning something similar, or will they handle the entire flow in-house?

3. Are they designing just the accelerator, or the whole system, including memory, interconnects, packaging and software?

4. How much of the design process is being automated? Are agents running the tools, analyzing results, and making decisions to design the chip, or is most of the work still being done by engineers?

I've previously written about how chip design is essentially a massive search problem. While being able to explore thousands of designs is great, it's not particularly useful if it takes several months to verify, optimize for PPA and then get ready for fabrication.

Now imagine getting that 9-month RTL-to-tapeout cycle down to 2–3 months? Or less...

What if we could try out many more architectures? There are many custom chips today that are just not worth building because of the cost.

Even though fabrication and silicon validation take time, there's plenty of room for improvement in the time before tapeout.

In terms of EDA, I don't think the underlying tools or signoff requirements are going away, but engineers might end up using them in very different ways.

In a few years, a small team of engineers with the right PDKs/IP, AI tools to explore the search space, and a foundry budget could design and tape out chips that today would take much larger design teams.

Are we approaching the end of painfully slow chip design cycles?

Some of my earlier thoughts/tweet on the search space: 

Chip Design Is Basically a Massive Search Problem

https://t.co/nO7yVME8Ng

text:
We don't need to re-invent the wheel when it comes to sensible regulation on DeFi activities, we just need to clarify the existing regulations and help our regulators understand this powerful technology that can transforming how money becomes productive onchain. 
Our very own @TuongvyLe12 worked with @aave and @kamino  to release a paper explaining this. 

Highly recommend giving it a read
author: veda_labs
quoted_text:
Onchain finance is powerful because it allows users to engage in familiar financial activities without relying on traditional intermediaries. DeFi protocols and vaults, for example, allow users to participate in lending and other onchain strategies while retaining greater ownership and control over their assets, with transparent, enforceable rules limiting what others can do with them.

How these activities are regulated should follow from that.

Today, @veda_labs, @aave, and @kamino released a paper based on our recent submission to the @SECGov  explaining how we believe existing securities laws apply to DeFi lending protocols and non-custodial vaults.

TL;DR: Discretion and control matter, but each statute requires its own analysis. Under the arrangements we examine:

(1) Where no person takes on a legal debt obligation, there is no note.

(2) Where users aren't investing in a common business venture whose fortunes they share, there is no investment contract.

(3) Where no separate investment vehicle owns the assets and issues interests in them, there is no investment company.

These distinctions matter for the future of onchain finance. Familiar financial activities can create very different legal relationships when carried out through new technology.

🚨 金与正再次发声！否认朝鲜参与 Binance 63 亿美元盗币案，并向美国提出对话条件。

11月4日，朝鲜劳动党中央委员会部长金与正再次就 Binance 加密资产被盗事件表态，明确否认朝鲜参与，并对美国发出强硬回应。

她的具体回应主要有三点：

1️⃣ 直接否认美国指控

金与正称，美国 FBI 将 Binance 盗币案归咎于朝鲜，是美国对朝敌对政策的又一表现。她将相关指控称为美国敌对政策的「冰山一角」，认为美方正在借网络安全问题损害朝鲜的国际形象。

2️⃣ 对美国提出明确条件

金与正表示，朝鲜并不排斥与美国对话，和平对话当然是一种选项，但这并不意味着朝鲜必须以牺牲国家利益为代价。

她强调：

「美国放弃对朝敌对政策，是解决所有问题的根本前提和关键。」

同时，她表示，没有必要与拒绝放弃对抗政策的美国方面坐下来面对面谈判。

3️⃣ 暗示可能采取进一步反制措施

金与正警告，面对美国持续释放的敌对信号，朝鲜也将重新审视自身应对方式，并称在美国不断刷新敌对政策纪录的情况下，朝鲜也有理由创造新的反制措施纪录。

值得注意的是，这已是金与正在短时间内第二次针对 Binance 事件发声。

此前，美国 FBI 指认朝鲜关联黑客组织 TraderTraitor 涉及约 63 亿美元加密资产盗窃。朝鲜则持续否认相关指控。

这场争议已经不只是一起加密货币盗窃案，更牵涉美朝网络安全指控、外交关系以及未来谈判条件。金与正此次表态，也再次将朝鲜对美关系的核心条件摆到了台面上。

Fitch looked at the $40B commitment and left SpaceX at BBB+, because that compute was already in its forecast. It's treating the deal like any other equipment lease.

text:
The Race Toward Autonomous Chip Design!!

Anthropic is reportedly using Claude frontier models for chip design... +OpenAI and Broadcom got Jalapeneo from RTL to tapeout in just 9 months, using AI to speed up the process. OpenAI is also working with Synopsys on AI for EDA.

I'm curious about a few things with Anthropic's approach:

1. To what degree is Claude doing the design for Anthropic? Is it just RTL generation and verification or does it also include synthesis, place and route, timing closure etc. until finally the GDSII file is written out?

2. Who's doing the physical implementation and signoff? OpenAI worked with Broadcom on Jalapeño, so is Anthropic planning something similar, or will they handle the entire flow in-house?

3. Are they designing just the accelerator, or the whole system, including memory, interconnects, packaging and software?

4. How much of the design process is being automated? Are agents running the tools, analyzing results, and making decisions to design the chip, or is most of the work still being done by engineers?

I've previously written about how chip design is essentially a massive search problem. While being able to explore thousands of designs is great, it's not particularly useful if it takes several months to verify, optimize for PPA and then get ready for fabrication.

Now imagine getting that 9-month RTL-to-tapeout cycle down to 2–3 months? Or less...

What if we could try out many more architectures? There are many custom chips today that are just not worth building because of the cost.

Even though fabrication and silicon validation take time, there's plenty of room for improvement in the time before tapeout.

In terms of EDA, I don't think the underlying tools or signoff requirements are going away, but engineers might end up using them in very different ways.

In a few years, a small team of engineers with the right PDKs/IP, AI tools to explore the search space, and a foundry budget could design and tape out chips that today would take much larger design teams.

Are we approaching the end of painfully slow chip design cycles?

Some of my earlier thoughts/tweet on the search space: 

Chip Design Is Basically a Massive Search Problem

https://t.co/nO7yVME8Ng

Pèp ayisyen,

Dessalines te libere Ayiti, men kèk moun ki te bò kote l te trayi l epi touye l. Moun ki te sanble avè l, ki te pale menm lang avè l, men ki pa t gen menm prensip avè l. Se te trèt ki t ap chèche sèlman avantaj pèsonèl yo, e ki te plonje Ayiti nan plizyè jenerasyon soufrans ak mizè.

Trèt sa yo toujou egziste ann Ayiti. Yo pa eritye Dessalines, yo se eritye trèt ki te asasinen l yo e ki te detwi eritaj li. Genyen ki manm gang, gen lòt ki finanse gang yo oswa ki ba yo zam, e gen kèk ladan yo k ap fè tout sa yo kapab pou anpeche pèp ayisyen an jwenn libète li.

Wi, anpil etranje te piye Ayiti, men anpil Ayisyen te fè menm bagay la tou. Yo te kolabore ak etranje sa yo, sèvi ak zam yo, vann dwòg yo, kontwole teritwa pou yo, epi fè pèp la sibi soufrans moun pa menm ka imajine.

Èske nou panse etranje sa yo t ap kapab fè tout bagay sa yo san èd moun sa yo? Kiyès k ap lonje zam sou nou? Kiyès k ap touye moun nou renmen yo? Kiyès ki vòlè kay nou ak byen nou yo, si se pa menm kalite bandi trèt ak sa yo ki te trayi epi asasinen Dessalines?

Nou kapab ede nou bat yo, men nou pa anvayisè. Nou se moun ki gen kouraj menm jan ak nou. Fòk nou leve kanpe, reprann kontwòl kominote nou yo, epi mete moun k ap fè nou sibi tout doulè sa yo, tout soufrans sa yo, anba kontwòl nou.

N ap la menm bò kote nou. N ap ede nou reprann peyi nou anba men trèt ki trayi eritaj Dessalines yo.

Epi, finalman, Ayiti ap lib.

Friday was my last day at Anthropic.

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

When we first launched, most people approved every permission prompt by hand and mostly used Claude to answer questions and write tests. 

Today, the default is trusting Claude's judgment to auto-approve. Claude does large migrations and builds new products. 

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime. 

Thank you to the incredible team behind Claude Code, Cowork, and Tag. These products are the sum of thousands of great ideas from you. I'll miss working with you all.

Excited to see what you all make next!

刚看到币安官推发布了安全调查报告，看完让人后背发凉，我根据我的理解梳理一下

9 月份：软件工程师 B 在一个正规的求职平台上，被一个「项目总监」联系，主动挖他。我猜大概率就是 LinkedIn 了，暴露了 B 是币安在职员工。

项目总监安排了两轮面试：一面是所谓 HR 视频面试，取得 B 的信任；二面是虚构公司的 CEO，通过 IM 进行，并且让 B 下载了一个包含恶意代码库的「作业」到他的工作电脑上。这个代码库的恶意代码，在安装过程中就执行了，引发了一系列未经授权的活动。而且这是一个 0-day 恶意软件，当时币安的终端安全软件都没检测出来，黑客还刻意清除了入侵痕迹，加大了发现和调查的难度。

10 月 20 号：黑客从 B 的电脑出发，借助币安公司内部的 AI 工具，控制了钱包运维工程师 A 和钱包软件工程师 C 的电脑。

控制 A 的电脑之后，黑客在上面发现了容器部署权限令牌。

10 月 29 日：黑客登录员工 C 的电脑，用从 A 那里偷来的凭证部署容器、运行恶意脚本，从而拿到内部钱包签名服务的访问权，在正常提现流程之外发起了转账。之后黑客又利用 EIP-7702 授权，批量转走了 ETH 链上的资产。

更早之前 6 月份的时候，A 其实在搜索引擎上搜热门 AI 编程工具后，就下载了被篡改的 Homebrew 安装包，但这次事件被安全团队及时发现了，没有酿成大祸。但工程师 A 的岗位及其钱包基础设施团队的相关同事，当时就已暴露给黑客

总结来说，这是一场多阶段攻击：结合了假面试、恶意软件下载、内部 AI 工具被利用、终端设备被入侵，以及高级的交易授权手法。

LinkedIn 暴露币安员工身份只是表象；A 下载被篡改的工具，让黑客锁定了钱包团队 + B 在工作电脑上运行「面试作业」直接打开大门，这才是根源；内部 AI 工具成了横向渗透的跳板，让黑客从一台电脑扩散到三个核心钱包工程师；而 EIP-7702 授权加上 MPC 钱包难以快速撤销，让事件在近 4 小时内没被完全控住，是催化剂

text:
Really happy to see the response to the Darkbloom update :)

A few people asked: “Won’t the new sandbox providers just undercut you?”

The simple answer: we’re giving your agents a Mac.

We aren’t stopping at 2-4 vCPUs. We want to offer 8, 16 or 32 physical CPU cores, plus Apple GPUs, for agents doing research and complex work.

Unlike inference alone, these workloads can put much more of the machine to use. We think there’s a real opportunity to compete on both price and performance here.

My bet is that the work we give agents will keep getting more compute-intensive. Bigger builds, more experiments, simulations, video editing, rendering. There’s a lot beyond running a few commands and managing your calendar in a terminal.

Think about an agent working in Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro, or using open-source creative tools. It needs access to the software, the environment and enough compute to actually do the work.

That’s what gets me excited about this. I want to see what agents can do when we give them a powerful Mac to work with.

That’s what we’re building towards with Darkbloom Sandboxes.

Cheers to the GOAT who made these chips! ❤️
author: darkbloomai
quoted_text:
Darkbloom just passed 1 trillion tokens processed :)

I haven't tweeted much recently or shared many charts. We've been heads down on the thing that matters most right now: getting providers more work and better earnings.

Honestly, it's been a hard stretch. Provider earnings have been low. People trusted us with their machines and their time, and we take that seriously.

Inference keeps getting cheaper as architectures improve and more supply comes online. That means more people can use AI, but it also makes the economics harder for our providers. We have to keep finding where these machines can be most useful.

The mission is still the same: bring together all the spare compute out there and make it easy to own & share AI. I believe in that more than when we started.

And there's a lot more these machines can do.

More agents means more code to run, more tests, more builds. All those actions need compute too. Apple has built some incredibly capable, energy-efficient CPUs, and we want to put them to work.

We've started the private beta for Darkbloom Sandboxes and CI/CD.

We're starting with our own pipelines, cutting our internal costs by 50% while leaving healthy margins for providers. This gives us another way to bring useful, paying work to the network.

If you're looking for Mac CI or sandboxes, let us know. We'd love to work with you.

We're also continuing to push on inference. There's a lot of work going into open-source clustering on top of MLX; huge kudos to @Spangler3000 and @TheDavidTai for absolutely killing it on that front and writing SOTA for  models such as GLM 5.3 Flash.

I'm attaching the debrief @0xkydo shared with providers last week. He laid out the difficult parts openly, and how people responded meant a lot to me. Seeing people care this much about making it work, especially through a hard stretch, reminds me why I love building this.

It's a hard problem. We're going to keep attacking it. Thank you to everyone who have been here in this journey and continuing to support & be with us.

text:
全场给苏妈起立🫡。AMD 三季度财报一扫市场阴霾，让市场看到了曙光。预计17号英伟达财报，大概率市场就能完全反转了！🧐

前两天英特尔指引拉胯，市场一片喊着AI泡沫要破。结果苏妈直接甩出一份力挽狂澜的成绩单：数据中心同比暴增97%，Q4指引170亿美元，远超预期的162亿。凭一己之力拉升了整个芯片板块。

说句心里话，真得要感谢苏妈🙏

其实昨晚开盘 $AMD 走势就很强，但尾部有些砸盘，其实市场还是有点担心的。财报前市场怕什么？PC成本涨卖不动、英特尔爆雷拖累行业、AI资本开支到底能不能变成真金白银。咱们看数据👇

📊 三季度核心数据：
• 总营收133.77亿美元（预期130.9亿）🟢 同比+45%，单季历史新高
• 调整后EPS 2.09美元（预期1.95）🟢 同比+74%
• 调整后运营利润率29%（预期28%）🟢

📊 Q4指引：
• 营收约170亿美元，上下3%（预期162.3亿）🟢 同比+66%，环比+27%
• 非GAAP毛利率约55%，环比略降1个点，主要是Helios系统放量和产品结构变化

📊 分类情况：
• 数据中心：85.46亿美元（预期82.7亿）🟢 同比+97%，占总营收64%
• 客户端PC：29.49亿美元（预期30.3亿）🔴 内存成本飙升，苏妈还提醒2027年PC出货量可能两位数下滑
• 游戏：7.73亿美元（预期6.34亿）🟢 但同比-40%，主机周期后半段，正常下滑

🧐财报解读，我的一些看法和理解：

1️⃣ AI 需求是真实的，大家还在买买买
三季度营收 133.77 亿美元、EPS 同比大增 74%，最核心的数据中心业务直接干到了 85.46 亿美元（占比近 64%）。微软、Meta、OpenAI、Anthropic、甲骨文，都已经部署了首批MI450/MI455X的Helios机架。这说明云巨头和前沿实验室不仅在买 AI 芯片，而且在加码买。

2️⃣ Q4 指引杀翻全场，增长还在“提速”
四季度指引中值 170 亿美元（同比增 66%），直接把华尔街预期踩在脚下。更炸裂的是，AMD 单季营收规模历史性地超越了英特尔全公司的季度收入区间。从当年被英特尔压着的“老二”，到如今在 AI 算力赛道上骑马绝尘，这个叙事彻底变了。

3️⃣ 短期现金流和库存的“瑕疵”，反而成了扩产的铁证
自由现金流虽然因为库存增加了近 30 亿美元而承压，但大家看得很清楚，在 MI450/MI455X 和 Helios 机架放量的关键节点，提前锁定晶圆、HBM 和封装产能的“屯粮”行为，正是为了保证 Q4 和 2027 年能有货交给客户。

🎯 AI绝杀组合拳：EPYC（CPU）与 Instinct（GPU）的协同优势

这次财报里最亮眼的，就是 AMD 从“卖单颗芯片”向“卖整套 AI 基础设施”的彻底蜕变。这就是他们打造的 Helios 机架级系统。

大家总以为 AI 只要买 GPU 就够了，但实际上，CPU 和 GPU 是缺一不可的“大脑与肌肉”：

1️⃣AMD EPYC 服务器 CPU（大脑与指挥官）
基于 2nm 架构的第六代 EPYC（Venice/Turin）不仅是传统算力支柱，更是 AI 时代的“超级指挥官”。随着 AI Agent爆发，复杂模型的调度、预处理、数据吞吐都需要极强的 CPU 配合。连 OpenAI 都选择 Turin EPYC 作为其自研加速平台的主机 CPU，可见其掌控力。

2️⃣AMD Instinct AI 加速卡（GPU 肌肉）
从 MI450 到 MI455X，提供了海量的并行计算能力和极高带宽的 HBM 显存。配合最新的 ROCm 10 生态，大大降低了开发者部署模型的门槛，目前Anthropic 的工程师爆料用 Claude 一个周末就能把模型挂上 MI355X 跑通。

3️⃣协同产生的“1+1 > 2”优势：

解决数据吞吐瓶颈：高核数的 EPYC 配合高带宽的 Instinct GPU，避免了“GPU 算得飞快，CPU 喂饭太慢”的尴尬情况。

灵活架构匹配需求：通过 Helios 机架，AMD 可以给超大云厂商提供全 CPU 高密度配置（单机架搭 144 颗 Venice，跑多 Task Agent 效率无敌），也可以提供 CPU+GPU 混合架构，拿一套基础设施通吃推理与训练。

极高性价比：在英伟达方案贵且产能吃紧的情况下，AMD 提供了同样具备极强纵向/横向扩展带宽的整架方案，给 Anthropic、Meta、微软、OpenAI 和甲骨文这些大客户提供了极其宝贵的第二选择。

如 CFO 所言，到了今年 Q4，AMD 的 AI GPU 收入将历史上首次超越服务器 CPU 收入。这标志着 AMD 正式蜕变成一家真正的 AI 算力巨头。

最后总结一下，AMD 这次大涨，说白了就是用确定性击碎了确定性缺失。当市场还在纠结 PC 降温和宏观逆风时，苏妈用数据证明，数据中心和 AI 的强劲爆发，已经足够扛起整家公司的利润引擎。面对 2027 年数据中心占比将超 80%、服务器营收翻倍的宏观远景，AMD 用产品迭代与供需两端的扎实配合，再次把整个半导体板块拉回了健康的增长轨道。

现在让我们把目光聚焦于17号英伟达财报吧，不出意料，是AI板块彻底反转的核心推动力！

Two years ago, when Claude Code was a small internal tool, I asked it to build an RL env. I steered it for tens of hours but never manually wrote a line of code. It worked, I was hooked, and I joined the team.

Helping build Claude Code into an industry-defining product has been the journey of a lifetime.

之前提过一个概念，基本面是柴，注意力是油，现在再完善下，增加流动性，我觉得可以比作氧气，柴和油是针对项目本身的，氧气是针对整个市场环境的。

有氧气的时候，柴和油不需要太多就能烧起来；缺氧的时候，柴和油再多也点不着。

所以：
基本面是柴，决定烧多久；
注意力是油，决定烧多旺；
流动性是氧，决定上下限。

最近1个多月其实一直在跟 AI 折腾，希望搞出一套基于三要素的项目估值体系。结果发现实在太难了，首先这三者本身各自都有一堆参数，很难具体量化，更何况他们还互相关联、影响，价格又有反身性，加密的历史又不长，数据不够多。

不能说绝对搞不出来吧，但恐怕至少得全身心投入个一年半载，难度不亚于发一篇牛逼的学术论文。

妈的，还是接地气一点，干中学吧。

quoted_text:
i just killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

they have 15M subs, a full team of writers, animators and voice actors behind every video

mine cost $0 and 20 minutes to make

im giving out the prompt for free, enjoy

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic (a what-if, a "why does X happen", a true story, or how something works), or pitch 3 with one shocking true angle each. Ask which image model I have (GPT Image 2, or another that takes reference images at 4K) and which voice service (ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free). Then write a 55-65 s script and a shot plan, and show me both before you spend anything.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1920x1080 flat vector explainer in the style of the big infographic animation channels. Every scene is a full illustrated place (a lab, a street, a classroom, a stage) with characters acting the line out.
Flat colour shapes, no outlines, one slightly darker flat shade for form, a muted palette (dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple), salmon-pink skin, big heads, dot eyes.
A new scene every 2-4 s and a hard cut on every sentence that changes the idea. A white splat wipe (0.2 s in, 0.2 s out) between big sections. The camera always drifts 2-4% or pans.
Text lives only on things in the world: signs on posts, hanging boards, chalkboards, building panels and screens.
- It is typed in Montserrat 800 at 26-34 letters a second. Each letter arrives 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right, then settles in 0.18 s.
- Ink is #2b2d42 on white boards.
- A red X (#d62828, 30 px round strokes, two strokes of 0.11 s each) goes over every wrong idea.
- Every date gets a white 330x120 card top left with an orange #f4a261 calendar.
- Headlines are white 92-96 px caps on a flat colour (#e2552f with drifting lighter puffs, or #5b3fa6 with slowly turning #6a4cb6 gears).
Banned: outlines, motion-design UI floating over the art (code editors, glass cards, checklists), emoji, burned-in subtitles, any channel's logo, a still frame longer than 1 s, and a character who doesn't move.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: the voice decides, 55-65 s at about 190 words per minute.
0 s a second-person hook that flips what the viewer assumes, acted out literally, then a red X on the denial line → 3-8 s the stakes in one shocking true line, with icons popping in one per word → 8-11 s the subject revealed under a spotlight, its name typed on a sign → 11-18 s the origin: the real place with its name typed on its own sign, a date card, people walking in or out of it → 18-24 s the types or parts, landing one by one on their names, each labelled → 24-25.5 s "so how does it work?" as a headline with question marks popping → 25.5-36 s the mechanism acted out in 2-3 places (a chalkboard, a machine, a map), with a counter rolling up to the big number → 36-46 s what it leads to, with characters who react (jump, turn, a "!" pops) → 46-55 s the twist that ties back to the hook → 55 s the last line is a question to the viewer, the viewer character from the hook reacts, and the sign holds to the end.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, librosa. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Art: everything at 3840x2160, with 3-5 frames of the reference channel as style references (crop their logo off first).
   - One EMPTY plate per scene: no people, straight-on, open floor, blank signs and screens to write on in code.
   - Character sheets on solid chroma green #00B140, with nothing green on anyone.
   - Draw any character who gestures a lot WITHOUT ARMS, only round shoulder sockets, so code draws the arms. Draw everyone else in the exact pose their scene needs: side view at a desk, side view walking, seen from behind, sitting.
3. Cutouts:
   - The background is every pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40, within 110 of the median green, connected to the border.
   - Add a 2 px soft alpha band, and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it.
   - Split heads at the neck, drawing hands, and walkers' legs below the coat hem.
   - Refill each hole with inpainting from the body's own colours (transparent pixels masked too), so a turning piece never shows a gap.
4. Voice:
   - Pick it by measuring median pitch (pyin) and MFCC timbre against a clip of the narrator you want.
   - Generate one take, cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, and atempo it to the target length.
   - Get word timestamps with faster-whisper. Every cut, sign and gesture starts on a real word.
5. Film: one HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time: window. seek(t), READY, END, and EV with the sound times. One function per shot.
   - Arms: two-bone IK tubes (upper 118, lower 112, 36 thick for a 918 px tall sprite) with mitten hands that open, point or make a fist.
   - Faces blink for 0.14 s every 2.7-4.2 s. Heads nod ±0.035 rad. Drawing hands scribble ±8 px.
   - Walks:
     - Thighs swing ±0.42 rad, and the knee bends 0.75·cos² on the swing.
     - The hips drop so the planted foot stays down.
     - The body moves 1.5 leg lengths per cycle, so feet never slide.
   - Draw each plate inside the same camera transform as everything on it, and clamp the camera to the plate's edges.
   - Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a fade.
6. Render: Playwright Chromium with --allow-file-access-from-files, 60 fps, 6 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, ffmpeg libx264 at CRF 16. Before rendering, show me two 16-frame contact sheets and fix empty boards, overflowing text, covered faces and black edges.
7. Sound:
   - Music: a light curious documentary bed (free on Pixabay), 10-11 dB under the voice in every phrase.
   - SFX: Mixkit, placed by their peaks. A typewriter tick on typed signs, a whoosh on wipes and drops, a pop on signs and icons, a hit on the red X, a ding on ticks.
   - Mix to -14 LUFS.
</build>

<gotchas>
Some image models ignore "no arms"; GPT Image 2 follows it. On outline-free art a floating flood fill leaks into dark clothes, so key by border-connected green instead. Look up repeated words by their occurrence number (the third "and", the fourth "this"), or cuts land on the wrong line; scan the render for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut. When a scene has a screen or a sign, write on the plate's own blank one (measure its rectangle), never on a card floating over the art.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, or pitch 3, then show me the script and the shot plan.
</start>

text:
我真心不想在竞争对手遭遇危机的时候批评他们。我真正希望的是，我们能够与他们携手合作，共同提高安全标准，更好地保护整个加密行业。

但我不得不说，那位自称已经不再管理币安的“币圈首富”（你们真的相信吗？）最近接受的采访，实在让我感到恶心。

整场采访充斥着胡说八道和误导性言论。他似乎在淡化自身应承担的责任，甚至试图通过贬低传统银行的安全性，为自己的失败寻找借口。

在这样一场危机中，我们本应看到的是责任担当和行业领导力。但这场采访给人的感觉，却是在不断推卸责任、转移焦点。

这绝不是我们这个行业需要的领导力。

自从事件发生以来，这位“币圈首富”似乎就一直停不下来：

1. 社交媒体上最活跃的人之一。 在整场危机期间，他可以说是币安相关人士中在社交媒体上发声最多、最活跃的一个。

2. 还有时间和马斯克吵架。 在如此严重的安全危机期间，他居然还有精力与 Elon Musk（@elonmusk）争论 SpaceX 股票投资的问题。

3. 反复强调“只有2%的资金流出币安”。 仿佛这个数字就能回答大家对平台安全性的根本质疑。

4. 继续开展营销活动吸引用户存款。 即使危机仍在持续，吸引新资金流入的营销活动也没有停止。

5. 试图暗示传统银行的安全性更差。 一个自称专业的加密行业领导者，怎么能做出如此具有误导性的比较？传统银行与加密交易所面对的威胁模型、攻击面以及安全事故的后果，都存在根本性差异。脱离这些背景进行简单比较，是极其不负责任的。

6. 几乎每次发声，都似乎把一位怀孕的女性推到危机最前线。 而自己则反复加上同一句免责声明：“我已经不管理币安了。”

与此同时，整个加密行业却在为这场危机付出代价：

1. 比特币价格据报道从约81,000美元跌至75,000美元。 市场在动荡中遭受了明显冲击。

2. 数十亿美元的杠杆仓位遭到清算。 市场波动引发了大规模的强制平仓。

3. 整个加密行业的公信力可能再次受到重创。 传统资本市场、机构投资者以及全球监管机构，可能因此对整个行业的安全性和可信度产生更深的疑虑。

经历了这一切，他们所谓的“多层安全防御体系”，如今看起来越来越像一个笑话。

我们的行业需要的，不是更多的借口，不是更多的公关话术，而是真正的合作、真正的责任担当，以及切实有效的用户资产保护和安全标准建设。

少一些推卸责任，少一些营销包装，多一些真正的安全投入和行业协作。

这才是我更愿意投入时间和精力去推动的事情。

即使是竞争对手，我也真心希望我们能够携手把这件事做好。

text:
After 2mo in the oven, I'm excited to share the Mission Statement at https://t.co/ENJpTp5ttR ♾🌌

In the fast-paced world of software dev, it's easy to take shortcuts, but I believe strongly that your Mission Statement should not be one of them.

Mission statements are a fundamental artifact that anything that "grows" truly must have in order to have a chance at being successful over time.

Orgs, teams, products, and even individuals.

But boy is it difficult to put together a good one... 😩

Here's why:

A great mission statement is both specific enough to weigh day-to-day prioritization, yet broad enough to guide 3yr plans.

https://t.co/ENJpTp5ttR's mission will now guide the product's every move.

Another reason they are difficult, is that they force you to be brutally honest with who you are, what you do, and why.

Sometimes, this is not the easiest of conversations to have with yourself, let alone with others.

During my most recent 10yrs as a leader of product teams, I always made it a point to sit down with everyone and align on a mission statement.

That convo was always first met with hesitation and seen as a distraction from "real work."

But then, everyone brings their ideas, their perspective, eyes widen and smiles appear as you start to get somewhere meaningful.

It quickly turns into a valuable opportunity to collaborate and align on a broader strategic purpose that you all share in together.

...It quickly turns into some of the most valuable IP the team produces.

And the team comes away with a measuring stick for reassuring each and every decision they make.

That is why they are so challenging, but also why they are SO rewarding once you've finally felt that feeling of "THIS IS IT, THIS IS US!"

quoted_text:
apeball

a coin that buys bored apes with its trading fees

an onchain game where anyone can purchase randomized nfts from a pool containing those apes

i've been watching token strategies since they launched and it's been v interesting to see how speculation is used to fund the accumulation of assets

but once assets are acquired, many of those strategies stall out because they require demand for the target collection to rise and buy the nfts that were listed at a markup

i've been curious about what happens if you keep the asset accumulation mechanism but give those assets a different way to circulate

enter: FWA custom pools

with apeball, trading fees fund a live eth bid for bored apes, and every acquired ape goes into the pool

rather than waiting for someone to purchase an entire ape at a markup, the pool distributes nfts through much smaller randomized purchases

the rest of the pool is filled with shapes (eth-backed nfts), which are minted on demand at different denominations, giving people a range of possible outcomes and keeping the draw price around 0.02 eth

as people play apeball, each ape's notional listing value gradually decays, increasing the odds that they get drawn

the pool generates revenue from each draw and all pool profits go toward accumulating APEBALL for buy and burns and additional ape acquisitions when needed

the buyback portion accumulates in a reserve until someone pulls an ape, at which point it's released to buy and burn the coin

so trading activity acquires the apes, the game provides a way to distribute them through smaller purchases, and the revenue from that activity feeds back into the coin

some details on the coin:

- 1 billion fixed supply
- no team allocation, presale, or emissions
- normal trading fees are 5% on buys and sells
- launch fee starts at 69% in both directions and decrease by 1 percentage point per minute until reaching 5%
- 99% of trading fees go to the ape pool, 1% goes to buy and burn LAYER

i earn from the mint fees on shapes, while the trading fees and game revenue remain in the protocol to fund acquisitions and buybacks

feels like we're just scratching the surface of how these different onchain mechanisms can work together, and i'm excited to see how this one plays out

deploying soon
